**Lesson 83: Explanation of Verses 1 to 29**

**Commentary on Verses 1 to 4**

﴿They ask you about the anfal. Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger. So fear Allah, set right the relations among yourselves, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.﴾ (8:1)

﴿The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, and when His verses are recited to them they increase their faith, and they put their trust in their Lord. Those who establish the prayer and spend out of what We have provided them. Those are truly the believers. For them are high ranks with their Lord, and forgiveness, and an honourable provision.﴾ (8:2–4)

The narrations about the revelation of these verses are many, and we mentioned a large part of them in the introduction to this surah. Here we add some other narrations, so that the circumstances in which this surah was generally revealed remain before the reader's eyes, especially the circumstances in which those verses concerning the booty were revealed. From these narrations it will also be known what the features of the community of Muslims were at the time of the establishment of the first Islamic government in Madinah, and what practical difficulties it was passing through.

Ibn Kathir says: Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh (the wording is theirs), Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim narrated this report through Dawud ibn Abi Hind and Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. He said: When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Whoever does such and such will receive such and such a reward." Thus the young men of the people advanced, while the elders remained near the standards. When the time for the booty came, they began to make the demands which the Messenger (ﷺ) had promised them. Then the elders said: "Do not make claims to priority, for we were a shelter for you; had you suffered a defeat, you would have taken refuge with us." Then a dispute arose between these two groups. On this occasion Allah revealed these verses: ﴿They ask you about the anfal . . . to ". . . and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers"﴾.

And al-Thawri narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas. He said: When the battle of Badr took place, the Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Whoever kills someone will have such and such a reward, and whoever takes someone captive will be given such and such a reward." On that occasion Abu al-Yasar took two men captive, and they said, "Here they are, O Messenger of Allah; you promised us." Then Sa'd ibn Ubadah stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you give these people the booty in this way, nothing will remain for your companions. Moreover, we did not refrain from fighting because we did not need the reward, or because we feared the enemy. We stood firm here so that you would be protected, lest the enemy attack you from behind." So a considerable dispute arose, and on this occasion these verses were revealed: ﴿They ask you about the anfal. Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾. They said this, and in connection with the same matter this verse was also revealed: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as booty, one-fifth of it belongs to Allah . . .﴾.

Imam Ahmad narrated a report. He said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated it from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah al-Thaqafi, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: On the occasion of the battle of Badr, my brother Umayr was martyred. I killed Sa'id ibn al-As and took his sword. The name of that sword was "Dhu al-Kafiyah." I came with this sword to the Messenger (ﷺ). He said, "Go and throw it into the spoils." He said: I threw the sword and returned, but only Allah knew my condition, that my brother had also been killed, and the valuable thing that had fallen into my hand could not be found. I had only gone a short distance when Surah al-Anfal was revealed. The Messenger (ﷺ) commanded me, "Go and take the sword that fell into your hand."

Imam Ahmad says: Aswad ibn Amir narrated from Abu Bakr, from Asim ibn Abi al-Nujud, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: I said to the Messenger (ﷺ), "Today Allah has given me relief from the polytheists; grant me this sword." The Messenger (ﷺ) said, "This sword is neither for me nor for you. Place it there." So I put the sword down and returned. I thought: perhaps this sword will go to a person who has not fulfilled its right as I did. Suddenly I heard someone calling behind me. I thought perhaps a verse had been revealed about me. The Messenger (ﷺ) said, "You asked me for the sword, and it was not mine; now it has been granted to me, so now it is yours." On this occasion these verses were revealed: ﴿They ask you about the anfal. Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i narrated this report from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash. Al-Tirmidhi, through several chains, called it *hasan sahih* (good and authentic).

From these narrations, the atmosphere in which Surah al-Anfal was revealed becomes clear. A person reading these reports is somewhat astonished: are these the people of Badr, and are these the things they did? For among them were the Muhajirun, who had sacrificed everything in Makkah and had come to Madinah solely because of their convictions, and in their eyes the worldly interests of this life were in any case worthless. And among them were the foremost Ansar, who had given refuge to these Muhajirun and had shared with them their lands and wealth. They did not withhold from them any worldly benefit. Concerning them Allah says: ﴿They love those who migrate to them, and they do not find in their breasts any need for what has been given to them; they prefer others above themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾ (59:9).

The circumstances described here are alluded to in these very reports. At that time, the booty was connected with the bravery and valour that a soldier displayed on the battlefield, and this material reward was also a sign that the recipient had shown valour. In that period people desired to receive a special reward from the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which would be considered a reward directly from Allah. Especially in that first encounter which took place between Islam and unbelief. Under the influence of this greed and the lure of reward, another quality was overshadowed, and some people spoke about the booty, and Allah drew their attention to the importance of that quality. That quality was: in dealings with one another, a little good conduct is needed, and there is a severe need for the reform of your hearts. So they perceived this matter well and understood it. On one occasion, Hadrat Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: "These verses were revealed concerning us, the Companions of Badr, when we disputed about the booty and went beyond the moral limits in it. Allah took those spoils out of our control and placed them in the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Allah Most High gave this community both practical and verbal training. He took away from them the authority over the distribution of the booty and placed it entirely in the hands of the Prophet (ﷺ), until detailed commands concerning the distribution of spoils were revealed. Thus there was no longer any right for them to dispute in this matter. This became a grace of Allah. The Messenger of Allah distributed it among them in the manner in which the Lord had guided him. Alongside this practical reform, this long and continuous guidance was also given to them, and this guidance extended throughout this surah. It began thus:

﴿They ask you about the anfal. Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger. So fear Allah, set right the relations among yourselves, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.﴾

This question came from those who had disputed over the spoils, and this call is also directed at them: fear Allah. Allah is the creator of your hearts and knows the thoughts that arise in your hearts. Allah does not take to account the reason why a desire for worldly aims arises in someone's heart, or why a dispute arose over it. Although at the root of that dispute there was the wish that rewards should come from the hands of the Messenger, which would be proof of their good performance. But Allah made it necessary for the success of this world and the Hereafter that you create in your hearts the feeling of *taqwa* and fear of Allah, because a heart that is not connected with Allah, and does not fear His wrath, and has no desire to obtain His pleasure, can never disregard worldly interests, and can never consciously keep itself away from those defilements.

The truth is that *taqwa* is the bridle of hearts, and through *taqwa* alone hearts can be led, and can be led with great ease. The Holy Qur'an, from beginning to end, leads human beings through this bridle of *taqwa* and connection with Allah, and presents it as the means of reform.

The Qur'an says: ﴿So fear Allah and set right the relations among yourselves﴾. And then it is said that this is the means through which you can obey the Messenger: ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers﴾.

The obedience owed to the Messenger first means that you accept the rulings that have come from Allah concerning the spoils (al-anfal). For example, the spoils of war have now been removed from the ownership of the fighters, and their ownership has been given to Allah and His Messenger. Therefore, the right to dispose of them now belongs solely to Allah and His Messenger. It is the duty of the believers to accept the rulings of Allah and His Messenger regarding this, and to accept the Messenger of Allah's distribution in accordance with the instructions of Allah, accepting it willingly, being content with what is decreed, improving their mutual relations, correcting their understanding and feelings, and purifying their hearts towards one another. "In kuntum mu'minin": if you are believers.

It is necessary that faith have a practical and real form, and that this practical form make faith visible and manifest. It should appear in embodied form, and a person's deeds should be the interpreter of his faith. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Faith is not mere wishful thinking, but it is that which settles in the heart and which deeds confirm." This is why such phrases in the Qur'an come again and again in a decisive manner, and their purpose is precisely to show what the reality of faith is and what its connection with deeds is. Faith is not merely the name of words that flow on the tongue, nor is it mere wishing, which has no reality in the real world and no existence in the world of action.

After this, it is explained what the true qualities of a sincere believer are, so that it may be made clear what is meant by "in kuntum mu'minin." Accordingly, it is stated that in the sight of the Lord of the worlds, the believer is one such as this:

"The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble; and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith; and upon their Lord they rely. Those who establish the prayer and spend out of what We have provided them. Those are the believers in truth. For them are degrees with their Lord and forgiveness and an honorable provision." (Qur'an 8:2–4)

Linguistically and grammatically, the manner of expression in these verses is extremely meaningful and carries profound significance. Here the particle of restriction (innama) is used. There is no reason to interpret the restrictive sense of innama away, since Allah wishes to state a matter with great emphasis. Some interpretations have said that it means complete faith; but if Allah had wished to say it that way, He would have said, "The perfect believers are those who are such and such." In reality, this is a highly detailed expression. The meaning is that those whose awareness and feelings are such, and whose qualities and deeds are such, are truly believers; and those who do not possess these qualities and deeds are not believers, because at the end of this verse this point is emphasized repeatedly: "Those are the believers in truth." And those who are not truly believers, what kind of believers are they then called? The expressions of the Qur'an explain and interpret one another. Allah says: "What, then, is there after the truth but error?" (10:32). Therefore, whatever is not truth will be error. I say that no expression can be the counterpart of "al-mu'minun haqqan" (the believers in truth). "Al-mu'minun imanan ghair..." Therefore, this clear and precise manner of expression in the Qur'an should not be put on the lathe of interpretations, which displace every correct concept and every correct expression from its place.

This is why some of the righteous predecessors (salaf) used to say that whoever does not have these qualities in his belief and in his deeds has not attained faith, and is not a believer at all. In Ibn Kathir it is related: Ali ibn Talha narrates from Ibn Abbas that in the verse "The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble," there is in fact a reference to the hypocrites. When they are praying, nothing enters their hearts; in truth they do not believe in the verses of Allah and do not rely upon Allah at all. And when they are not in front of people, they do not maintain ties of kinship, nor do they pay the zakat on their wealth. So Allah informed about these hypocrites that they are not believers. After this, Allah enumerated the qualities of true believers, such as:

"The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble," thus they fulfill their obligations. "And when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith": that is, when the verses of Allah are recited to them, their faith increases; that is, their affirmation increases. "And upon their Lord they rely": and they put their trust in their Lord.

In the following lines we shall prove that without these realities the very existence of faith does not remain. And this does not mean that with them faith becomes complete and without them it becomes deficient; rather, the question is of the existence or non-existence of faith: "The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned." When a believer remembers Allah in connection with a command or a prohibition, a spiritual trembling arises in his heart. Awe takes hold of his heart because of the majesty of Allah, and waves of the fear of Allah rise in his heart. In this way, the awe of Allah stands against his shortcomings and sins, and thus it becomes the cause of action and strength. As Umm al-Darda (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Wajal (trembling) in the heart is like the peeling of a palm frond. Do you not find its burning?" He said, "Yes." She said, "When you find it, then call upon Allah at that moment, for supplication removes that." To understand "wajal," think of it this way: when someone develops blisters, he feels a burning. Do you not feel a trembling in such a state? Yes, it is so. When you find such a state, call upon Allah; through supplication this state passes.

In short, this is the state in which restlessness arises in the heart, and in such circumstances, through remembrance and supplication, a person attains comfort and tranquility. This is the state in which a person remembers Allah in connection with a command and a prohibition. "And when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith": and when the verses of Allah are recited to them, their faith increases. For the believing heart, in truth, there are in these verses points that are a cause of increase in its faith and through which the believer attains tranquility of heart. The Qur'an deals directly with the believing heart, and only the veil of disbelief can come between the Qur'an and the heart, by which the heart is veiled from the Qur'an and the Qur'an from the heart. When the veil is lifted by faith, the heart begins to perceive the sweetness of the Qur'an, and thus through the successive effects of the Qur'an, faith continues to increase, until the person reaches the station of complete tranquility. Just as the effects of the Qur'an in the heart cause an increase in faith, so too the heart draws the effects of the Qur'an towards itself. This is why this phrase repeatedly occurs in the Qur'an: "Indeed in that are signs for the believers" (inna fi dhalika la-ayatin lil-mu'minin). This phrase repeats the same reality: "Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe" (inna fi dhalika la-ayatin li-qawmin yu'minun). And the meaning of the statement of some Companions, "We were given faith before we were given the Qur'an," is this.

This is why the Companions had a special bond and taste with the Qur'an, and the environment in which they found the fresh breezes helped them in this, while the Qur'an was their practical life. It was an action, not mere taste and perception. Among the narrations concerning the revelation of this verse is a report of Sa'd ibn Malik, who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to give him a sword as a share of the spoils. At that time the verses had not yet been revealed by which the spoils were returned to the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ). He had not been given the authority to dispose of them as he wished, and the Prophet gave him this answer: "Indeed this sword is neither mine nor yours; place it with the wealth." When Sa'd was called back from behind, although he had placed the sword and turned back, he expected that perhaps Allah had revealed some verses concerning the matter. He says: "I said, 'Has Allah revealed some verses concerning me?'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "You asked me for the sword when it was not in my power then; now, since Allah has given the spoils to me, I have given it to you." This was the state of these people with their Lord, and this was their conduct with this Qur'an that was being continuously revealed. This is a magnificent way of behaving.

In human history this was a remarkable era. Therefore they tasted the Qur'an in this way, and upon hearing it they immediately gave it reality in their practical lives. Their taste gave this reality a particularly excellent quality, and the listener and the reciter would influence one another. Although this first experience cannot be repeated, whenever a believing community arises on this earth such experiences continue to appear, provided that the movements which arise aim to establish the religion in the same way as the first Muslim community did; and within those communities which arise here and there and hold the goal of establishing the religion as the first community did, there arises the same taste for understanding the Qur'an that resembles that of the first community. Through its recitation their faith increases. For these communities, religion is the name of a movement whose aim is the establishment of religion, and they intend to repeat that first experience. For such people, faith is not mere wishing; rather, faith is called that reality which settles well in the heart and manifests itself in the form of action. "And upon their Lord they rely": "وعلى ربهم يتوكلون" — and they rely upon their Lord alone. Grammatically, this is its meaning, namely restriction (hasr).

They do not seek help from anyone by associating another with Allah, nor do they rely upon anyone else. Imam Ibn Kathir wrote: "They do not hope for anything except from Him; they do not turn their intention to anyone else, they do not seek refuge with anyone, they do not ask their needs from anyone, and their inclination is not toward anyone else; and they know that what Allah wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. He alone has authority in this universe, and He has no partner in it; no one can disobey His command. He is swift in reckoning." Accordingly, Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Relying upon Allah is the sweetness of faith."

This is the sincerity of the belief in the Oneness of Allah, the sincerity of servitude to Allah. Therefore it is not possible that a heart holds the belief in tawhid and yet at the same time that person relies upon others besides Allah. Those who rely upon others besides Allah and depend upon them should carefully examine their hearts and see whether faith is present in them or not.

Yes, reliance upon Allah does not prevent the taking of means, because the believer also takes the means in the path of faith and obedience. We believe that the Causer of causes is also Allah, and it is He who has commanded man to adopt the path of means. But the believer also has this faith: that the emergence of results does not depend upon means. Just as the means are within the creation and power of Allah, so too the results are created by Allah. In the believer's awareness and belief, it is not necessary that results appear after the means provided by God. Therefore, adopting means is worship and obedience, and results will appear by the decree of Allah. The emergence of results is subject to the decree of Allah. Only if Allah wills will results appear. In the awareness of a believer, there is no necessary connection between means and results. Likewise, the awareness of a believer is freed from servitude to means, and with this freedom, a believer adopts means for the sake of earning reward, so that he may be obedient to Allah.

Modern Jahiliyyah is still floundering in the dark sea of its belief that the connection between causes and effects is severed and the laws of nature are immutable, so that it may deny the decree of God and His unseen power. But as soon as this Jahiliyyah had travelled a certain distance on this path, it discovered that beyond it begin the limits of God's decree, and at that frontier this Jahiliyyah stands bewildered and perplexed. Now, having abandoned the theory that the laws of nature in the material world are immutable, it has adopted the theory of "probabilities." It is as though what it once called immutable has now become merely probable. And at the border of the unseen world where this Jahiliyyah stands, all its paths are closed beyond that point. This very reality must be acknowledged: it is the decree of God that operates in this world, and this verse of God, ﴿Thou knowest not; perhaps God will bring about some matter after that﴾ (Qur'an 65:1), governs that unseen realm. The theory of divine decree is the final and conclusive theory. And this theory plainly says that behind the material laws of this world the will of God is at work, and God's will is unrestricted. He does what He wills, His will is absolute and free, and He is not bound by the system of causes and effects that He Himself created.

Sir James, a professor of physics and mathematics, says: "Classical science asserted with certainty that nature can take only one path, and that it is the path prescribed for it before it set out. Along it nature must proceed from beginning to end. The law of cause and effect operates in this universe continually and permanently. There can be no deviation from the principle that state (A) will be followed by state (B). As for modern science, according to it one can say with certainty only this: after state (B), there is a probability that state (C) will follow; the probability of the appearance of state (C) is greater than the other probabilities, or the probability of J is greater than that of D, and so on."

Furthermore, it is within the scope of science to determine the relative probabilities of (B), (C) and (D). But it is difficult to say anything certain about the outcome: after state (A), which state will appear? For probability always remains probability, but which state has actually come to pass is then the decision of destiny. Now, what is the reality of destiny, whatever that reality may be? (A detailed discussion of this we have given under the verse "With Him are the keys of the unseen," see Part Seven, p. ...)

When the heart of the believer is freed from the pressure of apparent causes, then there is no justification left for relying on anyone other than God. For it is the decree of God from behind which everything emerges, and this is the certain reality. As for apparent causes, the results they produce can only be definite probabilities. This is that great revolution which the Islamic way of life produces in the human heart, and according to it human thought develops. Modern Jahiliyyah groped in darkness for three hundred years, and only after a full three hundred years has it been able to reach the threshold of this primary reality, namely from a purely rational standpoint. But it has not yet consciously entered into this reality, nor has humanity yet adopted the conduct that should be adopted toward God's system of decree and destiny, or the conduct that should be adopted toward apparent causes. This revolution is in essence a revolution of rational freedom and of reason. A conscious revolution is a political revolution, a social revolution and a moral revolution. And no person, as long as he is a slave to causes and regards nature as immutable, can be called truly free. For when he regards causes as immutable, he will become a slave to the will of men or be considered a slave to the will of nature. For if anyone regards anything as final other than the will and decree of God, let him understand that he is not free but a slave. This is why God commanded that one should rely upon God alone, and reliance upon God alone is an indication of faith and of its absence. The system of concepts in Islam is a single whole and a unity, and the system prescribed upon this worldview is likewise a whole, complete and unified. ﴿Who establish prayer﴾ (Qur'an 8:3). Here we see that faith appears before us in a dynamic form. In the truths stated earlier, faith was an inner and mental reality which was not visible, for the definition of faith is that it sits in the heart with dignity, and the actions of the limbs are what attest that it exists. Hence the indication of faith through action is outward, and the appearance of these outward signs is necessary so that testimony may be provided that faith exists within hearts.

The meaning of establishing prayer is not merely to perform the prayer, but to perform it in its true sense, such that it is evident that the worshipper stands before God. Prayer must not be merely standing, sitting and recitation, with bowing and prostration while the heart is heedless. If prayer is properly established, it is a witness to faith. ﴿And spend of what We have provided for them﴾ (Qur'an 8:3). This is general, whether it be zakat or other charities; whatever is spent will be from what God has given. Therefore it is regarded as part of the religion of God. The guidance of the Qur'an has its own colour and contains particular expressive indications. Here the indication is that you did not create this wealth and property; God has given it to you, and whatever has been given to you is the sustenance of God, and what God has given is so abundant that a person cannot count it. When a person gives from what God has bestowed, it is obvious that he gives a portion and keeps the rest for himself, yet the reality is that it is what God has given.

These are the qualities by which God has defined faith. Among these qualities is belief in God's oneness, and in accepting His oneness, remembrance of God, and then receiving a heartfelt impression from God's signs and remembrance; then trusting in God alone; then establishing prayer as it should be established; and finally, spending a portion of what God has given in His way. These are the signs of faith in this context.

These verses and qualities are in reality not the components and details of faith, as has been mentioned in other verses. Rather, what is described here is the actual situation, namely the actual circumstances in which disagreement arose over the spoils and booty, and the mutual relations among the believers were damaged. Therefore here the believers are informed of the qualities of the faithful and are reminded that the qualities of the believers are such; but if any one of these qualities is absent from a person, then the reality of faith may in practice be negated from such people. Hence these qualities are the foundational signs of faith, whether the faith possesses all these qualities or not, because it is the demand of the wisdom of Islamic training what conditions of faith it mentions for particular circumstances and which it does not mention. For the Islamic method of training is a practical and realistic method. It is not merely a theoretical procedure whereby it formulates a theory and spreads it, and nothing more. In accordance with this principle, this is the final commentary.

﴿Those are the true believers. For them are degrees with their Lord, and forgiveness, and a generous provision﴾ (Qur'an 8:4).
Such are the truly faithful. For them there are high ranks with their Lord, forgiveness of their faults, and excellent provision.

These are the qualities which any true believer finds present in his own self and his own deeds. If all these qualities are absent from a person's being, then in effect there is no quality of faith in him. Since these verses address an actual situation, their demand is that for those who display a particular conduct in specific circumstances there is a great reward, and for those in whom these qualities exist, with God there is a great reward and high ranks. Likewise, in them there is also an allusion to the events that took place at that time among the believers, as Hadhrat Ubadah ibn al-Samit said; so in these verses it was said that for those people there is forgiveness, and for those who disputed over property there is excellent provision. Therefore these verses also allude to those particular events. And the matter has been stated in principle: that believers are such; these are their qualities, and whoever lacks them should examine his own faith. ﴿Those are the true believers﴾ (Qur'an 8:4).

The first Islamic community is being taught that faith has a reality, and every believer should possess those realities within his soul; faith is not merely a claim. Faith is neither a name for a few words nor a name for a few innocent wishes. Hafiz Tabarani narrates through Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami, from Abu Bakr, from Ibn ibn al-Hubab, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abu al-Jahm, from Harith ibn Malik al-Ansari, who said: I passed by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the Messenger of God said: "Harith, how did you rise this morning?" Harith said, "I rose as a true believer." He (ﷺ) said, "Look at what you are saying, for everything has a reality. Tell me, what is the reality of your faith?" Harith said, "I have renounced the world; I stay awake at night and remain content during the day. My condition is as though I see the Great Throne of God with my own eyes, as though I see the people of Paradise with my own eyes meeting one another, and I see the people of Hell cursing one another."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Harith, you have attained it, so hold fast to it," and he said this three times. This companion, who was deemed worthy of a certificate of recognition from the Messenger of God, in describing his own state mentioned such matters that clearly manifest his consciousness, and he also mentioned things connected with deeds and movements: as though he sees the Throne of the Lord, sees the people of Paradise meeting one another, and sees the people of Hell.

This companion does not speak merely of theories. He continually speaks of actions. These actions and movements, together with that consciousness, dominate his life. He stays awake at night and rests peacefully during the day, and his certainty is such that everything appears to him.

We must be very serious about the reality of faith. Therefore in this matter we should not be so liberal. Faith must not be reduced to a few words that keep flowing on the tongue while practical life bears witness to the contrary. That condition is empty of the reality of faith. Caution does not mean that we become merely liberal regarding faith. The conscious reality of faith must exist, and caution is necessary in its conception, especially regarding those people who claim to have risen to perform the duty of leadership of religion, while the community in which they rise to establish the religion is entirely immersed in Jahiliyyah and has been moulded into the form of Jahiliyyah.

**Lesson 83: At a Glance**

This is the first lesson of this surah. Its subject is the *anfal* (the bounties, i.e. additional gains and special portions reserved by the leader) and the distribution of *ghanimah* (war booty). Anfal and ghanimah include everything that Muslims obtain on the battlefield when the fighting is *jihad fi sabilillah* (struggle in the way of Allah). The first dispute over the distribution of booty arose among the people of Badr. Allah turned the believers' attention to the matters of fear of Allah and obedience to the Messenger, and the feelings of faith and *taqwa* (God-consciousness) were stirred in their hearts.

Allah reminded them: "You had from the outset wished to attack the caravan and gain booty, but Allah's wisdom required that He bestow on you victory and honour." Then He told them to reflect on the stages of that battle: your numbers and equipment were very few compared with the enemy's, and they were far superior to you. Yet Allah strengthened your feet through the angels. Then He sent rain, which made fighting easier for you. Your feet were firmly planted, you were watering your livestock with the rainwater and bathing, because the battle of Badr was fought on sand, and in sand the feet of men and horses sink. Then you were reminded that a kind of sleep overtook you, and as soon as you slept you became tranquil. Then Allah cast terror into the hearts of your enemies and sent down a severe punishment upon them.

In the light of these experiences, the Qur'an commands you to show steadfastness in every battle, even though the strength of the enemy may seem greater to you outwardly, because it is Allah who actually kills. It is Allah who in reality shoots the arrow, and it is He who governs affairs. You are in truth only a veil for the decree of Allah; He drives you as He wills. After this, the lesson comments on the foolish behaviour of the polytheists, who before that event had prayed before Allah: "O Allah, if this party is in error and cuts off the ties of kinship, then destroy it in today's battle." Allah says: ﴿If you were seeking a decision, then the decision has come to you﴾.

The Muslims are told to remove hypocrisy from their lives and not to adopt the attitude of the hypocrites, who said, "We hear," but did not truly hear, because when they heard they did not accept.

At the end of this lesson, the Muslims are repeatedly called upon: "O believers! When the Messenger calls you, respond to him, because he gives you a call through which you will attain everlasting life, even though outwardly he may be calling you to death and slaughter." Allah reminds the believers to remember the time when you were few and weak, and were always afraid, on every side, that the enemy would snatch you away. In those circumstances Allah gave you refuge and support. And now there is a promise for you: if you adopt the path of *taqwa*, Allah will grant you decisive conduct and a decisive judgment, will forgive your sins, will overlook your shortcomings, and what Allah has prepared for you in the Hereafter is far greater than all the spoils and wealth of this world.

**Lesson 83: Explanation of Verses 1 to 29**

**Commentary on Verses 1 to 4**

﴿They ask you about the anfal. Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger. So fear Allah, set right the relations among yourselves, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.﴾ (8:1)

﴿The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, and when His verses are recited to them they increase their faith, and they put their trust in their Lord. Those who establish the prayer and spend out of what We have provided them. Those are truly the believers. For them are high ranks with their Lord, and forgiveness, and an honourable provision.﴾ (8:2–4)

The narrations about the revelation of these verses are many, and we mentioned a large part of them in the introduction to this surah. Here we add some other narrations, so that the circumstances in which this surah was generally revealed remain before the reader's eyes, especially the circumstances in which those verses concerning the booty were revealed. From these narrations it will also be known what the features of the community of Muslims were at the time of the establishment of the first Islamic government in Madinah, and what practical difficulties it was passing through.

Ibn Kathir says: Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Mardawayh (the wording is theirs), Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim narrated this report through Dawud ibn Abi Hind and Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. He said: When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Whoever does such and such will receive such and such a reward." Thus the young men of the people advanced, while the elders remained near the standards. When the time for the booty came, they began to make the demands which the Messenger (ﷺ) had promised them. Then the elders said: "Do not make claims to priority, for we were a shelter for you; had you suffered a defeat, you would have taken refuge with us." Then a dispute arose between these two groups. On this occasion Allah revealed these verses: ﴿They ask you about the anfal . . . to ". . . and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers"﴾.

And al-Thawri narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas. He said: When the battle of Badr took place, the Messenger (ﷺ) said, "Whoever kills someone will have such and such a reward, and whoever takes someone captive will be given such and such a reward." On that occasion Abu al-Yasar took two men captive, and they said, "Here they are, O Messenger of Allah; you promised us." Then Sa'd ibn Ubadah stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you give these people the booty in this way, nothing will remain for your companions. Moreover, we did not refrain from fighting because we did not need the reward, or because we feared the enemy. We stood firm here so that you would be protected, lest the enemy attack you from behind." So a considerable dispute arose, and on this occasion these verses were revealed: ﴿They ask you about the anfal. Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾. They said this, and in connection with the same matter this verse was also revealed: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as booty, one-fifth of it belongs to Allah . . .﴾.

Imam Ahmad narrated a report. He said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated it from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah al-Thaqafi, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: On the occasion of the battle of Badr, my brother Umayr was martyred. I killed Sa'id ibn al-As and took his sword. The name of that sword was "Dhu al-Kafiyah." I came with this sword to the Messenger (ﷺ). He said, "Go and throw it into the spoils." He said: I threw the sword and returned, but only Allah knew my condition, that my brother had also been killed, and the valuable thing that had fallen into my hand could not be found. I had only gone a short distance when Surah al-Anfal was revealed. The Messenger (ﷺ) commanded me, "Go and take the sword that fell into your hand."

Imam Ahmad says: Aswad ibn Amir narrated from Abu Bakr, from Asim ibn Abi al-Nujud, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: I said to the Messenger (ﷺ), "Today Allah has given me relief from the polytheists; grant me this sword." The Messenger (ﷺ) said, "This sword is neither for me nor for you. Place it there." So I put the sword down and returned. I thought: perhaps this sword will go to a person who has not fulfilled its right as I did. Suddenly I heard someone calling behind me. I thought perhaps a verse had been revealed about me. The Messenger (ﷺ) said, "You asked me for the sword, and it was not mine; now it has been granted to me, so now it is yours." On this occasion these verses were revealed: ﴿They ask you about the anfal. Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger﴾.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa'i narrated this report from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash. Al-Tirmidhi, through several chains, called it *hasan sahih* (good and authentic).

From these narrations, the atmosphere in which Surah al-Anfal was revealed becomes clear. A person reading these reports is somewhat astonished: are these the people of Badr, and are these the things they did? For among them were the Muhajirun, who had sacrificed everything in Makkah and had come to Madinah solely because of their convictions, and in their eyes the worldly interests of this life were in any case worthless. And among them were the foremost Ansar, who had given refuge to these Muhajirun and had shared with them their lands and wealth. They did not withhold from them any worldly benefit. Concerning them Allah says: ﴿They love those who migrate to them, and they do not find in their breasts any need for what has been given to them; they prefer others above themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾ (59:9).

The circumstances described here are alluded to in these very reports. At that time, the booty was connected with the bravery and valour that a soldier displayed on the battlefield, and this material reward was also a sign that the recipient had shown valour. In that period people desired to receive a special reward from the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which would be considered a reward directly from Allah. Especially in that first encounter which took place between Islam and unbelief. Under the influence of this greed and the lure of reward, another quality was overshadowed, and some people spoke about the booty, and Allah drew their attention to the importance of that quality. That quality was: in dealings with one another, a little good conduct is needed, and there is a severe need for the reform of your hearts. So they perceived this matter well and understood it. On one occasion, Hadrat Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: "These verses were revealed concerning us, the Companions of Badr, when we disputed about the booty and went beyond the moral limits in it. Allah took those spoils out of our control and placed them in the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Allah Most High gave this community both practical and verbal training. He took away from them the authority over the distribution of the booty and placed it entirely in the hands of the Prophet (ﷺ), until detailed commands concerning the distribution of spoils were revealed. Thus there was no longer any right for them to dispute in this matter. This became a grace of Allah. The Messenger of Allah distributed it among them in the manner in which the Lord had guided him. Alongside this practical reform, this long and continuous guidance was also given to them, and this guidance extended throughout this surah. It began thus:

﴿They ask you about the anfal. Say: the anfal belong to Allah and the Messenger. So fear Allah, set right the relations among yourselves, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.﴾

This question came from those who had disputed over the spoils, and this call is also directed at them: fear Allah. Allah is the creator of your hearts and knows the thoughts that arise in your hearts. Allah does not take to account the reason why a desire for worldly aims arises in someone's heart, or why a dispute arose over it. Although at the root of that dispute there was the wish that rewards should come from the hands of the Messenger, which would be proof of their good performance. But Allah made it necessary for the success of this world and the Hereafter that you create in your hearts the feeling of *taqwa* and fear of Allah, because a heart that is not connected with Allah, and does not fear His wrath, and has no desire to obtain His pleasure, can never disregard worldly interests, and can never consciously keep itself away from those defilements.

The truth is that *taqwa* is the bridle of hearts, and through *taqwa* alone hearts can be led, and can be led with great ease. The Holy Qur'an, from beginning to end, leads human beings through this bridle of *taqwa* and connection with Allah, and presents it as the means of reform.

The Qur'an says: ﴿So fear Allah and set right the relations among yourselves﴾. And then it is said that this is the means through which you can obey the Messenger: ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers﴾.

The obedience owed to the Messenger first means that you accept the rulings that have come from Allah concerning the spoils (al-anfal). For example, the spoils of war have now been removed from the ownership of the fighters, and their ownership has been given to Allah and His Messenger. Therefore, the right to dispose of them now belongs solely to Allah and His Messenger. It is the duty of the believers to accept the rulings of Allah and His Messenger regarding this, and to accept the Messenger of Allah's distribution in accordance with the instructions of Allah, accepting it willingly, being content with what is decreed, improving their mutual relations, correcting their understanding and feelings, and purifying their hearts towards one another. "In kuntum mu'minin": if you are believers.

It is necessary that faith have a practical and real form, and that this practical form make faith visible and manifest. It should appear in embodied form, and a person's deeds should be the interpreter of his faith. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Faith is not mere wishful thinking, but it is that which settles in the heart and which deeds confirm." This is why such phrases in the Qur'an come again and again in a decisive manner, and their purpose is precisely to show what the reality of faith is and what its connection with deeds is. Faith is not merely the name of words that flow on the tongue, nor is it mere wishing, which has no reality in the real world and no existence in the world of action.

After this, it is explained what the true qualities of a sincere believer are, so that it may be made clear what is meant by "in kuntum mu'minin." Accordingly, it is stated that in the sight of the Lord of the worlds, the believer is one such as this:

"The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble; and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith; and upon their Lord they rely. Those who establish the prayer and spend out of what We have provided them. Those are the believers in truth. For them are degrees with their Lord and forgiveness and an honorable provision." (Qur'an 8:2–4)

Linguistically and grammatically, the manner of expression in these verses is extremely meaningful and carries profound significance. Here the particle of restriction (innama) is used. There is no reason to interpret the restrictive sense of innama away, since Allah wishes to state a matter with great emphasis. Some interpretations have said that it means complete faith; but if Allah had wished to say it that way, He would have said, "The perfect believers are those who are such and such." In reality, this is a highly detailed expression. The meaning is that those whose awareness and feelings are such, and whose qualities and deeds are such, are truly believers; and those who do not possess these qualities and deeds are not believers, because at the end of this verse this point is emphasized repeatedly: "Those are the believers in truth." And those who are not truly believers, what kind of believers are they then called? The expressions of the Qur'an explain and interpret one another. Allah says: "What, then, is there after the truth but error?" (10:32). Therefore, whatever is not truth will be error. I say that no expression can be the counterpart of "al-mu'minun haqqan" (the believers in truth). "Al-mu'minun imanan ghair..." Therefore, this clear and precise manner of expression in the Qur'an should not be put on the lathe of interpretations, which displace every correct concept and every correct expression from its place.

This is why some of the righteous predecessors (salaf) used to say that whoever does not have these qualities in his belief and in his deeds has not attained faith, and is not a believer at all. In Ibn Kathir it is related: Ali ibn Talha narrates from Ibn Abbas that in the verse "The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble," there is in fact a reference to the hypocrites. When they are praying, nothing enters their hearts; in truth they do not believe in the verses of Allah and do not rely upon Allah at all. And when they are not in front of people, they do not maintain ties of kinship, nor do they pay the zakat on their wealth. So Allah informed about these hypocrites that they are not believers. After this, Allah enumerated the qualities of true believers, such as:

"The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble," thus they fulfill their obligations. "And when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith": that is, when the verses of Allah are recited to them, their faith increases; that is, their affirmation increases. "And upon their Lord they rely": and they put their trust in their Lord.

In the following lines we shall prove that without these realities the very existence of faith does not remain. And this does not mean that with them faith becomes complete and without them it becomes deficient; rather, the question is of the existence or non-existence of faith: "The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned." When a believer remembers Allah in connection with a command or a prohibition, a spiritual trembling arises in his heart. Awe takes hold of his heart because of the majesty of Allah, and waves of the fear of Allah rise in his heart. In this way, the awe of Allah stands against his shortcomings and sins, and thus it becomes the cause of action and strength. As Umm al-Darda (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Wajal (trembling) in the heart is like the peeling of a palm frond. Do you not find its burning?" He said, "Yes." She said, "When you find it, then call upon Allah at that moment, for supplication removes that." To understand "wajal," think of it this way: when someone develops blisters, he feels a burning. Do you not feel a trembling in such a state? Yes, it is so. When you find such a state, call upon Allah; through supplication this state passes.

In short, this is the state in which restlessness arises in the heart, and in such circumstances, through remembrance and supplication, a person attains comfort and tranquility. This is the state in which a person remembers Allah in connection with a command and a prohibition. "And when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith": and when the verses of Allah are recited to them, their faith increases. For the believing heart, in truth, there are in these verses points that are a cause of increase in its faith and through which the believer attains tranquility of heart. The Qur'an deals directly with the believing heart, and only the veil of disbelief can come between the Qur'an and the heart, by which the heart is veiled from the Qur'an and the Qur'an from the heart. When the veil is lifted by faith, the heart begins to perceive the sweetness of the Qur'an, and thus through the successive effects of the Qur'an, faith continues to increase, until the person reaches the station of complete tranquility. Just as the effects of the Qur'an in the heart cause an increase in faith, so too the heart draws the effects of the Qur'an towards itself. This is why this phrase repeatedly occurs in the Qur'an: "Indeed in that are signs for the believers" (inna fi dhalika la-ayatin lil-mu'minin). This phrase repeats the same reality: "Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe" (inna fi dhalika la-ayatin li-qawmin yu'minun). And the meaning of the statement of some Companions, "We were given faith before we were given the Qur'an," is this.

This is why the Companions had a special bond and taste with the Qur'an, and the environment in which they found the fresh breezes helped them in this, while the Qur'an was their practical life. It was an action, not mere taste and perception. Among the narrations concerning the revelation of this verse is a report of Sa'd ibn Malik, who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to give him a sword as a share of the spoils. At that time the verses had not yet been revealed by which the spoils were returned to the authority of the Prophet (ﷺ). He had not been given the authority to dispose of them as he wished, and the Prophet gave him this answer: "Indeed this sword is neither mine nor yours; place it with the wealth." When Sa'd was called back from behind, although he had placed the sword and turned back, he expected that perhaps Allah had revealed some verses concerning the matter. He says: "I said, 'Has Allah revealed some verses concerning me?'" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "You asked me for the sword when it was not in my power then; now, since Allah has given the spoils to me, I have given it to you." This was the state of these people with their Lord, and this was their conduct with this Qur'an that was being continuously revealed. This is a magnificent way of behaving.

In human history this was a remarkable era. Therefore they tasted the Qur'an in this way, and upon hearing it they immediately gave it reality in their practical lives. Their taste gave this reality a particularly excellent quality, and the listener and the reciter would influence one another. Although this first experience cannot be repeated, whenever a believing community arises on this earth such experiences continue to appear, provided that the movements which arise aim to establish the religion in the same way as the first Muslim community did; and within those communities which arise here and there and hold the goal of establishing the religion as the first community did, there arises the same taste for understanding the Qur'an that resembles that of the first community. Through its recitation their faith increases. For these communities, religion is the name of a movement whose aim is the establishment of religion, and they intend to repeat that first experience. For such people, faith is not mere wishing; rather, faith is called that reality which settles well in the heart and manifests itself in the form of action. "And upon their Lord they rely": "وعلى ربهم يتوكلون" — and they rely upon their Lord alone. Grammatically, this is its meaning, namely restriction (hasr).

They do not seek help from anyone by associating another with Allah, nor do they rely upon anyone else. Imam Ibn Kathir wrote: "They do not hope for anything except from Him; they do not turn their intention to anyone else, they do not seek refuge with anyone, they do not ask their needs from anyone, and their inclination is not toward anyone else; and they know that what Allah wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. He alone has authority in this universe, and He has no partner in it; no one can disobey His command. He is swift in reckoning." Accordingly, Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Relying upon Allah is the sweetness of faith."

This is the sincerity of the belief in the Oneness of Allah, the sincerity of servitude to Allah. Therefore it is not possible that a heart holds the belief in tawhid and yet at the same time that person relies upon others besides Allah. Those who rely upon others besides Allah and depend upon them should carefully examine their hearts and see whether faith is present in them or not.

Yes, reliance upon Allah does not prevent the taking of means, because the believer also takes the means in the path of faith and obedience. We believe that the Causer of causes is also Allah, and it is He who has commanded man to adopt the path of means. But the believer also has this faith: that the emergence of results does not depend upon means. Just as the means are within the creation and power of Allah, so too the results are created by Allah. In the believer's awareness and belief, it is not necessary that results appear after the means provided by God. Therefore, adopting means is worship and obedience, and results will appear by the decree of Allah. The emergence of results is subject to the decree of Allah. Only if Allah wills will results appear. In the awareness of a believer, there is no necessary connection between means and results. Likewise, the awareness of a believer is freed from servitude to means, and with this freedom, a believer adopts means for the sake of earning reward, so that he may be obedient to Allah.

Modern Jahiliyyah is still floundering in the dark sea of its belief that the connection between causes and effects is severed and the laws of nature are immutable, so that it may deny the decree of God and His unseen power. But as soon as this Jahiliyyah had travelled a certain distance on this path, it discovered that beyond it begin the limits of God's decree, and at that frontier this Jahiliyyah stands bewildered and perplexed. Now, having abandoned the theory that the laws of nature in the material world are immutable, it has adopted the theory of "probabilities." It is as though what it once called immutable has now become merely probable. And at the border of the unseen world where this Jahiliyyah stands, all its paths are closed beyond that point. This very reality must be acknowledged: it is the decree of God that operates in this world, and this verse of God, ﴿Thou knowest not; perhaps God will bring about some matter after that﴾ (Qur'an 65:1), governs that unseen realm. The theory of divine decree is the final and conclusive theory. And this theory plainly says that behind the material laws of this world the will of God is at work, and God's will is unrestricted. He does what He wills, His will is absolute and free, and He is not bound by the system of causes and effects that He Himself created.

Sir James, a professor of physics and mathematics, says: "Classical science asserted with certainty that nature can take only one path, and that it is the path prescribed for it before it set out. Along it nature must proceed from beginning to end. The law of cause and effect operates in this universe continually and permanently. There can be no deviation from the principle that state (A) will be followed by state (B). As for modern science, according to it one can say with certainty only this: after state (B), there is a probability that state (C) will follow; the probability of the appearance of state (C) is greater than the other probabilities, or the probability of J is greater than that of D, and so on."

Furthermore, it is within the scope of science to determine the relative probabilities of (B), (C) and (D). But it is difficult to say anything certain about the outcome: after state (A), which state will appear? For probability always remains probability, but which state has actually come to pass is then the decision of destiny. Now, what is the reality of destiny, whatever that reality may be? (A detailed discussion of this we have given under the verse "With Him are the keys of the unseen," see Part Seven, p. ...)

When the heart of the believer is freed from the pressure of apparent causes, then there is no justification left for relying on anyone other than God. For it is the decree of God from behind which everything emerges, and this is the certain reality. As for apparent causes, the results they produce can only be definite probabilities. This is that great revolution which the Islamic way of life produces in the human heart, and according to it human thought develops. Modern Jahiliyyah groped in darkness for three hundred years, and only after a full three hundred years has it been able to reach the threshold of this primary reality, namely from a purely rational standpoint. But it has not yet consciously entered into this reality, nor has humanity yet adopted the conduct that should be adopted toward God's system of decree and destiny, or the conduct that should be adopted toward apparent causes. This revolution is in essence a revolution of rational freedom and of reason. A conscious revolution is a political revolution, a social revolution and a moral revolution. And no person, as long as he is a slave to causes and regards nature as immutable, can be called truly free. For when he regards causes as immutable, he will become a slave to the will of men or be considered a slave to the will of nature. For if anyone regards anything as final other than the will and decree of God, let him understand that he is not free but a slave. This is why God commanded that one should rely upon God alone, and reliance upon God alone is an indication of faith and of its absence. The system of concepts in Islam is a single whole and a unity, and the system prescribed upon this worldview is likewise a whole, complete and unified. ﴿Who establish prayer﴾ (Qur'an 8:3). Here we see that faith appears before us in a dynamic form. In the truths stated earlier, faith was an inner and mental reality which was not visible, for the definition of faith is that it sits in the heart with dignity, and the actions of the limbs are what attest that it exists. Hence the indication of faith through action is outward, and the appearance of these outward signs is necessary so that testimony may be provided that faith exists within hearts.

The meaning of establishing prayer is not merely to perform the prayer, but to perform it in its true sense, such that it is evident that the worshipper stands before God. Prayer must not be merely standing, sitting and recitation, with bowing and prostration while the heart is heedless. If prayer is properly established, it is a witness to faith. ﴿And spend of what We have provided for them﴾ (Qur'an 8:3). This is general, whether it be zakat or other charities; whatever is spent will be from what God has given. Therefore it is regarded as part of the religion of God. The guidance of the Qur'an has its own colour and contains particular expressive indications. Here the indication is that you did not create this wealth and property; God has given it to you, and whatever has been given to you is the sustenance of God, and what God has given is so abundant that a person cannot count it. When a person gives from what God has bestowed, it is obvious that he gives a portion and keeps the rest for himself, yet the reality is that it is what God has given.

These are the qualities by which God has defined faith. Among these qualities is belief in God's oneness, and in accepting His oneness, remembrance of God, and then receiving a heartfelt impression from God's signs and remembrance; then trusting in God alone; then establishing prayer as it should be established; and finally, spending a portion of what God has given in His way. These are the signs of faith in this context.

These verses and qualities are in reality not the components and details of faith, as has been mentioned in other verses. Rather, what is described here is the actual situation, namely the actual circumstances in which disagreement arose over the spoils and booty, and the mutual relations among the believers were damaged. Therefore here the believers are informed of the qualities of the faithful and are reminded that the qualities of the believers are such; but if any one of these qualities is absent from a person, then the reality of faith may in practice be negated from such people. Hence these qualities are the foundational signs of faith, whether the faith possesses all these qualities or not, because it is the demand of the wisdom of Islamic training what conditions of faith it mentions for particular circumstances and which it does not mention. For the Islamic method of training is a practical and realistic method. It is not merely a theoretical procedure whereby it formulates a theory and spreads it, and nothing more. In accordance with this principle, this is the final commentary.

﴿Those are the true believers. For them are degrees with their Lord, and forgiveness, and a generous provision﴾ (Qur'an 8:4).
Such are the truly faithful. For them there are high ranks with their Lord, forgiveness of their faults, and excellent provision.

These are the qualities which any true believer finds present in his own self and his own deeds. If all these qualities are absent from a person's being, then in effect there is no quality of faith in him. Since these verses address an actual situation, their demand is that for those who display a particular conduct in specific circumstances there is a great reward, and for those in whom these qualities exist, with God there is a great reward and high ranks. Likewise, in them there is also an allusion to the events that took place at that time among the believers, as Hadhrat Ubadah ibn al-Samit said; so in these verses it was said that for those people there is forgiveness, and for those who disputed over property there is excellent provision. Therefore these verses also allude to those particular events. And the matter has been stated in principle: that believers are such; these are their qualities, and whoever lacks them should examine his own faith. ﴿Those are the true believers﴾ (Qur'an 8:4).

The first Islamic community is being taught that faith has a reality, and every believer should possess those realities within his soul; faith is not merely a claim. Faith is neither a name for a few words nor a name for a few innocent wishes. Hafiz Tabarani narrates through Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Hadrami, from Abu Bakr, from Ibn ibn al-Hubab, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Hilal, from Muhammad ibn Abu al-Jahm, from Harith ibn Malik al-Ansari, who said: I passed by the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the Messenger of God said: "Harith, how did you rise this morning?" Harith said, "I rose as a true believer." He (ﷺ) said, "Look at what you are saying, for everything has a reality. Tell me, what is the reality of your faith?" Harith said, "I have renounced the world; I stay awake at night and remain content during the day. My condition is as though I see the Great Throne of God with my own eyes, as though I see the people of Paradise with my own eyes meeting one another, and I see the people of Hell cursing one another."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Harith, you have attained it, so hold fast to it," and he said this three times. This companion, who was deemed worthy of a certificate of recognition from the Messenger of God, in describing his own state mentioned such matters that clearly manifest his consciousness, and he also mentioned things connected with deeds and movements: as though he sees the Throne of the Lord, sees the people of Paradise meeting one another, and sees the people of Hell.

This companion does not speak merely of theories. He continually speaks of actions. These actions and movements, together with that consciousness, dominate his life. He stays awake at night and rests peacefully during the day, and his certainty is such that everything appears to him.

We must be very serious about the reality of faith. Therefore in this matter we should not be so liberal. Faith must not be reduced to a few words that keep flowing on the tongue while practical life bears witness to the contrary. That condition is empty of the reality of faith. Caution does not mean that we become merely liberal regarding faith. The conscious reality of faith must exist, and caution is necessary in its conception, especially regarding those people who claim to have risen to perform the duty of leadership of religion, while the community in which they rise to establish the religion is entirely immersed in Jahiliyyah and has been moulded into the form of Jahiliyyah.

...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verses 5–8:

Now, from verse 5 onward to verse 14, the events of the battle are described, as a result of which these spoils of war came into hand, and as a consequence differences arose among the Muslims, and they became entangled with one another, as Hadrat Ubadah ibn al-Samit described with great sincerity, clarity and frankness. Here a general comment is made on the circumstances and events, and the positions and feelings of various people regarding them are recorded. From this whole commentary it becomes clear that in this battle the Muslims were, as it were, a veil for the hand of divine power, and whatever events occurred and whatever results emerged, including the spoils of war and the disputes concerning them, all of them were wonders of divine destiny. Everything took place in accordance with Allah's plan, destiny and guidance. As for the plans or intentions the Muslims themselves had regarding this battle, they were a very trivial matter, extremely limited. And what Allah intended was very great and boundless, because Allah wanted this encounter to be a great and decisive one (the Day of Criterion, Yawm al-Furqan), and to have effects both on the earth and in the heavens. Its benefit would reach the inhabitants of the highest assembly (al-mala' al-a'la), and the creatures of the earth would also be affected. Through it the course of human history was to be changed completely. He says that a group among you was going out to that battle with great reluctance. Some started a dispute over the spoils (al-anfal). So see that what you were thinking, and what you liked or disliked, was very insignificant compared with the decisions being made by Allah. All affairs ultimately lie in the hand of Allah.

...

Allah placed the authority over the spoils of war in the hand of the Prophet ﷺ so that he would distribute them among them on the principle of equality. As is coming later, he was given the authority that the khums (one-fifth) was reserved for the Messenger ﷺ for public expenses, and this arrangement was made so that, in the sacred duty of jihad, the greed among the believers' hearts that they would also receive something from the spoils would be removed, so that disputes over the spoils would not arise in the future. In this matter the right of disposal was placed in the hand of the Messenger ﷺ. As a result of the Prophet's ﷺ distribution, obviously there was no question of anyone having any complaint, and so that the resentment would be removed from the hearts of those who had gathered the spoils, since they were, after all, equal partners with everyone on the principle of equality.

Now Allah, Exalted is He, illustrates here, by presenting an example from their own conduct, that what Allah wills is better. And what they themselves wish is insignificant in comparison with Allah's plan. Therefore they should understand that the Islamic law which Allah is revealing regarding the anfal will be the better one, because people can see only the benefit in front of them; the unseen world is not before their eyes. And Allah makes this comment, taking as its subject the very event that is before them and is part of the same battle in which spoils were obtained and they began to quarrel. About that battle, what they intended, and what Allah decided for them. Now look at your own intention and also at Allah's intention; see how great the difference is in worth and value. How far apart these two intentions are.

*"As your Lord brought you out of your house in truth, though a party of the believers were averse. They disputed with you concerning the truth after it had become clear, as if they were being driven to death while looking on. And when Allah promised you that one of the two parties would be yours, and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours, while Allah intended to establish the truth by His words and to cut off the roots of the disbelievers; so that He might establish truth and abolish falsehood, even though the guilty disliked it."* (Qur'an 8:5–8)

The sharing of the spoils by returning them to Allah and His Messenger, then gathering them and distributing them among the Muslims on the principle of equality, and some people disliking this principle of equality, and earlier the Prophet ﷺ giving some young men a better share than others, were likewise unpleasing to people, just as going out to the battlefield was unpleasing to those people. Because the opposing side was equipped with better weapons and equipment. Therefore some of the believers disliked the battle at that time, but the outcomes were all laid out before them.
