Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 8, verse 24:

Now the believers are addressed again, that they should answer the call of Allah and the Messenger. For answering the call of the Messenger is beneficial for you, and if you refuse, it will be bad for you.

In this call are presented those beliefs and conceptions by which hearts and minds are filled with life, and become purified of all superstitions and ignorance. People are freed from illusions and fables, and from the bonds of apparent causes and natural laws, and it delivers man from the worship of other than Allah and from the slavery of fellow human beings.

This call presents before you a legal system that is from Allah. In this legal system are presented the principles of human freedom and human dignity that are from Allah. In its social system all people stand in one row; they are of absolutely equal standing. In this system there is no rule of an individual, there is no concept of the rule of a class, there is no concept of the rule of a race, there is no concept of the rule of a nation; rather, in this system all people are free and mutually equal, and all of them are bound only by the law of the Lord of the worlds.

This call invites them to a system of life, a system of thought, and a system of concepts, which frees them from every kind of bond except the laws of nature. These laws of nature are those rules and regulations which the Creator of nature has organized. This Creator knows His creatures well. These rules and regulations protect the creative powers of man from mutual clash and conflict, and they do not waste these creative powers, nor do they eliminate them, nor do they place any negative restrictions upon them.

This call invites you to strength, honour and exaltation, and teaches them that they should strengthen their beliefs and their system. They should place complete trust in their Lord and in their religion. Rise up with this call and grant this freedom to all the people of the world. Grant freedom to all people from the slavery of other human beings like themselves, because throughout the world people have been enslaved by rebels and transgressors.

This call invites them to jihad in the way of Allah, so that the system of Allah's sovereignty may be established in the world, so that the lives of people may be arranged according to that system, and so that the authority of those self-styled claimants of supreme sovereignty may be ended in the world. Those who have reserved for themselves the right of Allah's sovereignty and the station of supreme authority, until they accept the command and authority of Allah on this earth. This jihad should continue until the religion is entirely for Allah alone. If in the course of this jihad their lives are lost, they will attain the rank of martyrdom.

This is the comprehensive introduction to the call which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is giving, and therefore this call is a call to grant life in every meaning and every aspect.

The reality is that the religion of Islam is a complete code of life. It is not a secret belief. It is a practical system, and under the shade of this system humanity in fact attains life and progress. This is why it was said here that the call of the Messenger is in fact a call to make you alive. And it is that which, in every field and from every aspect, makes any society live forever. The Qur'an sums up this great truth in a few words. Consider once again:

يٰٓاَيُّھَا الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوا اسْتَجِيْبُوْا لِلّٰهِ وَلِلرَّسُوْلِ اِذَا دَعَاكُمْ لِمَا يُحْيِيْكُمْ ۔ "O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life."

Answer his call by accepting it willingly and becoming obedient servants. Allah could, though He might compel you onto the path of guidance, but He did not do so.

وَاعْلَمُوْٓا اَنَّ اللّٰهَ يَحُوْلُ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهٖ ۔ "And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart." He is the Absolute Powerful, and His power is an extremely frightening power. He even intervenes between a person and his own heart and mind, and exercises a decisive role. He dominates it, blocks its way, and turns it in whichever direction He wills, in whatever manner He wills. Whoever has a heart in his side has no control over it.

In reality this is a frightening power, and the Qur'an draws its picture in such words. Human expression is in reality completely incapable of such a sensory, verbal, meaningful and impactful expression.

This frightening image is the guarantor of a Muslim's constant alertness. The believer remains vigilant at all times, cautious, and keeps the beating of his heart, its inclinations and its tendencies under control. He keeps every whisper and every evil inclination under control so that he does not slip. He always keeps his eye on his path, on the places where there is a danger of stumbling. Where are the whisperings and attractive places? This is because a believer keeps his relationship with Allah strong, so that at any moment of heedlessness, through any slight slip, by means of any action, he does not go astray.

Although he was the Messenger of Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ often used to recite this supplication:

یا مقلب القلوب ثبت قلبی علی دینک۔ "O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." If this was the condition of the Messenger of Allah, then what will be the condition of us people who are neither messengers nor infallible?

This is the scene from which hearts tremble, and when a believer finds himself addressed by the Qur'anic verses, his whole body shakes. For if even the heart at his side is not his own but is in the control of Allah, then what is his standing? Consider the verse once again:

يٰٓاَيُّھَا الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوا اسْتَجِيْبُوْا لِلّٰهِ وَلِلرَّسُوْلِ اِذَا دَعَاكُمْ لِمَا يُحْيِيْكُمْ "O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life."

By presenting this verse, Allah tells them that Allah has the power to compel you to answer, so that you could be forced to accept this call against your will, if He wished. But Allah wants to grant you the honour that you become obedient and accept this call by your own will and choice, so that you are rewarded for it, and your humanity is elevated above the level of one who is compelled. You reach the lofty station of humanity and enter among the creatures who attain guidance by their own choice, becoming an understanding and deliberate creation, and walk upon this path by your purpose, will, knowledge and recognition.

Because وَاَنَّهٗٓ اِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُوْنَ "and that to Him you will be gathered." Your hearts are in His hand. You will have to rise and stand in the field of resurrection. There is no other path for you except this, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. But despite this state of affairs, Allah invites you so that you walk this path freely, not in the form of a subdued and compelled servant.

Following this, the believers are warned against abandoning the act of jihad fi sabilillah and against abandoning this call, which is the water of life. For jihad means the eradication of evil from the world, and evil is harmful to everyone.

What is fitnah? Trial and affliction are fitnah. And a society which allows some of its ignorant members to commit oppression under any circumstances, and does not block the path of the oppressors, does not confront them, deserves that the whole of it be overtaken by corruption (fasad). Let it be remembered that nothing can cause greater corruption than placing obstacles in the way of the Islamic Shariah and the Islamic system. Therefore Islam is a system whose parts all stand as guarantors for one another. It is a positive system, and it does not permit its adherents to oppress one another and corruption to spread in that society, let alone that the complete religion of Allah should be suspended in that society, and that the sovereignty, governance and divinity of Allah should be denied, with the servitude of human beings established in its place, and this society should remain silent and yet still expect that Allah will protect these people from fitnah and affliction, merely because they are righteous individually.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 26:

In confronting oppression, one must give both life and property in sacrifice. For this reason the Qur'an reminds the first community of Muslims, its immediate addressees, to remember that they were weak and few in equipment. You were beset by hardships, and a climate of fear and dread always hung over you. But when you came under the protection of the Islamic call, you became honoured, prosperous, and owners of good provision. Therefore do not become heedless of this call, in which lies for you the water of life, which is a gift of Allah, and Allah Himself is its protector.

﴿And remember when you were few and considered weak in the land, fearing that people might snatch you away. Then He sheltered you, strengthened you with His help, and provided you with good things, that perhaps you would be grateful.﴾ Remember the time when you were few, when you were regarded as powerless in the land, and you feared that people would wipe you out. Then Allah gave you a place of refuge, strengthened your hands with His help, and gave you good provision, so that perhaps you would be thankful.

Remember your former position so that you may be certain that the Islamic call is truly the water of life. Keep this in mind so that you do not stop struggling in the path of the Islamic call and facing its difficulties. Just recall your days of weakness and fear. Now Allah has commanded you to fight the polytheists, and the Messenger has advised you to fight the armed army of the Quraysh, and you do not like this. But remember also the days of Makkah, when dangers came at you from every direction, and now you are revolutionaries, victors, deserving of the reward of the Hereafter, and recipients of goodly provision. Have good foods and provisions not been given to you? Yet you do not thank Allah for them.

The Qur'an has expressed the state of fear and weakness in these words: ﴿takhafuna an yatakhattafakumu an-nas﴾, "you feared that people would snatch you away." This is a scene in which a person awaits a calamity that may descend at any moment. He is waiting for an event in a state of fear, as if he sees the coming calamity with his own eyes. In the frightening turmoil his eyes are restless. It appears that dreadful hands are advancing, and there is a small number of Muslims crouching in a fearful state.

From that frightening scene, He brought you out into security, victory, help, comfort and a life of provision, under the shade of Allah and in the protection of Allah: ﴿fa'awakum wa ayyadakum bi-nasrihi wa razaqakum min at-tayyibat﴾ "Then Allah gave you a place of refuge, strengthened your hands with His help, and gave you good provision, so that perhaps you would become thankful."

And this guidance of Allah remained with them so that they might render thanks and attain reward: ﴿la'allakum tashkurun﴾, "so that perhaps you would be thankful." Who is there who would reflect upon this great revolution and then not respond to this firm, peaceful and complete call, that is, to the call of the Prophet ﷺ? And who is there who would reflect upon Allah's blessings and favours, His support and aid, and these scenes presented in the Qur'an, and not respond to them? Therefore these scenes have very powerful effects and clear signals and guidance for the listener.

Furthermore, this first group of the Muslim community consisted of those who had personally passed through these circumstances in practice, and the scenes of both hardship and harshness, and of abundance and peace, were fresh in their minds. They were well aware of their past and present. In this way the Qur'an's call made a greater impact upon them.

Every Islamic movement today whose aim is to revive this religion practically in the lives of Muslims and to establish a collective order according to it on this earth, even if it is not practically passing through these two stages and has not itself seen these two conditions, the Qur'an still addresses it in the same way, and today we are the fulfilment of Allah's saying: ﴿idh antum qalilun mustad'afuna fi al-ardi takhafuna an yatakhattafakumu an-nas﴾. "Remember when you were few, regarded as powerless in the land, and you feared that people would wipe you out." Therefore it is better for the Islamic movement of today to respond to this call to a new life to which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is calling, and to await with utmost certainty and confidence the time when Allah's true promise will come to pass, which He made to the first Islamic movement and which was fulfilled. This is His promise to every movement that is established in the name of Allah, which bears the difficulties of this path and awaits its outcome.

﴿fa'awakum wa ayyadakum bi-nasrihi wa razaqakum min at-tayyibat la'allakum tashkurun﴾. Then Allah gave you a place of refuge, strengthened your hands with His help, and gave you good provision, that perhaps you would be thankful.

Outward appearances can be deceptive, but the matter of an Islamic movement is between it and Allah, and it relies upon Allah's promise, and Allah's promise is bound to be fulfilled. And it is in favour of the Islamic movement whose aim is to establish the Islamic revolution.

Now the believers are once again addressed. The financial circumstances, dealings and the interests of one's children sometimes prevent a person from striving, out of fear and miserliness. The life to which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ invites is a dignified life, and in the pursuit of this life difficulties will inevitably arise and sacrifices must also be made. Therefore the Qur'an corrects these weaknesses by warning the Islamic movement about the trial of wealth and the trial of children. Both of these things are a trial in the sense that through them a person's faith is tested. Passing through this test and trial is a difficult task. Because of them, a person holds back from the call to jihad and falls short in fulfilling the demands of trust (amanah), covenant ('ahd) and allegiance (bay'ah). Therefore, be warned that remaining behind from jihad is treachery against the Messenger of Allah and betrayal of the trust that has been entrusted to the Muslims, namely the aim of raising the word of Allah (i'la' kalimatullah), establishing the sovereignty of Allah (hakimiyyat-i-ilahiyyah), and conveying the truth and the call of humanity to the people. They are also reminded that the great reward with Allah, in this movement of jihad, is more precious than wealth and children.

The abandoning of the obligations placed upon the Ummah of Muslims on this earth, and withdrawing from them, is treachery against Allah and His Messenger. The foundation of Islam is the kalimah tayyibah (La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad Rasul Allah). That is, Allah alone, without partner, is the Sovereign. And this sovereignty is in the form presented by Hazrat Muhammad ﷺ. Throughout their entire history, human beings have never completely denied the existence of the Divine Being; rather, humans have repeatedly erred by associating other deities with Allah. Sometimes this association occurs on a limited scale in beliefs and worship, and sometimes on a very broad scale even in the supreme authority and right of sovereignty of Allah. And this second form is the form of great shirk. Therefore, for Islam, the issue has never been that people should acknowledge God and be invited to the belief that God exists; rather, the issue has always been that this God is one without partner, and that He be acknowledged in this status. The meaning of La ilaha illa Allah is that on this earth the right of sovereignty belongs to Him alone, and just as all people acknowledge that the Sovereign of this universe is Allah, so too they should acknowledge that on earth He is the Deity, and in the heavens as well: "Huwa alladhi fi as-sama' ilah wa fi al-ard ilah" — "He is the One who is God in the heavens and God on the earth." This is the real issue. Furthermore, since the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is also the bearer of the message of Allah, believing in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is also necessary.

This is the real issue of the religion of Islam, namely the beliefs that must take root in the heart and mind, and the practical struggle through which a practical system is established on this earth. Therefore, to withdraw from these aims is treachery. Allah the Exalted warns the believers here: you must never withdraw from these aims; this would be considered treachery. Therefore, the group that proclaims this ideology must fulfil its duty to strive for it, and endure the difficulties of jihad that arise on this path, whether it costs wealth or requires sacrificing children.

Likewise, Allah warns Muslims against betraying the trust which they have held since the time the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, because Islam is not merely a set of words that may be uttered in any language, nor merely a name for certain acts of worship and supplications, but a complete system of life that encompasses all of human life. Great difficulties arise in establishing it. Islam, in reality, means that a person should make his entire practical life rest upon the principles of the kalimah tayyibah, and that people should be returned to the servitude of Allah. Human society should be returned to the sovereignty of Allah and to His law and moral system. Those who transgress upon the right of Allah's sovereignty, who establish their own divinity, should be rejected, and in this system complete justice and equity should be enforced among people, and on this earth humanity, while discharging the trust of the Divine Vicegerency (khilafah ilahiyyah), should do all of this.

These are the obligations that are imposed upon every Muslim, and whoever does not fulfil them is, in effect, a betrayer. He is violating the covenant he made with Allah. He is breaking the allegiance (bay'ah) to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and is committing treachery against it.

And these obligations demand certain sacrifices. Their first demand is that a person should succeed in the trials and tests of wealth and children, and that his aim should be the pleasure of Allah and the reward of the Hereafter, which is a great reward, reserved for those who are trustworthy (amin), patient (sabirin), sacrificing, and who give precedence to the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 8, verse 28:

The Qur'an addresses the human reality, because the Creator of the universe knows humanity well. He knows its outward and inward capacities and its weaknesses. He is thoroughly acquainted with the ups and downs of this path.

He is also aware of the weak aspects of this creation, and He knows that the greed for wealth and the interests of children are deeply embedded in its nature. Therefore Allah warns the human being about the true reality of wealth and children. Allah has given these two beloved gifts to man as a test. They are the adornment of worldly life and they are a trial. Allah wants to see how the servant conducts himself with regard to wealth and children: whether he fulfils the right of the blessing by giving thanks, or whether he falls into heedlessness and disobedience. ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾. Trial does not come only in the form of hardship and deprivation; it also comes in the form of prosperity and the bounties of Allah, and trials also come in the form of wealth and children.

This is an extremely important warning. ﴿And know that your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾, and that ﴿with Allah is a great reward﴾. When a person comes to know in his heart what he is being tested with, this knowledge helps him, so that he remains alert and adopts a cautious attitude. Lest he err in the test and fall behind in it.

Yet even in this test Allah does not leave the servant without support. Allah knows that a person may fail the test despite the warnings, because the difficulties of this path are very great, especially when the matter concerns wealth and children. Therefore Allah shows man this light: the great reward of the Hereafter with Allah is precisely what stands against wealth and children.

﴿And that with Allah there is a great reward.﴾ It is Allah who gives wealth and riches, and the reward that is with Allah is more valuable than children and worldly wealth. Therefore no one should fall behind in discharging the rights of this greatest trust, and this is a kind of help from Allah to this weak human being. And Allah knows well that ﴿man was created weak﴾.

In short, the Islamic system is a complete code of life. It contains beliefs and concepts, it contains the means of guidance and training, and it contains obligations and duties. This is a system devised by Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware. ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware.﴾

Now the final call to the believers, at the end of this lesson, is this: they should adopt taqwa (God-consciousness and piety). This call is made because only those who have the light of taqwa can fulfill this great responsibility, and through it they can confront the satanic doubts and whisperings, and their feet remain firm on this path. Their attention and focus can be achieved only when they make use of the divine illumination and light obtained through taqwa.

This is the provision for the journey and the true equipment for travel. The provision of taqwa revives hearts, awakens them, and creates enthusiasm in them. Moreover, through it, caution and vigilance arise in hearts, and through it a person receives the light of insight, by which all the ups and downs of this path become illuminated. The thoughts of a person are not affected by those doubts and whisperings which make the path dark. Furthermore, through taqwa a person also receives forgiveness for his shortcomings, and seriousness and steadfastness come into his life. A person becomes hopeful and does not despair because of difficulties and failings.

The truth is that through taqwa there arises in a person's heart that clear insight by which he can make right decisions amid the difficulties of his path. But this is a reality which, like all spiritual experiences, is fully disclosed to a person only after he practically adopts it. Its true nature cannot be fully described through speech and explanation alone, especially to those who have no taste for it at all.

Some matters are intricate between what is good and what is action, and human thought and vision have always been prone to complexity in identifying the way of truth. On the important paths of life, a person can hardly distinguish truth from falsehood. Even great arguments often fail to give a person peace of heart. In the end, silence falls and hearts and minds are not satisfied. This debate and contention of proofs and arguments is fruitless, but in the end it is taqwa that comes to the fore. It is through taqwa that the intellect receives light. Taqwa itself determines the form and shape of truth, the path becomes unveiled, the heart becomes satisfied, the conscience finds rest, the feet become firm, and a person sets out upon the road.

The truth is that truth itself is not hidden from human nature; the foundation and structure of human nature is based upon truth, and the heavens and earth were created with this truth. But human desires come between truth and nature. Personal desires create pollution in the atmosphere, the true vision of a person does not function, and the path of truth does not appear to him. Personal desires cannot be rejected merely by argument and proof. It is taqwa and fear of God alone through which desires can be subdued. The fear of God and taqwa perform their function at the right time, both in secret and in open circumstances. This is why taqwa has been described as the source of the Criterion (furqan), by which insight is illuminated and every kind of confusion and doubt is removed.

This is a power and capacity which cannot be bought in the marketplace. It is only the great grace of Allah, which He bestows upon whom He wills, and as a result of this great grace sins are forgiven. And this is the general forgiveness which the Lord of the worlds grants, by His special generosity, to whomever He wills.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 30:

Lesson No. 84 At a Glance

In this surah the thread of discourse moves forward. Commentary on current events continues in the light of past events. By depicting this great victory before the Muslim ummah, it is shown: just consider how much your present state has changed compared with your past. What a great revolution has been brought about in the twinkling of an eye! But how did this happen...? Solely through the grace of the Lord and the planning of Allah. Look at this great revolution! In comparison with it, wealth and spoils are how insignificant. Moreover, the sacrifices you gave and the hardships you endured must seem very great to you, but now, compared with the results, how insignificant they are.

In the previous lesson it was explained how poor the condition of the Muslims was in Makkah, and that before this battle your position in Madinah was not good either. You were few and weak. You were surrounded by dangers at all times. There was the threat that you would be wiped off the face of the earth. In Madinah you became believers, and after this battle and this victory, by the planning of Allah alone, you became honoured and powerful.

In this lesson the stance of the polytheists is portrayed, and it is shown: look, these people were plotting against you. Shortly before the Hijrah, they used to claim that if we wished, we could compose speech like what this man recites of the signs of Allah. And in their malice and enmity they went so far as to confront the punishment of Allah themselves, saying that if the Islamic call is true, let a punishment descend upon us. After this it is said: look, these people are spending their precious wealth wastefully to block the path of the Islamic call, and are preparing for war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. But they will fail in this world, and in the Hereafter they will be fuel for Hell; moreover, they will suffer loss in both this world and the Hereafter.

Finally, Allah commands His Prophet to speak to the disbelievers and give them the choice of one of two matters. Either they should desist from disbelief, malice, and lining up against Allah and His Messenger; if they do so, Allah will forgive their former shortcomings committed in the age of ignorance. Or they should return to the state in which they were and suffer the evil end that befell everyone who adopted that path. Then the sunnah of Allah will take effect upon them, as He wills and as is pleasing to Him.

Finally, Allah guides the Muslims that they should continue fighting these disbelievers until there is no longer in the hands of the disbelievers any power that poses a danger to the Muslims. The divinity of Allah should be established in this world and religion should become purely for Allah. If they submit, the Prophet will accept this from them. As for their intention, the matter will rest with Allah, because Allah is All-Aware and All-Seeing. If they turn away, continue this war against Islam, and their malice and enmity towards Islam remains in this state, and they do not acknowledge the sole sovereignty of Allah and do not bow before the supreme authority of Allah, then the Muslims will continue jihad against them. In this, they will rely solely upon Allah, who is their Protector. He is an excellent Protector and the best Helper.

Lesson No. 84 Explanation of Verses: 30 to 40

Commentary on verse 30:

﴿وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ ۚ وَيَمْكُرُونَ وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ ۖ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ﴾

And remember the time when those who disbelieved were plotting against you, to imprison you, or kill you, or expel you. They were plotting, and Allah was plotting, and Allah is the best of plotters.

Now the circumstances of Makkah are brought onto the screen, at a time when the revolution that has now taken place had not yet occurred in the situation. The people of Makkah were firmly adhering to their position. The point is that the situation is moving in a very good direction and the future is bright, but in this you have no personal merit; this is the working of Allah's plan and decree. In the world only that happens which is the will of God. Those people who were being addressed at the beginning were well aware of both phases of the situation, because they had passed through them. For them the earlier period was recent past, and the fear and anguish they were afflicted with in that period was well remembered by them; the tranquillity of the present was before their eyes. They were seeing what deceptions had been devised against them and against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and are being devised, and how they had come through them successfully. They had not only been freed from difficulties but had also succeeded in them.

Their plan was to imprison the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in chains, until he died, or to kill him, or to expel him from Makkah. They had considered all these proposals, and in the end they reached the conclusion that they should kill him. This task would be carried out by young men from all the tribes, so that his blood would be divided among all the tribes, and the Banu Hashim would be unable to take revenge, and would eventually agree to blood-money.

Imam Ahmad has narrated, from Abdul Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Uthman al-Jazari, from a freed slave of Abbas, who said that Ibn Abbas said: the explanation of "and when those who disbelieved were plotting against you" is that one night the Quraysh consulted together in Makkah. Some said that when they came out in the morning they should bind him, that is, the Prophet ﷺ. Some said he should be killed, and some said he should be expelled. The Prophet ﷺ was informed of this. Ali slept that night on the Prophet's bed, and the Prophet went out and hid in the cave. But the polytheists kept watch over the Prophet's house during the night. When morning came, they attacked. When they saw that Ali was sleeping on the bed, and that Allah had turned their plan back upon them, they asked Ali, "Where is your companion?" Ali said, "I do not know." So they began to search for him and followed his footprints. When they reached the mountain, the traces of his feet became mixed up. They went up the mountain and reached above the cave. They saw that a spider had woven its web across the entrance. They said, "If he had entered here, there would not be a spider's web here." So the Prophet ﷺ spent three nights there.

﴿وَيَمْكُرُونَ وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ ۖ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ﴾: "They were plotting, and Allah was plotting, and Allah is the best of plotters." The words in which the Qur'an describes these circumstances are extremely impressive, through which the scene of the assembly of the Quraysh comes to mind; their schemes, proposals and plots come before the eye, but Allah encompasses them. In their case the plans of Allah come before us, and because of them all the plots of the polytheists are reduced to dust, yet they remain unaware of it until their last breath.

This is a deeply captivating depiction, and also a frightening one, since what can weak humans do against the Absolute Almighty? Allah is the Subduer, the Compeller, and encompasses everything. The Holy Qur'an expresses this reality in its own distinctive style, such that on reading it hearts tremble and the human consciousness is profoundly affected.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 31 (part 1 of 2):

From here on, in the context of the discourse, the deeds and conditions of the disbelievers are described. Their claims and their admissions are stated. Even their claim is recorded here, that if they wished they could produce this kind of speech, while in their own assumption this Qur'an is merely a book of ancient tales.

Allamah Ibn Kathir, in his tafsir (exegesis), has related from Sa'id, al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj and others that the one who made this statement was al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. "This accursed man had travelled through the lands of Persia. He had memorised the history of the kings of Persia and the tales of Rustam and Isfandiyar. When he returned from Persia, the Prophet ﷺ had already been sent, and he was reciting the Qur'an before the people. Whenever the Prophet ﷺ rose from a gathering after preaching, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith would arrive there and narrate these tales to the people, and he would say: 'Swear by God, tell me, who among us is the better storyteller? I or Muhammad?' When the Battle of Badr took place, God caught him. The Prophet ﷺ ordered that his neck be struck off in his presence, and so it was. He had been taken prisoner by al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad." Concerning this, Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] narrates from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that on the day of Badr the Prophet ﷺ ordered the necks of 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, Tu'aymah ibn 'Adi and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith to be struck off. Al-Miqdad had taken al-Nadr prisoner. When the Prophet ﷺ issued the order for his execution, Hadrat al-Miqdad said: "O Messenger of God, he is my prisoner." Upon this the Prophet ordered his execution. Then Hadrat al-Miqdad again said: "O Messenger, he is my prisoner." The Prophet ﷺ then said: "O God, make al-Miqdad independent through Your bounty." Upon this Hadrat al-Miqdad said: "This is exactly what I wanted."

It is said that this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but the tales of the ancients."﴾

The Qur'an has repeatedly mentioned the claim of the polytheists that there are tales of the ancients in the Qur'an: ﴿They say, "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ This is among the obstacles they placed against the revolutionary teachings of the Qur'an, although the Qur'an's address was to human nature, and these words had such an effect upon human nature that it would sway and respond. When these words fell upon hearts, they would tremble and be unable to stand against them. Therefore the leaders of Quraysh used these kinds of stratagems against this speech. Yet they themselves knew that these schemes would not be effective. Nevertheless they found something in the words of God that resembled their ancient tales. Taking advantage of this, they tried to mislead the ignorant Arabs, so that they would not be influenced by this revolutionary movement, and so that the common people would continue, as before, in servitude to those great ones (kubara').

The leaders of Quraysh also knew the reality of the Islamic call. They were Arabs and were well acquainted with the themes of the Qur'an. They also knew what the meaning and substance of the sacred formula (kalima tayyiba) "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God" is. Its purpose is that the one who bears witness rejects the sovereignty and dominion of all human beings. He removes himself from the dominion of all people and declares that from today he has entered only into the servitude and dominion of God. Then he also declares that from today he has entered not only into the servitude and dominion of God. Then he also declares that from today he has entered only into the servitude and dominion of God. Then he also declares that after this he will take every kind of guidance from the Messenger of God ﷺ. Now he will not take guidance from those who speak in the name of idols. They also knew that those who bear this testimony, the moment they recite the kalima, are freed from the slavery of Quraysh, from their influence and from their authority. They become cogs in the collective system whose leadership is in the hand of Hadrat Muhammad ﷺ. They become subject and obedient to the leadership and lordship of the Prophet. Whatever tribe they belong to, their ties of lineage and social life with that tribe come to an end, and they become loyal and responsible to the new leadership, which is called the leadership of Muhammad.

This was the meaning of the kalima tayyiba, "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God." They had seen this meaning walking through the streets of Makkah. Day and night they felt threatened by this meaning. Their collective order, their tribal existence and their leadership and lordship appeared to them to be coming to an end.

The weak, purposeless and ineffective meaning of "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God," which we understand from this formula today, was never the true meaning. We claim that we are Muslims merely because we utter the words of the testimony of faith with our tongues and also perform some acts of worship, while on earth sovereignty belongs to others and there is no trace of the Islamic system in people's lives. Over Islamic society, jahili leaderships (jahiliyyah: the state of ignorance before Islam) and the followers of jahiliyyah are the rulers and heads, and they carry out all affairs according to their own will.

The truth is that in Makkah there was neither an Islamic government nor was the Shariah enforced there. But those who professed the kalima tayyiba surrendered their entire leadership and authority into the hands of the Prophet ﷺ, and their loyalties were cut off from their own society and became attached to the Muslim community (jama'ah muslimah). These people not only threw off the yoke of jahili leadership from their necks, but they also rebelled against jahili values. They immediately cut themselves off from their tribe, their family and jahili leadership the moment they recited the testimony of faith. Therefore the kalima tayyiba, from these people, was not merely an empty statement. It was a meaning, and that meaning appeared in the lives of the Muslim community.

This was the real matter that frightened Quraysh. They saw that Islam was surging forward like a flood. Before this there had also been a group of hunafa' (monotheists who rejected idolatry before Islam), who kept away from the beliefs and practices of the polytheists and did not worship as they did. They regarded God as one without partner, worshipped only God, and none of them worshipped idols. As far as this goes, whatever attitude a person adopts, no jahili system would trouble him, because such an attitude posed no threat to the system of the people of jahiliyyah. These were merely dissenting beliefs and a separate manner of worship. But this alone is not Islam, as some pure and well-meaning people think, and they wish to believe that they have become good Muslims. The truth is that these are simple-hearted people, and they do not even know what the reality of Islam is. Islam is not merely the correct recitation of the kalima. Along with it, it is also the name of a movement, and the movement is that a person immediately comes out from the grip of jahili concepts, jahili society and jahili leadership, and, leaving the laws and Shariah of jahili leadership, attaches his entire loyalty to Islamic leadership, which wishes to enforce Islam in practice upon some part of the earth.

This was the very matter because of which the sleep of the great ones (kubara') of Quraysh was forbidden, and they were tossing and turning like on thorns. They rose up with all kinds of tricks against the Islamic movement. One of these tricks was to spread doubts about the Qur'an, that these are merely ancient tales, and that if they wished they could compose such tales. But before this, the Qur'an had challenged them repeatedly, and they had been unable to produce any such speech. The word asatir (tales) is the plural of usturah (myth). By it is meant those narratives which contain mythological nonsense, that is, tales of gods, stories of ancient peoples, the heroic deeds of religious leaders, and extraordinary events that are composed of imagination, where imagination is the fundamental element of those tales.

Quraysh, by pointing out the stories of earlier nations mentioned in the Qur'an, would take from them the miracles and the events of how God dealt with those who denied in earlier times, and they would tell the heedless and ignorant people of Makkah: "Read for yourselves, these are ancient tales. Muhammad has taken these stories from people who are outside this field. From the Mahayrin (?) he comes and recites them to you here." And he believes that these are revealed to him. Thus al-Nadr ibn al-Harith himself would sit in the gathering of the Messenger of God and say these things, or he would set up his own gathering opposite the gathering of the Prophet ﷺ and say such things in it. In it he would narrate the old historical tales of the Persians, and then he would tell the people: "Look, these are also the same kind of stories as the Qur'an narrates. See, on the strength of such stories he claims to be a prophet, and I do not make such a claim, but both of these are just ancient tales."

This was the speech of that accursed man. It is necessary that in the circles of Makkah, especially in the early period, it must have had some effects. In that early period, in which the distinction between the stories of the Qur'an and the old tales of the Persians was not yet clear in people's minds. For this reason, the Prophet's herald had proclaimed shortly before the battle of Badr that al-Nadr ibn al-Harith must not escape, and that he must be killed. And when he was brought as a captive, the Prophet ordered him to be killed, and did not accept ransom from him as he had accepted it from the other prisoners.

But after the initial assault, all these schemes in Makkah became ineffective, and this internal opposition soon came to an end, and the truth of it became clear to the people. The overpowering force of the Qur'an, which God has given to it, and the power that is hidden within the truth it presents, take possession of human nature. Thus against it such stratagems soon failed, and soon the field was clear of them. Now Quraysh, in a state of bewilderment and distress, were compelled to change their policy. Earlier they used to invite people to a contest of eloquence. Now they began to say: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during its recitation, that perhaps you may prevail.﴾ But even the most prominent among them, such as Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, could not comply with this order. They would go secretly at night and listen to the recitation of the Qur'an. They could not be patient until the appointed time of the Qur'an's recitation at night, and they would reach there secretly, away from others. But when their secret was revealed to one another, they took a very strict oath that they would never come again, lest they fall victim to the Qur'an.

It should be remembered that the movement of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith against the Qur'an has not ended, nor will it end, and it was not the last movement. This movement too has always existed in human history in various forms. The enemies of the religion of Islam have always striven to keep the people of Islam away from the Qur'an. When they could not destroy the Qur'an by other means, they began to sing it. Qurra' (reciters) recite it with a beautiful voice, and these people sway to it. They also began to make amulets and charms from its commands and verses. Some tied them on their arms, some hung them around their necks, and some placed them under their pillows. And they thought that they were Muslims, that they had fulfilled the right of the Qur'an, and that in this way the right of this religion had been fulfilled.

Today the situation is that the Qur'an is no longer the source of guidance and right direction for people's lives. The enemies of the religion have set up other sources and references in place of the Qur'an, from which people take guidance. These people take their concepts and aims from these new references, and they also take laws and regulations from these other sources. They take the values of life and the standards of good and evil from these sources as well, but with their tongues they say that the religion of Islam is respected, the Qur'an is preserved, and it is recited to people morning and evening. Singers sing it, reciters recite it. After this melody and this chanting, what else do people want? As for concepts and subject matter, the standards of good and evil and the values of life, the organisation of society and social customs, laws and regulations and principles and constitutions, the Muslims have fabricated another Qur'an in regard to these matters, and these people never return to the real Qur'an.

Is there a difference between this stratagem and the stratagems of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith? Yes, modern stratagems are in a modern style. They are more complex and more hidden than those, and these modern schemes are more successful in the complexity of modern life. But the truth is that these are the same kind of conspiracies as those Quraysh used, or those that occurred throughout the long history of Islam.

But what can be said of the Qur'an? It is a remarkable book. In its long history, these games and intricate conspiracies against it have continued, but in the end the victory is always the Qur'an's. Remember, the Holy Qur'an has extraordinary characteristics, and its grip upon human nature is very strong. No plot of the Jews, the Hindus, humans or devils succeeds against it. Today the global conspiracies being carried out against it, whose thread lies in the hands of global Judaism and global Zionism, are continuing and spreading, and the Qur'an remains dominant and victorious.

This Qur'an today, too, is defeating its enemies over the whole face of the earth. These enemies are compelled to broadcast its recitation throughout the world. Europe, America and the Hindus and others broadcast it through their media, and the rulers who are agents of the Jews and Christians also make it part of their broadcasts, those agents who also claim to be Muslims.

Truly, these people do make the Qur'an part of their broadcasts, but they have reduced the Qur'an merely to a means of recitation, melody and measured chanting, or beyond that they use it for the purposes of amulets and charms. They have removed the Qur'an from the Muslim mind and displaced it from its place of guidance for Muslims in thought and in practice. For the guidance of Muslims in thought and practice, these enemies have fabricated modern philosophies and ideologies, yet this Book continues to confront all conspiracies. It continues to do its work, and in every part of this world there are groups who are striving to give it its rightful place. They are striving so that this Book becomes the reference point of guidance and right direction. These groups are active everywhere, seeking and hoping for the support and help of Allah, that Allah may grant them dominion over this earth and that the Qur'an may attain its true station. If it has succeeded once before, then, God willing, it will certainly succeed again. Insha'Allah. Insha'Allah.

Let us look further. When these enemies are unable to withstand the Qur'an and their conspiracy fails, they adopt a strange attitude towards it. Their spirit of hostility and their arrogance compel them to adopt this attitude and not to accept it under any circumstances. Now these people enter the world of wishful thinking, saying: "If this is the truth, O Allah, then rain down stones upon us, or send some other painful punishment upon us." Yet they are by no means prepared to follow the truth or to support it.

This is a strange and bizarre supplication. It shows the extent of the intense hatred and enmity that existed in these people's hearts against Islam, such that they invite destruction and ruin, yet are not prepared to accept Islam and support it, even though it is the truth. The natural attitude of a sound disposition is that when it is troubled by some matter, such a person prays: "O Allah, show me the right path in this matter." He never feels bitterness regarding that matter. But when pride, arrogance, and hostility corrupt the sound disposition, then the situation becomes that arrogance and enmity incite a person to evil. People prefer to die, but they do not prefer to accept the truth, even though truth and falsehood become clear before them, and they themselves are left with no doubt about it. The clear example of this is the attitude of the polytheists of Makkah. They continued to oppose the call of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until their last breath, but despite their hostility, this call achieved victory.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 33:

In response to this obstinacy and this supplication, what does the Qur'an say? It is true that these people deserve a rain of stones, and they demand it on the condition that, "if this Qur'an is true." And it is evident that the Qur'an is true, and the condition is fulfilled. But despite their calling for destruction, Allah does not send this general punishment upon them because the Beloved of God (ﷺ) is present among them and is continually inviting them to the truth. And Allah has never completely destroyed any people while a Messenger is present among them, calling them. Nor does Allah destroy people as long as they keep seeking forgiveness for their sins. And this punishment is not being sent upon them merely because these people are the inhabitants of the House of Allah, although they are not deserving of the guardianship of that House.

This is a great mercy of Allah that He has granted them respite, and because of their deep obstinacy the punishment is not descending upon them. These people prevent others from the Masjid al-Haram, and yet the rope of respite for them is being extended. In that period they also used to prevent Muslims from performing Hajj, while the Muslims neither prevented anyone nor interfered with anyone.

This mercy of Allah was granting them respite so that perhaps those among them in whose hearts the seed of faith exists would believe, even if they come later. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is still present and carrying out his work. Some people still had expectations from them. Therefore, because of the blessed presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), they were being granted respite. The door to escaping the great punishment was still open, if they would accept, embrace the Islamic call, and refrain from their conduct.

﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them. And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness.﴾ At that time Allah was not going to send punishment upon them while you were present among them, and it is not the way of Allah that He would punish people while they are seeking forgiveness.

﴿But if Allah wished to deal with them according to their circumstances, then indeed they deserve the punishment of Allah.﴾

Their punishment is not being delayed for this reason: that they claimed to be descendants of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him), or that they are the custodians of the House of Allah. This was merely a claim upon claim; it had no foundation. In reality, these people were not servants and custodians of this House at all. They were its enemies. They had seized it by force. It was not an inheritance that they had received from their forefathers. The right to custodianship of the House of Allah belongs to the God-fearing servants of Allah. Their claim that they are the heirs of Prophet Ibrahim is also incorrect, because truthfulness is not connected with blood and lineage. In truth, the inheritance is the inheritance of religion and belief.

"For on this path, so-and-so the son of so-and-so has no standing" (a line of Persian verse).

The true heirs of Prophet Ibrahim are the people of taqwa (God-consciousness). Prophet Ibrahim built this House so that people might visit it, and you prevent them from it, and you have also snatched its custodianship away from those who deserve it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 35:

These people, although they perform their prayer at this House, are not entitled to its custodianship. So what is their prayer? Whistling and clapping of hands. Such noise and uproar, in which there is neither gravity nor seriousness, nor any awareness of the sanctity of this House, nor any sense of the holiness and greatness of Allah.

It is related from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that these people used to place their cheeks on the ground and would whistle and clap. And this brings to mind the picture of the so-called Muslim world, in which people sing and play music at shrines, make uproar, chant "Allah Hu" slogans, and rub their faces on the thresholds of graves. In short, all these are manifestations of jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance before Islam), which at one time appeared in one form and at another time appears in another form. But the root and fundamental form of all these forms is that the sovereignty of humans be established in the world, and that humans rule over people. This is a great and all-encompassing jahiliyyah, which encircles all jahiliyyahs, large and small, and these other jahiliyyahs are its branches and frames.

﴿So taste the punishment, because of your disbelief that you used to commit.﴾

And what punishment is this? It is the same punishment that reached them at the hands of the Muslim community at the Battle of Badr, the punishment they themselves had sought, namely that their roots be cut off. Allah did not send that punishment upon them at this point because Allah is Most Merciful and Most Generous, and because, in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), the descent of this kind of punishment was not appropriate, for he is the Prophet of mercy, and there remained hope that some of the disbelievers would repent and seek forgiveness.

Now look at the conduct of these disbelievers: they spend their wealth for the purpose of barring people from the path of Allah. What were their aims at Badr? Simply this: their sole intention from that battle was to destroy this group and uproot the movement of religious devotion, as had been attempted before. After Badr too, their thinking remained the same. Allah warns them that in the end you will surely fail, and you will be deeply regretful of your conduct, because in this world you will be struck by defeat, and in the Hereafter there will be a painful punishment for you.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from al-Zuhri and others. They said: When the Quraysh suffered defeat at Badr and their defeated army reached Makkah, and Abu Sufyan arrived there with the caravan, Abdullah ibn Rabi'ah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Safwan ibn Umayyah, along with some other people, went to the houses of those whose fathers, children, and brothers had been killed in that battle. They spoke with Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and all those whose wealth was in that caravan. They said: "O people of Quraysh, Muhammad has taken full revenge upon you and has exceeded the limits, and has killed your best men. So give the wealth of the trade caravan as a contribution, so that we may take revenge for Badr." They accepted this proposal. Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه) said that this verse was revealed concerning these people.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth...﴾ Whether this happened at Badr or after Badr, it is a common tactic of the enemies of the religion. These people spend their wealth and their strength for the uprooting of the religion. They bar people from the way of Allah. They place obstacles in the path of the religion, and these people have continued waging war against Islam everywhere and in every age.

This battle has not ended. The enemies of the religion have never sat at ease at any moment, and they have never allowed the supporters of the religion to sit at ease even for a single moment. This is because the only path for this religion is that it remain active and assault the jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance). It is the very attribute and aim of the people of the religion that they remain active at all times and break the backbone of the people of jahiliyyah. They should raise the banner of Allah so high and dominant that no enemy of the religion would dare to look towards it.

Allah warns those who spend their wealth in barring the way of the religion: their action will be a cause of astonishment for them. All these expenditures will soon come to nothing, and the people of truth will be victorious and triumphant in this very world. And in the Hereafter, these people will be heading toward Hell, and that will be a great astonishment for them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 8, verse 37:

How this process will operate: this wealth that is being spent gathers together the forces of falsehood and incites them to aggression against the truth. And the truth confronts it, and the field of striving and struggle becomes hot. The truth advances in the form of a movement and smashes the head of falsehood. Through this conflict and this bitter process alone, the distinction between truth and falsehood becomes clear. The People of Truth and the People of Falsehood become distinguished. Even among those who stand in the ranks of Islam, the weak ones fall away, and only those remain who are steadfast, patient, brave, and deserving of Allah's help. This is because only such people are fit to bear this great trust. They do not turn away from their position because of any trial or any difficulty. Through this same process, heaps of wickedness can be gathered together and cast into Hell, and this very course becomes the cause of the loss of the People of Falsehood.

Here the Qur'an has presented wickedness in a personified form, as though heaps of it have been piled up, and it can be eliminated only by taking it into Hell. There is no other way of eliminating it apart from this.

﴿فَيَرْكُمَهٗ جَمِيْعًا فَيَجْعَلَهٗ فِيْ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ "So that He may pile it up all together and place it in Hell." And He gathers every kind of filth together and piles it up. Then He casts that heap into Hell. The benefit of presenting a concept in such a concrete form is that it becomes a part of feeling and consciousness. This is a unique style of the Qur'an.

Now the discussion reaches its decisive point: the end of the disbelievers is settled, and the method for clearing away this heap of filth is laid down. The address now turns to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he should give the disbelievers a final warning, and the believers too are commanded to hold firmly to the path and method that has been prescribed for them. Jihad and qital (fighting) are the only way of Islam. And this will continue until every kind of fitnah (strife) and corruption is removed from this earth, until the pure religion (din) prevails, and until the Islamic movement becomes content and secure. Only in that case will Allah be the supporter and helper of the movement, and no one among the people will be able to harm the movement, whether by war or by conspiracy.

Therefore, you still have the opportunity to save yourselves from that evil end, not to gather together against Islam, and not to throw your wealth and trade into it. The door of repentance is still open before you. Return to the way of Allah. Allah will forgive all your shortcomings. And if, after this warning, these people again adopt the same attitude, then the Sunnah of Allah will certainly take its course. Their end will be the same as that of those who have walked this path since ancient times, and its essence is that the friends of Allah are granted dominance and supreme authority, both in this world and in the Hereafter. Now, O disbelievers, you stand at a decisive crossroads. This is the moment of decision.

Now (in the next verse), having ended the direct address to the disbelievers, the believers are told the method of the Islamic revolution.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verses 39–40:

Commentary on verses 39–40: These are the limits and conditions of Islamic jihad (the struggle in the path of God). They apply everywhere and in every age. These rulings were not confined to the time of the Prophet (ﷺ). The rulings on jihad that come in this surah have not come in their final form. The law of war in Islam was completed in Surah al-Tawbah, which was revealed in 9 AH. As we said at the beginning of this surah, Islam is a positive movement, and toward the whole of humanity it adopts those means which suit the circumstances of the time. This movement is a gradual movement, and each stage has its own specific rulings and clear objectives and requirements.

Despite all these considerations, it is decisive that this command: ﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for Allah﴾ ("Fight against these disbelievers until fitnah no longer remains and the religion becomes entirely for Allah") is a permanent command for the Islamic movement and a standing policy against jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance).

At the beginning of this surah, in its introduction, we said that Islam came into the world precisely to free human beings from the servitude of their fellow humans, and so that no one serves his fellow servants, and likewise that no person serves his own carnal desires. This aim can be achieved only when the sovereignty and supreme authority of Allah alone is established on this earth, and Allah alone is the sovereign and Lord of all humanity on it. This proclamation is in fact a declaration of rebellion against all the prevailing sovereignties and authorities of humankind, and a practical war against all those forms in which one human being rules over another in any shape. (For details, see the pages of this part ...)

Therefore, two things are necessary to attain this great objective. First, the people who believe in this religion must be secure and protected from fitnah and corruption. They must be in a position to declare their liberation from servitude to their fellow humans and to declare the servitude of Allah alone. No human being should have supreme authority over them. This is not possible unless there exists a group that has its own leadership, and which is practically implementing this ideology on some land, and which is practically arrayed against every tyrant (taghut) in that land. And it must not fail to suppress those forces which prevent such a community from living according to the religion of Islam, or which inflict oppression upon such people.

The second condition is that no power should exist in the world, and if it does, it must be crushed, which stands as an obstacle in the path of the primary objective. That is, all those powers which obstruct the establishment of divine government (hukumat-e-ilahiyyah) on this earth must be eliminated. In short, the supreme sovereignty of God must be fully established on this earth.

Here it is necessary to answer an important question. The Qur'an contains the command of Allah: ﴿There is no compulsion in religion. Right has become clearly distinct from error.﴾

Despite the fact that we have discussed the Islamic theory of jihad, and especially after the lengthy excerpt we gave from the book al-Jihad fi al-Islam by the respected Ustadh Maulana Sayyid Abul A'la Maududi, no further detail on this subject is needed. However, here we wish to provide a somewhat further clarification of this matter, because on this point the cunning enemies of Islam spread doubts through propaganda from every direction.

What this verse states is: "the religion becomes entirely Allah's." This means that there should be no material obstacles in the face of the religion which create hindrances in its path. And these material obstacles are in fact in the form of systems which are tyrannical systems (taghuti nizam), and whose conditions are such that human beings are bound in the shackles of oppression. Therefore the demand of this verse is that there should be no system in the world in which the supreme authority of anyone other than Allah is enforced, nor any system in which people are obedient to anyone other than Allah. When all such obstacles are removed from the path of humankind, then human beings will be free. There will be no barrier to their adopting any belief. That is, there will no longer be a situation in which a doctrine opposed to the Islamic worldview is backed by material power that influences the common people, and in which those who wish to accept the Islamic worldview cannot do so for fear. Those who have already adopted it will have no fear of any fitnah or corruption. In this way, humankind will be practically free from all tyrannical fitnahs, because people will be free in adopting belief and ideology, and there will be no authority over them other than the supreme sovereignty of the Lord of the worlds.

Let it be remembered that humanity cannot attain the station of dignity and honour as long as it is not free from any authority other than that of Allah. Only in this way can this goal be achieved: that religion belongs solely to Allah, and that there be no fitnah for Muslims.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 41 (part 1 of 4):

Para Number 10 at a Glance

This para contains the remaining part of Surah al-Anfal, the initial portion of which passed in the ninth para. Its remaining portion comprises most of Surah al-Tawbah. Here we will introduce the section of Surah al-Anfal under discussion, and the introduction to Surah al-Tawbah will come at its beginning, as is customary, God willing.

At the end of the ninth para, in the introduction to Surah al-Anfal, we clarified the important outlines of this surah's themes. The features of the section under discussion in this surah are the same as those of its first section. However, since the topics of discussion are different, no repetition is felt in them. The arrangement of the topics is such that it appears that its first section was its first phase and this section is the second phase, because there is a great degree of harmony among its subjects and themes.

The first section began with people asking questions about the spoils (al-anfal), and a dispute among the Muslims concerning them was mentioned, and as a result, the ownership and authority over the spoils, and their distribution, was returned to the Messenger of Allah. People were told to fear God, and it was explained what true faith is, and they were invited to rise to the level of that true faith. After that, they were told that all the events of Badr were a manifestation of God's providence and planning; the whole scheme was God's, and all the help was from God. The entire battle was made to occur so that God's will might become manifest; as far as the people were concerned, they were merely instruments, and the instruments of God's decree. After the reality of that battle was revealed, they were called upon to show steadfastness at the time of war, and were assured that God would help and support them and would punish their enemies for their evil deeds. After that, they were warned against betraying God and the Messenger of Allah. They were cautioned about the trial of wealth and the trial of children, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to inform the disbelievers of the end they were about to meet. And if they repent and outwardly accept the call, their acknowledgment should be accepted and their inner state left to God; and if they do not accept, then they should be fought until the world is purified of tumult and the system of life is entirely Islamic.

This was the summary of the first section. Now observe that in this second section too, the discussion begins with the spoils, and then they are invited to faith in God, and to faith in the Book that was revealed on the day the two hosts met. After that it is explained that the circumstances in which these spoils came into your hands were planned by God's providence, and some other aspects of the positions and observations of that battle are presented, through which the active working of that providence and planning becomes clear, and it is also made known that the believers were in reality the veil of the hand of power and acted as instruments. After that they are called upon: when you have to confront the disbelievers, show steadfastness on the battlefield, for you already know the reality of events; remember God constantly, obey God and His Messenger, and avoid all kinds of disputes, for in case of disputes your strength will dissipate and you will become weak. Then they are instructed in patience, and it is explained that in jihad they should avoid pride, arrogance and self-display. They are told not to adopt the attitude of those who went out from their homes in conceit, displaying their power, while the purpose of their act was to bar people from the path of God. And these people were trapped in the snare of Satan's cunning. Then they are invited to rely solely on God, who is All-Powerful, All-Wise and the Disposer, and by whose command all affairs are accomplished. After that they are told that they (the disbelievers) are disbelievers, and how He seizes the deniers, and that this seizure is because of their deeds. In the first section it was mentioned how the angels descended on the battlefield and how they were striking off the necks of the disbelievers and striking them from front and back; in this second section it is said that when the angels take the souls of the disbelievers, they beat them severely; and in the first section it was said that they are evil beasts, and similarly in this section it is explained that these people do not keep their covenants, and at this point their bestial nature is mentioned. In this section, certain injunctions regarding international law are given to the Prophet (ﷺ). Some of these laws are definitive and some are provisional, and some of their details will come later in Surah al-Tawbah.

Up to this point, this second section parallels the first. Even the arrangement of topics and events is identical. Yes, on some topics the discussion is brief in one place and detailed in another. For example, certain rulings and dealings concerning the Islamic camp and non-Islamic camps have been presented in detail.

At the end of the surah, various miscellaneous topics and rulings have also been given, which are the completion of the discussion of the themes that have come in these two sections. For example, God makes clear to the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers this favour of His, that He has joined their hearts together, although by nature these people were rebellious, and without the grace and kindness of God, producing this harmony of hearts among them would have been a difficult task.

God also assures the believers that He is sufficient for them, and that He is their supporter and helper. Therefore, through the Messenger of Allah, they are commanded to urge the believers to fight. And they are assured that, because of their faith, they will prevail over disbelievers many times their number. This is because disbelievers are an unintelligent people, and they are unintelligent because they do not believe, and understanding cannot come without faith, provided that you are patient, and God is indeed with those who are patient.

After this come the matters and rulings concerning the ransom of prisoners. It is said: O Prophet, you have not yet trampled the disbelievers or broken their power and might, yet you have accepted ransom; this is not a good thing you have done, for your power and dominion are not yet firmly established. Therefore it is explained here that different methods are adopted in different circumstances, and so flexibility has been built into the policy of the Islamic movement, so that different policies may be adopted in different situations. It is also explained here how they should treat prisoners, how they should incline them towards faith, and adorn faith in their hearts. If these prisoners again betray, then just as God first defeated them, so He will again defeat them, and they will be humiliated before the Messenger of Allah.

Finally, there are mentioned the principles upon which the members of the Muslim community are to maintain their mutual relations, as well as the dealings with those who have not come to the Abode of Islam but accept Islam. Then come the rulings on relations with disbelievers. From all these rulings it becomes clear what the social system of Islam is like and what the policy of the Islamic system is. These rulings show that the Islamic society and the Islamic system are a dynamic system, and it is a fundamental principle of the Islamic system that it remains dynamic, and through this movement its internal and external rulings will continue to be formulated. Therefore, in the Islamic system, Islamic ideas cannot be separated from activism and practical existence. The Islamic society must have a practical existence in every age and under every kind of circumstance.

For this brief preface, this much commentary suffices; so now let us take up the details of the verses.

Lesson No. 85 at a Glance

Between the beginning of this lesson and the end of the previous lesson, the flow of speech is continuous and connected. At the end of the ninth para, the command to fight was given, and in this lesson the explanation of the rulings of fighting continues. The conclusion of speech at the end of the previous para was this:

Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven them; but if they return [to it], then the way of the former peoples has already gone before. And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is entirely for God. And if they cease, then indeed God is Seeing of what they do. But if they turn away, then know that God is your Protector; an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper.

O Prophet, say to these disbelievers that if they still desist, what has already happened will be overlooked; but if they return to their former conduct, then what has happened to the earlier peoples is known to all. O you who believe, fight these disbelievers until fitnah no longer remains and religion is entirely for God. Then if they stop from fitnah, God is the observer of their deeds. And if they refuse, know that God is your Protector, and He is the best Protector and the best Helper.

Despite the fact that by this clear text the objectives of jihad were fixed, that this jihad and fighting is for God, that it is for the objectives of the Islamic call, and for the establishment of the Islamic system of life; and despite the fact that at the very beginning of the surah a firm decision was given that the spoils belong to God and the Messenger of Allah, and the mujahideen were cleansed of any interest in them so that a sincere intention would arise in them and all their movements and rests would be for God, still, despite all these matters, the Islamic system of life also gives organized and realistic rulings concerning these properties, because the spoils exist and the deserving mujahideen exist, and these mujahideen are expending their wealth and their lives in the path of God. They take part in jihad voluntarily and bear their own expenses, and they also bear the expenses of those among the other volunteer mujahideen who are needy. Then these people take possession of the spoils in that battle, and through their patience, steadfastness, striving and jihad they obtain these properties; and God has also purified their hearts from every kind of greed and covetousness regarding these spoils, by transferring their ownership to God and the Messenger of Allah. Therefore, now there is no harm in giving a share of these properties to such people, provided they understand that it is a pure gift from God and the Messenger of Allah, and that it is being given only so that their genuine needs may be met, so that the satisfaction of their human feelings may be achieved, and there may be no individual or collective snatching and grabbing from it, and no dispute, since at the beginning of the surah it was commanded that the real owners are God and the Messenger of Allah.

This is the Islamic system of life, and it knows human nature well. Therefore it deals with it in this balanced and comprehensive manner. Through it the satisfaction of human feelings is achieved, and their genuine requirements are also fulfilled; and along with this, the hearts of the members of society remain clear towards one another. The demands of collective justice are also met, and the spoils do not become a source of evil, but rather a source of mercy.

Lesson No. 85: Explanation of Verses 41 to 54.

Commentary of Verse No. 41:

And know that whatever you obtain as spoils of war, a fifth of it belongs to God and to the Messenger, and to the near of kin, the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer, if you have believed in God and in what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met. And God is over all things Competent.

The narrations concerning this verse contain lengthy juristic disagreements. The first disagreement concerns the meaning and implication of "ghanaim" (spoils). Then concerning the meaning of "anfal", whether they are two names for one thing or two different things. Second, concerning the fifth after the division of four parts among the mujahideen, there are also disagreements about how this fifth is to be distributed. Third, concerning the fifth of the fifth that belongs to God, whether it is a separate share or the same as what belongs to the Messenger of Allah. Fourth, whether the share of the Messenger of Allah was exclusively for his person, or whether after him other imams also have this right. Fifth, whether the share of the near of kin still remains for the near of kin of the Messenger of Allah, that is, for the Banu Hashim and the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, as it was in his time, or whether this has ended; and whether its disposal also rests with the Messenger of Allah and, after him, with the caliphs. And there are other similar subsidiary disagreements.

In Fi Zilal al-Quran, we have adopted the method of not entering into these minor jurisprudential (fiqh) disputes, because the appropriate place for such disagreements is the books written specifically on those subjects. That is the general point. But regarding the spoils of war in particular, the present situation is that there is no real or practical question before us that requires resolution. There is no practical issue, no Islamic state, and no community currently engaged in jihad in the way of Allah that has acquired spoils of war and needs to know how to distribute them.

Time has turned back such that the condition of this religion has become exactly what it was on the first day it was revealed to the world.
