At that time, people had completely returned to jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). They were associating many lords with Allah, and these lords were giving people their legal systems. The condition of this religion has become just like its initial circumstances, and our duty is that people enter it afresh. They should once again recite the testimony of faith, *La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammadun Rasul Allah* (there is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah). They should regard Allah as the One without partner and the sole absolute sovereign. They should seek guidance only from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and live in the form of a community whose aim is that this religion be re-established. All such people should be fully loyal to this new community and its leadership, and they should not give such loyalty and obedience to any jahili leadership or authority.

This is a real and living issue confronting this religion. Initially, the religion faces no other issue apart from this one. There is no question here of the spoils of war, because at present no jihad is taking place anywhere. Indeed, nowhere is Islam facing any administrative problem, neither in internal relations nor in external ones. The reason for this is very simple and easy to understand: there is no Islamic society anywhere in the world with a stable existence that would require rules and guidance for its internal relations or for its relations with other societies.

The Islamic way of life is a practical system. The Islamic system does not discuss issues and matters that do not exist in practice. Therefore, it does not deal with issues that are not practically present. It is such a realistic and practical system that it avoids this kind of fruitless debate. Engaging in purely imaginary talk is not the method of this system. This is the work of idle people who have spare time and no practical task before them, and who spend their free hours on purely theoretical and conceptual discussions. The duty of such people, concerning subjects that have no practical existence in this world, is to direct their efforts and their strength toward establishing the Islamic way of life and to bring into existence an actual Islamic society. And they should carry out this task in accordance with the method for establishing the Islamic system. That is, first of all, they should call people to the testimony of faith. People should announce their re-entry into the religion of Islam, just as this work first began in Makkah. A movement arose, it had its own leadership, and this community emerged, cut off from the jahili society surrounding it. Then a struggle took place between it and that jahili society, after which Allah granted truth victory and an Islamic state was established. Only then will people need the rules concerning ghanaim (spoils) and anfal (bounties), when those matters actually confront them, so that disputes among people may be settled according to Islamic law. And when the Islamic state is established, rulings will arise for its relations with other states. Now, in the modern age, if some problems have arisen, the mujtahidin (qualified jurists exercising ijtihad, independent reasoning) of the time will seek solutions for them, whether these problems are internal or external. Only then will ijtihad have any value, because it will be a realistic and genuine ijtihad.

Since we have fully understood this practical aspect of the Islamic way of life, we do not enter here into the fiqh disagreements about spoils and bounties that are found in the books of jurisprudence. A time will certainly come when research on these matters will be undertaken. An Islamic society will exist, it will practically act upon jihad, and in it the rules of spoils and bounties will come before us. We should, while observing the historical process of the Islamic movement, adopt the principles of faith and keep before us the method of training of Islam. This is a permanent feature of this Book, which is not affected by the passage of time. As for other methods and issues, they are explanations of it. The general ruling that is understood from this verse is this:

﴿And know that whatever spoil you have gained, a fifth of it belongs to Allah, to the Messenger, to the near relatives, to the orphans, to the needy and to the wayfarer.﴾ And this is the translation of the verse as presented.

The summarized ruling is this: from everything taken as ghanimah (spoils), four parts are to be distributed among the mujahidin, and in the fifth part the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has the authority to dispose of it as he wishes. After him, this authority belongs to the heads of state who uphold the Shariah and who strive in the way of Allah, and they will spend this portion on these purposes: in the way of Allah, for the Messenger of Allah, for the relatives, for the orphans, and for the needy. In this way, this share will meet the real needs of the people. Here, it is sufficient to say only this much.

After this, there is a continuing guidance, which is the second part of the verse:

﴿If you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met, (then accept this portion willingly); and Allah has power over everything.﴾

Faith has certain signs by which one can tell that a person is a believer. Allah, in order to affirm the faith of the people of Badr, also gives as evidence that they have accepted Allah's Shariah concerning spoils and wealth, and therefore they are believers. Although the people of Badr were the people of Badr, they became believers because they accepted the rulings sent down to Allah's servant on the Day of Criterion. In effect, accepting the law of the Shariah was made by Allah a condition of faith, and obedience to the Shariah was declared to be the requirement of their faith, so that it would become evident that their declaration of faith was true.

In short, the concept of faith in the Quran is unequivocal. It has no flexibility, and it does not need interpretation or patchwork, nor the subtleties that were created because of some fiqh discussions. Later, when the schools of fiqh came into existence, they produced all kinds of interpretations of the texts (nusus), and people began engaging in disputation in the logical and theological (kalami) style, in the form of hypotheses, about these fiqh and religious subjects. In later eras, because of these fiqh and theological disagreements, each sect made accusations against the others, and the others responded to these accusations. Then people began attributing kufr (disbelief) to one another, and the others began to respond in kind, and all this disputation was not based on the clear principles of religion. Rather, all these discussions were founded on personal interests, desires, and the hostility and enmity of opponents. And then the markets of fatwas of kufr became hot, and debates on subsidiary matters took place. Then these accusations began to be answered with violence, and people became very harsh in these accusations. This extremism occurred because of those particular historical causes and factors. The religion of Islam is in fact entirely clear. There is no flexibility in it, no patchwork in it, and no extremism in it. It is said in a hadith: "Faith is not...": faith is not merely wishful thinking, but faith is that it settles in the heart and action confirms it. For faith to stand, it is necessary that the law Allah has made be implemented in actual life. And it is disbelief (kufr) to abandon the law that Allah has made, and to make judgments according to laws other than Allah's, and to seek judgment from courts other than the Shariah. Whether the matters are small or great, this is kufr. These are the plain, unequivocal, and clear commands of God and His Messenger. Whatever other opinions there are beyond this are merely interpretations and the result of religious disagreements.

This is a clear example, in which Allah speaks in a clear, unequivocal, and emphatic manner:

﴿And know that whatever spoil you have gained, a fifth of it belongs to Allah, to the Messenger, to the near relatives, to the orphans, to the needy and to the wayfarer, if you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met.﴾ The meaning is: and know that whatever spoil you have gained, its fifth belongs to Allah and the Messenger and to the relatives and orphans and needy and the traveller. If you believe in Allah and in what We sent down to Our servant on the day of Criterion, the day the two armies met.

This is exactly the example of all those guidance and declarations that the Quran gives very clearly about faith, its limits and conditions, and its requirements, which are wholly unequivocal and decisive.

Allah took ownership of the spoils from those who had gathered them and placed it in the hands of Allah and the Messenger of Allah, as was clearly stated at the beginning of the surah. This was done so that full authority over this matter would transfer to Allah and the Messenger of Allah, and so that the hearts and resolve of the mujahidin would be entirely purified of those worldly impurities, and so that they would hand over their affairs from beginning to end to Allah and the Messenger of Allah. Allah is their Lord, the Messenger is their leader, and they participate in this struggle solely for Allah, gathering only under the banner of Allah. Obeying Allah, they should accept with their soul, their body, and their wealth the commands of Allah and the Messenger of Allah. And in all their affairs they should accept the decisions of Allah and the Messenger of Allah without question. This is the reality of faith. At the beginning of this surah, when people were being asked to give up their right of ownership over the spoils to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they were addressed in this way:

﴿They ask you about the bounties. Say: The bounties belong to Allah and the Messenger. So fear Allah, set right what is between you, and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you are believers.﴾

Then, after they submitted and were content with this command of Allah, and the reality of faith settled in their hearts, Allah returned four parts to them and left the fifth part as it was, so that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) could dispose of it as he wished, and from this share the entitled ones of the Muslim community, the relatives, orphans, needy, and travellers, would be provided for. Now, when the four parts were returned to them, this idea settled in their hearts: this is Allah's property. It did not become their possession merely because of jihad and victory. Because jihad and fighting are for Allah, and victory belongs not to them but to the religion of Allah. That they have become entitled to it is merely a gift from Allah, just as victory is also a gift from Allah. For Allah Himself arranged the entire plan of that battle with His own hands, and this idea was repeatedly placed in their minds. Accepting this new command of Allah is also a requirement of the command of God, and it is pure faith. It is a condition of faith, it is an inevitable requirement of faith. Consider again:

﴿And know that whatever spoil you have gained, a fifth of it belongs to Allah, to the Messenger, to the near relatives, to the orphans, to the needy and to the wayfarer, if you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day the two hosts met.﴾

These verses consistently establish one clear, unequivocal, and decisive principle, which concerns the foundations of religion. In them, the meaning and implications of faith are defined. The reality of faith, its conditions, and its requirements are mentioned.

Here the word "Our servant" (ʿabdinā) is used for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This word is used in the context in which, at the very beginning, authority over all the bounties and spoils was given to the Messenger of Allah, and then, leaving aside four parts, authority over the fifth part was given to him ("Our servant"). This phrase also points to the fact that servanthood and worship are part of the reality of faith, and that the station of "Our servant" is that lofty station which any servant may someday reach. This is said in a context in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was being given, alongside the propagation of religion, administrative authority over worldly affairs as well. In truth, this station is indeed a lofty one, which no one could reach: that a person should possess authority over both religion and worldly affairs and, at the same time, hold the station of servanthood.

Only the pure worship of Allah can lift a person above the worship of his own desires. Likewise, this same worship can protect a person from the worship of other human beings. A human being can attain the high dignity and superiority of humanity only when he is safe from the servitude of all people other than Allah.

Those who refuse to become servants of Allah alone then put on the yoke of the most degrading servitudes. They become slaves of their carnal desires and base inclinations, and the immediate result is that the quality which Allah gave to humans alone among His creatures, that they are beings who move by will, ceases to exist for them. When they no longer have control over their will, they become mere animals. Indeed, they become more degraded than those animals, and they become the lowest of the low, although Allah had created them in the best of forms (﴿لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنسَانَ فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ﴾).

Moreover, those who turn away from the servitude of Allah become entangled in other dangerous servitudes. They adopt the servitude of human beings like themselves. These human masters shape the lives of these people according to their own desires and aims. Whatever theories their limited vision can reach, they guide these people toward those theories, and behind those theories there are only these theories and aims, so that through them the human masters establish their own superiority, and the life of the people becomes full of ignorant defects and based on arrogance.

These human masters prescribe for them axiomatic principles, and they say and make them believe that there is no alternative for them except this. They should bow before these principles and not oppose them. Some principles are based on historical dialectics, some on economic realities, and some on natural evolution. In short, these and other similar servitudes, which materialism has imposed upon humans, have so entrapped humanity in their quagmire that they neither want to escape from them, and even if they wish to, they see no way out. He is bound by these self-made inviolable principles and lives under a terrifying determinism.

After this, the second word here is also extremely important. Here, for Badr, the term Yawm al-Furqan (the Day of Criterion) has been used, meaning the day of decision, that is, the day of the encounter of the two armies. The reality is that the day of Badr was actually a decisive day. Allah had prepared the entire plan for that day, and the work was done in it according to Allah's help and guidance. That day was the day of decision between truth and falsehood. The exegetes have stated this in summary: it was the day of decision. This is because its results were extremely profound, far-reaching and all-encompassing.

That day was in practice a day of decision between truth and falsehood. But on that day the decision was between the real truth and falsehood, upon which the heavens and the earth are actually established. The nature of all things and all living creatures is founded upon that truth: the truth which acknowledges Allah's essence as one, recognizes Allah alone as King, and accepts Him as the sole governor and administrator of this world, the truth which teaches that this entire universe is the servant and slave of Allah. In its heavens, its earth, its things and its living creatures, Allah alone exercises authority, and all these things are under Allah's divinity, His kingship and His creative dominion, and no one can refuse obedience to Him. And which falsehood is falsehood? It means the falsehood which is counterfeit, and which at that time, on the day of Badr, had overspread the world and had suppressed that great truth. That falsehood had produced on the surface of the earth such satanic powers as decided matters of human life in whatever way they wished. In that false system, it was human desires that decided the destinies of all things and living beings. This was the great decision that took place on that day. That is, on the great day of Badr, a decisive battle occurred between that great truth and that all-encompassing falsehood. Between them, on the day of Badr, such a decision and separation took place that thereafter no confusion or association between them ever occurred again.

That day was a decisive day between truth and falsehood in a very wide and profound sense, and in a very subtle and refined sense. It was a decision between truth and falsehood in the depths of the human conscience. In the field of human ideas and consciousness, it was the Criterion between monotheism and polytheism. In human morality and conduct, it was a decisive day between truth and falsehood. In the worship and servitude of Allah, it was a decisive battle between truth and falsehood. It was a decisive day between monotheism and all forms and shapes of polytheism, whether that relates to persons, values, customs and traditions, or any other form. And in terms of outward events too, it was a decisive day between that truth and that falsehood. On that day there was a conflict between the worship of desires and persons on one side and values and civilization on the other. On one side were personal interests, and on the other side were divine laws. On one side were the ideas of the sovereignty, divinity and supreme authority of Allah alone, and on the other side was the superiority of humans over humans. Thus it was established that there is no one who can benefit or harm except Allah, no ruler except Him, and no lawgiver except Him. Now people's heads were raised high. Now they would not bow before any other. All people were considered equal with one another. If there was any superiority over them, it was that of Allah and His law. Now people would rise in crowds and raise the banners of freedom, and be delivered from oppressors and rebels.

In the history of the Islamic movement, this day was a dividing line between two eras. Previously the movement had acted on the principles of patience and endurance, and was gathering its strength. Now the era of the strength, initiative and growth of the Islamic movement began. Islam gave a new concept for the whole of life. It gave a new system for settling human affairs, and a new collective system was presented. A new political system and constitution for government was proposed, and it was proclaimed that now no human being would be the slave of another human being. All would be slaves of Allah, the Lord of the worlds alone. And now those satanic powers which had usurped Allah's right of sovereignty had no justification to remain alive. For such a concept of Islam, it was necessary that it have its own power, that it be a movement, that it hold an initiative position, and that it have the capacity to move forward. This is because Islam, holding such ideas, cannot adopt the position of a silent spectator for an indefinite period. Islam's intention was not that it should remain merely an idea and belief for its adherents, or that its manifestation should be only in some rituals of worship, or that it should consist only of particular individual moral norms. Therefore it was necessary that it give new moral concepts, give a new system, a new government, and lay the foundation of a new society, and that all these manifestations be practical. Then, to achieve those goals, it would remove all the obstacles that stood in the way of those aims and would not allow the above-mentioned principle to be implemented in the lives of Muslims or to be put into practice on this earth, whereas Islam had come from Allah precisely so that it might be implemented in the world (for details see Surah al-Anfal).

This day was also the Yawm al-Furqan in the entire history of humanity. This is because the humanity that inhabited the earth before that day was, on the whole, different from the humanity that emerged in the system that came after that day. This new concept and ideology, as a result of which this new system was formed, and the new human being who emerged through the ideas this new system gave, was in essence a new birth for all humanity. These values upon which the whole of life is founded, on the basis of which the collective system is also prepared, and on the basis of which the legal system is also prepared, all these matters, after the battle of Badr, ceased to be the sole possession of the Muslims, when the new collective system had been established. Rather, gradually these values became the possession of all humanity. Humanity was affected by this change within the Dar al-Islam just as it was affected outside the Dar al-Islam. People were affected by it in friendship with Islam, and people were also affected by it in enmity towards Islam. The Crusader forces that launched a military campaign against Islam from the west, whose aim was to wage war against Islam and to end its superiority, were influenced by the customs and the principles and laws of the Islamic society. Returning from here, they began a struggle against the feudal system prevalent in the West, because although they had not seen the real Islamic system, they were influenced by the traces of Islamic principles that remained in Middle Eastern society. The Tatars, who began attacks on Islam from the east, intended to uproot Islam from its foundations, and the Jews and the Crusaders had incited them to this task. They were influenced by Islamic ideas, spread Islam to further new regions, and established a system of government, namely the Islamic Caliphate, which remained in the heart of Europe from the fifteenth century until the twentieth century. In short, after Badr, the entire human history was influenced by Islamic thought, and this day was also a dividing line and a Furqan between ancient and modern history. Humanity was influenced by Islam both within the Muslim world and within the opposing bloc.

Similarly, this day was a dividing line between two concepts of victory and support. Here, all the essential elements of victory and support were present on the side of the polytheists, and all the apparent causes of defeat were present on the front of the Muslims. Even the hypocrites and those with sick hearts made the remark that ﴿غَرَّ هَؤُلَاءِ دِينُهُمْ﴾ (Their religion has deceived these people). But it was Allah's will that the battle should take place in this manner. It was a battle between a large number of disbelievers and a small number of believers, so that it could be shown that the criteria of victory and support are not what is known among ordinary people. Rather, Allah willed that here the national ideas, with scarce equipment, should triumph over a great army that lacked conviction, so that people would know that support is destined for a righteous belief and true ideas, and that victory is not attained merely on the basis of numbers and weapons. It was also intended to show that people of conviction should throw themselves into the battle against disbelief and not wait for the time when the apparent strength of the two sides becomes equal, because people holding true ideas have the power of truth behind them. This is not merely an empty claim, but in the battle of Badr it was decisively settled, and people saw it with their own eyes.

At the end, I say that the battle of Badr was also, from another perspective, a Furqan between truth and falsehood, and this aspect is pointed out in this verse:

﴿وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللَّهُ إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيْرَ ذَاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمْ وَيُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَن يُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِمَاتِهِ وَيَقْطَعَ دَابِرَ الْكَافِرِينَ ۔ لِيُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ وَيُبْطِلَ الْبَاطِلَ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾

Remember when Allah promised you that one of the two groups would be yours. You wished that the group without armed strength would be yours. But Allah's will was that by His words He would establish the truth as truth and cut off the root of the disbelievers, so that truth would be established as truth and falsehood would be left as falsehood, even though the criminals might dislike it.

Those who went out for Badr went out only with the intention of seizing the caravan of Abu Sufyan, which was unarmed. But Allah did not fulfill their desire. Allah gave Abu Sufyan's caravan the opportunity to escape, and made the people of Islam clash with the mighty army of Abu Jahl. As a result, a battle took place, the Muslims were granted victory, and the disbelievers were taken captive and killed. And it did not happen that the Muslims went out for amusement and, by seizing the caravan, obtained the spoils of war by an easy means. Allah did this so that ﴿لِيُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ وَيُبْطِلَ الْبَاطِلَ﴾ (that truth might be established as truth and falsehood as falsehood). In this, Allah wanted to show what the method of establishing truth is according to His plan. The meaning was that truth is not established merely by preaching and admonition, nor by theoretical and wise propagation, nor is truth established as a result of theoretical debate and argument, that someone should say by proofs that this is truth and that is falsehood. Truth does not take practical form, and falsehood is not removed from the practical life of people, until the power and authority of falsehood is ended and the supreme authority of truth is established in its place. And this is not possible until the armies of truth are granted support and victory, and falsehood is defeated, that is, in a military battle. In short, this religion is a dynamic methodology; it is not merely a theory, it is not merely scholarly debate and argument, nor is it merely a negative belief that there is no deity except Allah. Rather, it also has a positive aspect. The establishment of truth and the abolition of falsehood take place on the battlefield, and truth in practice receives support, and this practical support is the Furqan. In this verse, attention has been drawn to this reality, that Allah the Exalted said what you wanted, and that Allah had brought the Messenger of Allah out of his house on that day with the truth, and the truth was that the caravan would pass by and you would encounter the army equipped with provisions.

This was the significance of the Criterion (al-Furqaniyyah) of this religion and this day, through which the reality of this religion and its temperament become clear and become part of the awareness and consciousness of the Muslims. It is a Criterion whose need is felt today, because within the awareness and consciousness of the Muslims today, a deviation and laxity has arisen regarding the correct concept of Islam, and this slackness has spread to such an extent that some people claim to be engaged in the call to religion (da'wah) and the propagation of religion (tabligh), yet they have not been able to attain this method of establishing the truth (ihqaq al-haqq).

This was the significance of the Day of Badr as a Criterion, about which it was said that it is (the Day of the Criterion, al-Yawm al-Furqan) and (the Day when the two hosts met, Yawm al-Taqa al-Jam'an), and which contains profound meaning. "And Allah is over all things Competent" (wa-Allahu 'ala kulli shay'in qadir), and the Day of Badr is the finest example of the power of Allah. It is an example in which there is no need for speech, and in which there is no room for doubt or suspicion. It is a witnessed reality, and there is no need for lengthy discourse to explain it. Indeed, Allah is over all things capable.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 8, verse 42:

Now the context moves into further details of the Day of Criterion (Yawm al-Furqan). Scenes of the battle are presented. In them, this battle is depicted in an extraordinarily striking and vivid manner, as though this scene is running on a screen, and in its scenes the planning and decree of Allah are manifest and prominent. In such a way that the hand of divine power is clearly visible, doing its work. Moreover, from these glimpses the purposes that Allah desires, and which are still the aim of faith, are plainly evident.

In this battle, the camps of both sides come into view, and in it the hand of divine power is moving along. The hand of Allah's power is clearly prominent. This is the camp of those people, and that is the opposing party on the other side, while the caravan is passing far away along the sea coast. The words of the Qur'an are drawing a picture of the Messenger of Allah's dream; in that picture the disbelievers appear few to the Muslims, and the Muslims appear few to the disbelievers. Such scenes, in a few words, are the distinctive feature of the Holy Qur'an alone. The scenes and their background both appear clear and transparent. The movements and striving within the scene are plainly visible, in just a few phrases.

These scenes which these verses have presented: we have already given details from the Sirah of these scenes earlier, when the Muslims left Madinah and descended in a valley near Madinah, and on the other side of the same valley the disbelievers had set up their camp. Between the two there was a high mound which separated them. As for the caravan, Abu Sufyan had led it towards the coast, lower down than both armies.

No army knew where the opposing party was. Allah gathered them on both sides of a single mound. This was Allah's special will. Had the place of meeting been fixed beforehand between them, they would not have come so close to one another in this way; perhaps they would have avoided each other. Here Allah indicates precisely this point, that it was His special planning.

﴿When you were on the nearer side of the valley, and they were on the farther side, and the caravan was lower than you.﴾ ﴿And even if you had made a mutual appointment, you would certainly have differed about the appointment;﴾ ﴿but it was so that Allah might accomplish a matter which was destined to be done.﴾ Remember the time when you were on the near side of the valley and they were on the far side, while the caravan was below you (towards the coast). Had you and they made a pact to meet, you would certainly have evaded that appointment at that moment; but what happened occurred so that Allah might bring to pass a matter He had already decreed.

Thus the encounter with one another, and that too so close that there was no way to flee: this too was Allah's will; there were certain outcomes whose manifestation was the divine will. Therefore Allah brought about so secret and sudden a confrontation, and made you the means. For the manifestation of those outcomes, and for you, all circumstances were made conducive.

What then was that matter? What was that purpose for which all these arrangements were made through the higher realm? ﴿That he who perishes might perish by clear proof, and he who lives might live by clear proof.﴾ "So that whoever is to perish should perish with clear evidence, and whoever is to live should live with clear evidence."

By "perishing" is taken both its apparent meaning and it is applied to disbelief. Likewise the word "life" is used both in its lexical and direct meaning and it is applied to faith. Here the second meaning is intended. This meaning is used with this word in other places in the Qur'an as well: ﴿Is he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness and will never emerge from it?﴾ Here disbelief is described as death and faith as life. Thus the Islamic concept of life defines its standpoint regarding the reality of faith and the reality of disbelief, and while explaining the above-mentioned verse we have discussed this at some length in Surah al-An'am. See Surah al-An'am.

Here we prefer this meaning because the Day of Badr, according to the Qur'an, was the Day of Criterion. In that battle Allah made a thorough separation between truth and falsehood, which we have already mentioned. Therefore, whoever now adopts disbelief is, in effect, denying clear argument and proof, and whoever believes, believes in clear proof. And these proofs are now bright and evident because that encounter has laid everything open.

The manner in which this battle took place, and the circumstances and conditions in which it was fought, are in themselves a sign that cannot be denied. In it there are indications that behind human plans the hand of divine power is at work; these indications were most evident signs, and they showed that besides human strength there are other decisive forces that operate. This establishes that this religion has a Lord, and that He stands behind His sincere, struggling servants, provided they are patient and steadfast. Had the outcome matched apparent material strength, the polytheists would not have been defeated and the Muslim community would not have attained such a great victory.

The polytheists themselves acknowledged this reality: when they were setting out for the battle, their ally offered them assistance, and they said: "By God, if we were to fight only against men, we would not be weak; but if we are fighting against God, as Muhammad claims, then no one has any power against God." They themselves believed that they were fighting against God, as Muhammad claimed, for Muhammad had told them this truth, and they also acknowledged that Muhammad was truthful and trustworthy. Now, if they perished, they perished in the right. Allah, commenting on this, said: ﴿That he who perishes might perish by clear proof, and he who lives might live by clear proof.﴾

But alongside this, another indication appears here: that when truth and falsehood contend on the battlefield, and truth emerges victorious on the field, when it has already prevailed ideologically, this causes it to become completely clear and prominent in the eyes of people, and no doubt or suspicion remains in the hearts and minds of people concerning it. In such a way that the victory of truth on the field becomes entirely manifest, and after such clarity, if anyone still chooses disbelief and destruction, he has no excuse. Now, if someone disbelieves, he is destroying himself; and if he accepts Islam, he accepts life and truth with full insight, and he has certainty of Allah's help, because he is upon the truth. He receives Allah's help, and his enemies meet defeat and rout.

Now let us go back a little. In the introduction to the ninth part and to Surah al-Anfal, we explained that jihad is necessary so that the power of evil forces is broken over the face of the earth, tyrannical rule is ended, and the word of Allah and the banner of Allah are raised high. Why? So that truth becomes clear and manifest, and then, if anyone perishes, he perishes with full insight, and if anyone lives, he lives with full insight. And from this one also gauges the far-reaching effects of the guidance given in this surah, in which the command is given: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war, by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others besides them whom you do not know.﴾ Preparing strength and striking fear into enemies is also a means by which truth becomes clear. Some people accept the truth in this way. Some people, overawed by strength and seeing the blows of truth, come to understand, and when they see it they perceive that this movement is in reality a movement for human freedom, and as a result, human beings attain freedom throughout the entire universe.

This whole discourse is followed, in this respect, by the statement that in this battle the divine plan was working toward these objectives: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.﴾ Allah is that Being from whom nothing is hidden, whether it belongs to the true party or to the party upon falsehood. And He is aware of the thoughts they hold behind their deeds and words. Therefore, the plan He makes is based on information of both the outward and the inward. He is indeed All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

This was the commentary on the system of divine planning: how profound, hidden and subtle its plans were. Now it is explained what the form and shape of these plans was. (See the next verse.)

Among the subtle arrangements of Allah was that He showed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the enemy as few in number in his dream. They appeared to him as having neither strength nor any weight. The Messenger (ﷺ) related his dream to his Companions. They took it as good news, their resolve grew, and they threw themselves into the battle.

Allah also tells us why the Prophet (ﷺ) was shown the enemy as few: had their number been shown as large, their eyes would have been fixed on their own paucity of numbers and paucity of war equipment, even though they had set out only to meet the caravan and did not expect a battle. In this way they could have fallen into weakness and feebleness. And at the moment of meeting the enemy, a dispute and debate would have begun. Some would say that fighting is good, while others would say that avoiding the encounter is beneficial. In such circumstances, this intellectual disarray within an army is fatal for an army that is preparing for war. "But Allah saved you from it. Indeed, He knows well what is in the breasts," and "Allah knows the state of hearts." Allah showed great kindness to the Muslims by saving them from that state of confusion which causes weakness. Therefore the polytheists were shown as few in the dream, and not shown as many.

And the meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) dream was also real. The Messenger (ﷺ) saw that the disbelievers were few. Although they were greater in number, in terms of weight they were light. Their reality was nothing; their hearts and minds were empty of firm convictions. Their hearts were empty of faith, and they were devoid of beneficial equipment. Although their outward status was deceiving the eyes, inwardly they were without substance and without weight. Allah showed His Messenger (ﷺ) their inner condition. Thus the hearts of the people were filled with tranquility. This is because Allah knew the secrets of hearts. Allah knew that the number and equipment of the Muslims was less than that of the enemy, and what thoughts would arise in their hearts if they came to know the true situation. This was one of the great arrangements among the arrangements of Allah, because Allah is All-Hearing and All-Knowing.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 44:

Now that the armies stand facing each other on the field of Badr, the true dream of the Messenger (ﷺ) comes to the fore again, and it appears in a state of the two sides' battle-array. This too was one of the special arrangements of Allah. Allah reminds them: just keep this in view once more; during the commentary on the events of this battle it is reminded that:

﴿And remember when, at the time of the encounter, Allah showed them to you as few in your eyes and made you appear as few in their eyes, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. And to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

Among the important arrangements of Allah was that this battle should not be avoided, and that both parties should be prepared for this encounter. The Muslims, who saw the enemy as few, were seeing them according to their reality. And the disbelievers, who saw the Muslims as few, were also seeing with their outward eyes. Each saw from its own viewpoint, and the purposes of the divine arrangement were working in both. Thus these events took place in accordance with the command of Allah and His will.

﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾: this remark is most fitting for expressing the truth that all outcomes come out according to the system of divine decree and destiny. The return of all affairs is to Allah; He disposes of His universe as He wills, with His authority, His will, His power and His wisdom, and nothing in this universe can come to pass except in accordance with the requirements of Allah's decree.

---

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 45:

If the matter stands thus, then all the planning belongs to Allah, and victory comes from Allah. Mere numerical superiority is not the decisive factor, and mere material equipment is not decisive in any battle. Therefore, those who have believed should, when they encounter the disbelievers, hold firm. They should prepare the real equipment for the battle between truth and falsehood, and adopt those means which relate to the armoury of the One who plans and the One who decrees. They should seek victory and help from the True Sovereign, turning to the One who is the supreme authority and the possessor of power and majesty. And they should avoid those things which bring defeat upon the disbelieving polytheists, even though their numbers and equipment are very great. They should also avoid pride, arrogance, showing off and display, and be wary of the deceptions of Satan, who destroyed the disbelievers. Therefore they should place their trust in Allah, who is the Mighty, the Wise.

In these brief phrases there surges an ocean of meanings and allusions. Important principles and guidance have been firmly set down. The scenes and visions appear as though they are running on a screen, and you are seeing them with your own eyes. The words are the manifestation of the thoughts of the heart, the emotions of the conscience and the hidden corners of the mind. If a human being or a writer wished to record these very meanings, volumes would be needed, and even then it would not be possible for him to do them full justice. In short, this is the astonishing portrayal that the Qur'an presents.

The believers are addressed, and the successive calls in this surah are arranged in this manner. Instructions are given that whenever they face an enemy, they should strive to remain steadfast, and that they should develop within themselves the real means of victory. This is the true preparation.

يٰٓاَيُّھَا الَّذِيْنَ اٰمَنُوْٓا اِذَا لَقِيْتُمْ فِئَةً فَاثْبُتُوْا وَاذْكُرُوا اللّٰهَ كَثِيْرًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُوْنَ ۔ وَاَطِيْعُوا اللّٰهَ وَرَسُوْلَهٗ وَلَا تَنَازَعُوْا فَتَفْشَلُوْا وَتَذْهَبَ رِيْحُكُمْ وَاصْبِرُوْا ۭ اِنَّ اللّٰهَ مَعَ الصّٰبِرِيْنَ ۔ وَلَا تَكُوْنُوْا كَالَّذِيْنَ خَرَجُوْا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ بَطَرًا وَّرِئَاۗءَ النَّاسِ وَيَصُدُّوْنَ عَنْ سَبِيْلِ اللّٰهِ ۭوَاللّٰهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُوْنَ مُحِيْطٌ ۔

O you who believe! When you meet a company (of the enemy), stand firm and remember Allah much, that you may be successful. And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute with one another, lest you lose courage and your strength depart. And be patient; surely Allah is with those who are patient. And do not be like those who came out of their homes insolently and to be seen of men, and who bar (others) from the way of Allah. And Allah encompasses what they do.

These are the true causes of victory: that the army of Islam stands firm against the enemy, that its hearts are bound to Allah, that it is obedient to the Messenger and its leader, that its members avoid mutual disputes and differences, that they bear the difficulties that come upon them on this path, and that they are neither arrogant and showy nor rebellious because of their strength.

As for steadfastness and standing firm, it is the first step on the path of victory and success. Whoever stands firm on the battlefield will be the one who attains victory. Moreover, while the Muslims do not even know how much hardship their enemy is suffering, and how the pains that reach them also reach the enemy, the believers are hopeful of ranks through honour and martyrdom from Allah, whereas the enemy has no such hope; rather, Hell is certain for them. The believer hopes for reward from Allah, and therefore he remains steadfast, whereas they have no hope at all. If they show even a little patience and steadfastness, the enemy is bound to break. The Muslims will surely attain one of two good things, and they have been given the guarantee of either martyrdom or victory and help. Whereas their enemy has no guarantee even of this worldly life for which he sacrifices himself, because in the Hereafter there is nothing at all for him.

Then, remembrance of Allah in battle is a lasting provision for the journey, and the believers have been strongly enjoined to it. The believing mujahideen have always kept the remembrance of Allah alive in their tongues and hearts, and in describing the history of the believers, the Qur'an has mentioned this specifically.

The Qur'an repeatedly mentions the remembrance of Allah on the part of the believers. When the sorcerers accepted faith in the face of Moses (peace be upon him), and Pharaoh addressed them with threatening words, their reply was: "وما تنقم منا الا ان امنا بايات ربنا لما جاءتنا ربنا افرغ علينا صبرا وتوفنا مسلمين" — "And you take vengeance on us only because we have believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims."

Similarly, this quality is also mentioned in the account of a small army of the Children of Israel. When this small number faced Goliath (Jalut) and his large army, they said: "ولما برزوا لجالوت وجنوده قالوا ربنا افرغ علينا صبرا وثبت اقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين" — "And when they went out against Goliath and his hosts, they said: 'Our Lord, pour upon us patience, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people.'"

Likewise, in Islamic history, the Qur'an says of the countless believing bands who took positions against the disbelievers:

"وكاين من نبي قتل معه ربيون كثير فما وهنوا لما اصابهم في سبيل الله وما ضعفوا وما استكانوا والله يحب الصابرين. وما كان قولهم الا ان قالوا ربنا اغفر لنا ذنوبنا واسرافنا في امرنا وثبت اقدامنا وانصرنا على القوم الكافرين" — "And how many a prophet has fought, and with him many godly men. They did not lose heart for what befell them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken or submit. Allah loves the patient. Their only words were: 'Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people.'"

This teaching sank deeply into the community of believers. Whenever it met the enemy, its conduct was always of this kind. Afterwards, at the Battle of Uhud, the community of Muslims faced difficulties and became disheartened; yet on the very day after Badr, when that defeated army was called again, this teaching was fully dominant over their souls. "الذين قال لهم الناس ان الناس قد جمعوا لكم فاخشوهم فزادهم ايمانا وقالوا حسبنا الله ونعم الوكيل" — "Those to whom people said: 'The people have gathered against you, so fear them,' and it increased them in faith, and they said: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'"

When facing the enemy, there are countless benefits of remembering Allah. One benefit is that a person is connected to a power over which no other power prevails. Then there is trust in Allah, who supports His friends fully. Through this, the reality of the battle, its causes and its aims remain present in the mind, for this battle is fought for the sake of Allah. It is fought for the establishment of the rule of Allah on this earth and for the destruction of the tyrannical powers that have forcibly seized the rights of sovereignty, for the aim of this battle is that the word of Allah be raised in the world. This war is not for conquest of lands, nor for spoils of war and plunder, nor for the establishment of personal rule, nor for the establishment of national rule. Moreover, this command also emphasises that even in the most difficult circumstances a person should not remain heedless of the remembrance of Allah. All these allusions are most precious, and through the teachings of Allah they take the form of reality.

The matter of obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger is that its purpose is this: that upon entering the battle, a person should bow his head in submission, and that the very motives which give rise to disputes among Muslims should be eliminated. The command is: ﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength depart﴾. Disputes among people arise only when the sources of their leadership become more than one, and they take guidance from various directions, or when they merely follow their own desires, and the source of their thoughts and concepts is nothing but their base passions. By contrast, when people are obedient only to Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the first major cause of dispute is eliminated at its root, even though people's viewpoints differ, because dispute does not arise merely from difference of viewpoint, but its origin is the desire of the self (hawa al-nafs). Owing to the desire of the self, every person holding a viewpoint begins to insist upon his position, even when he can see that the truth lies on the other side. Now, in one pan of the scale is the person's own self, and in the other pan is the truth. And at the outset, people give preference to their own self over the truth. Therefore, here it is taught that people should obey Allah and His Messenger at the time of battle. This matter is the requirement of discipline (dissipline), and in battles discipline is the foremost factor. That is, obedience to the supreme command, and then obedience to the commander who runs that supreme command. In Islam, the obedience that exists is inward obedience, and it is not like the obedience of ordinary worldly armies, because the fighting of ordinary armies is not for the sake of Allah, and nor is there among their members a brotherhood for the sake of Allah. Therefore there is a very great difference between the discipline of Islamic armies and the discipline of secular armies.

As for patience, it is an important quality of those who fight in battle, especially those who fight for the sake of Islam, whether this battle is between truth and falsehood within human psychology or is on the field of combat. ﴿And be patient; indeed, Allah is with the patient.﴾

This passage is clearly a translation task I can do. Here is the translation:

These instructions are being given for the purification of the Muslim community and the group of mujahideen: that they should not take part in fighting and jihad in a state of being proud of their strength and numbers, and should not spend the strength that Allah has given them on paths for which Allah has issued no command. For the detachments of the believers go out for qital fi sabilillah (fighting in the way of Allah), and their aim is that the sovereignty of Allah be enforced in the lives of people, so that people become slaves of Allah alone. For this reason they raise the banner of jihad, to crush all the tyrannical powers that have enslaved people and that are establishing their own divinity on earth in opposition to Allah, although Allah has given them no permission to do so. Nor does the Shariah of Allah accept their action. This banner is raised so that all human beings across the entire earth may be freed from every kind of slavery, since these slaveries are against human dignity and nobility, and Islamic detachments go out for jihad and qital only so that the dignity and freedom of people may be protected. Their aim is not to establish their own rule or to gain supremacy on earth. Nor is their aim to make people their slaves, or to strut about in pride and spend the strength Allah has given them in wrong ways. Thus the aims of Islamic detachments contain no share of personal goals, and if they receive help and become victorious, they have done so in obedience to the command: they establish the Islamic system of life, raise the word of Allah, and seek the bounty and pleasure of Allah. And even the spoils of war that they obtain from the battle, they are indifferent to them.

Who went out in pride, who was displaying their strength before people? And who was barring people from the path of Allah? These people were before the eyes of the Muslims. They were present in the form of the army of Quraysh, just as that army had set out. The Quraysh who went out with boasting and vainglory, their end was also before the Muslims, and the humiliating and shattered state to which they had fallen was also before the people of Islam. The address Allah made to the believers was embodied before them. Just consider it again.

*"And do not be like those who went out from their homes in insolence and to be seen by people, and who bar from the path of Allah. And Allah is encompassing of what they do."* (Qur'an 8:47)

Insolence, showing off, and barring from the path of Allah were all made evident by the remark of Abu Jahl. When Abu Jahl received the message from Abu Sufyan that he had escaped by the coast and that he should return with his army, since there was no need for them to fight Muhammad and his companions, the condition of Quraysh was this: they had brought along singing girls as well. Along the road they were singing and playing music, slaughtering livestock, and passing around cups of wine and kebabs. In reply to that message, Abu Jahl said: "We will not return until we reach the field of Badr, stay there three days, slaughter animals, drink wine, and hold gatherings of singing and music. If we do this, all the Arabs will fear us." When Abu Sufyan's messenger returned and conveyed Abu Jahl's reply, Abu Sufyan said: "Alas for what will become of my people! This is Abu Jahl's doing. He disliked turning back, because he was the leader of the people, and he adopted insolence. Insolence is in any case a defect and an ill omen. If Muhammad crushes this army, we will be humiliated forever." Abu Sufyan's foresight proved correct. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions reduced that army to ruin, and the army of disbelief was humiliated because of that insolence, since they carried the aims of arrogance, display, and barring the path of God. This is why their backs were broken at Badr. *"Wallahu bima ya'malun muhit"*: "What they are doing is within the grasp of Allah." No plan of theirs can escape from Allah, and no strength of theirs can oppose Him. Their strength and their knowledge are all within His grasp.

Next it is explained that Satan kept constantly inciting the polytheists to fight this battle, and since these people had been deceived by Satan, they were thus made to suffer humiliation, and they fell into defeat and collapse.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 48:

The incident alluded to here is reported in several narrations. However, none of these narrations has the status of a hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. There is only one hadith, which Imam Malik has related in the Muwatta. Ahmad narrates from Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Ibn al-Majishun, from Malik, from Ibrahim ibn Abu Ablah, from Talhah ibn Ubaydullah ibn Kurayz, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Iblis is never as humbled, as despised, as angry as on the Day of Arafah. This is because he sees the mercy descending and Allah forgiving sins. Yes, on the Day of Badr he was also like this." The Companions asked what he had seen on the Day of Badr that made him like this. He said: "He saw Jibril distributing the angels."

This hadith is also mursal, and in its chain is the narrator Abd al-Malik ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Majishun, who is weak (da'if).

Apart from this, the reports that exist come from Hadrat Ibn Abbas, and these narrations have been transmitted through Ali ibn Abu Talhah and through Ibn Jurayj, or from Urwah ibn Zubayr through Ibn Ishaq, from Qatadah through Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and from Hasan and Muhammad ibn Ka'b. All of these have been related by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari.

From Muthanna, from Abd Allah ibn Salih, from Mu'awiyah, from Ali ibn Abu Talhah, from Hadrat Ibn Abbas, it is said that Iblis came on the Day of Badr with a host of devils. He had a banner with him. He was in the form of a man of the Banu Mudlij. Satan himself was in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum. Satan said to the polytheists: "Today no one will overcome you, and I am your neighbour." When the people drew up their ranks, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a handful of dust and threw it at the faces of the polytheists. They were defeated. When Jibril turned his attention to Iblis, his hand was in the hand of one of the polytheists, so he pulled his hand away from that polytheist and turned his back and fled, and those with him also fled. A man said: "O Suraqah! You think you are our neighbour?" He replied: "I see what you do not see. I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment." He said this when he saw the angels.

From Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, it is said that when the Quraysh gathered and set out, I mentioned to them the matters between them and the Banu Bakr, that is, the war. They were about to turn back, when Iblis appeared to us in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Mudlji. This man was among the nobles of Kinanah. He said: "I am your companion. If Kinanah take some action against you from behind, you will not like it." Upon this they set out with great speed.

From Bishr ibn Mu'adh, from Yazid, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, it is said that in the commentary of the verse "wa idh zayyana lahum al-shaytan a'malahum" up to "wa Allahu shadid al-iqab," it was mentioned that Satan saw Jibril descending and with him other angels. This enemy of Allah became certain that he could do nothing against the angels. So he said: "I see what you do not see; I fear Allah." These words were a lie uttered by this enemy of God. There is no fear of God in his heart, but he knew well that he could not stand against them. It is the habit of this enemy of Allah that he leads his followers, but when truth and falsehood face each other, he abandons his companions in a shameful manner and declares his disavowal of them.

In Fi Zilal al-Quran, in accordance with the method we have adopted, we do not comment on unseen matters regarding which the Qur'an and Sunnah give no detail, because unseen matters relate to belief, and matters of belief must be established either from the Qur'an or from the Sunnah of the Prophet. But it is also not our method to deny every unseen matter merely because it is unseen.

Here the verse of the Qur'an makes clear that Satan had made the deeds of the polytheists appear attractive to them. Satan had incited them to march against the Muslims and that he would help them. Then, when the two armies faced each other and saw one another, this Satan turned on his heels and fled, and said: "I see what you do not see. I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment." Thus Satan humiliated them and left them to their own state, so that they might reach their end by themselves, and he did not fulfil the promise he had made to them.

Now, what is the manner in which Satan made their deeds appear attractive to them, and how he made them believe that today no one would be victorious or superior over the polytheists, and how he made a promise of help and how he fled, are not all details found in the Qur'an.

That is to say, regarding the detailed manner of these events we cannot say anything with certainty, because Satan and his activities all pertain to unseen matters, and we cannot say any definite or certain thing about them unless there is a clear text. The Qur'anic text mentions the incident and event, but the detailed circumstances are not described here.

Here our ijtihad ends. In this matter we do not adopt the view of the school of Shaykh Muhammad Abduh, which adopts a fixed method of interpretation for all such unseen matters, denying every sensory action in those unseen realms. In the commentary of this verse, Shaykh Rashid Rida writes:

"Wa idh zayyana lahum al-shaytan a'malahum" — O Prophet, remind the believers that Satan, through his whisperings, made the deeds of these polytheists appear attractive to them, and placed in their hearts the feeling that they were saying: today no one will overcome them, neither the weak and feeble followers of Muhammad nor the other tribes of the Arabs, because you are greater in number and equipment, your soldiers are more warlike than theirs, and along with these circumstances I am your helper. Baydawi has said that he placed in their illusion the notion that those who obey him have him as a helper. And this is why they used to pray: "O Allah, help whichever of the two groups is more upon guidance, and help whichever of the two religions is more upon truth."

"Falamma taraa'at al-fi'atan nakasa 'ala 'aqibayh" — that is, when the two armies drew near to each other and began to see one another and to understand the situation, before the people struck each other and before the battlefield became hot, Satan fled and turned back on his heels, that is, backwards. The meaning given by those commentators who said that "taraa'a" means when the people clashed on the battlefield is mistaken. The meaning is that Satan now ceases to beautify their deeds for them and ceases to mislead them. This speech is then a kind of parable, in which Satan's whisperings are likened to a person who comes, and the act of abandoning those whisperings is likened to a person who turns back on his heels. In addition to this, it is mentioned that he disavowed his connection with those people and left them to their own state. "Wa qala inni bari'un minkum" — that is, he declared that he was free of responsibility for them. And when he saw that the angels were helping the Muslims, he despaired. "Wa Allahu shadid al-iqab" — this may be the speech of Satan, or it may be a separate sentence. I say that the summary of all these matters is that the armies of Satan were spread among the ranks of the polytheists, placing whisperings in their hearts, that is, deceiving them by joining their spirits, while on the other side the angels were spread among the ranks of the Muslims, and they used to place in the pure souls of the Muslims that which strengthened their hearts and made their certainty in Allah's promise of victory even firmer.

This tendency, that the function and share of the angels in that battle was only to give spiritual help to the Muslims, is stated explicitly by the author elsewhere to mean that the angels did not take part in fighting on the Day of Badr. This is a mistaken tendency, because the Qur'an says elsewhere: "Fa-dribu fawq al-a'naq wa-idribu minhum kulla banan" — "So strike above the necks and strike every fingertip of them." An explanation of Satan's actions that makes them merely spiritual contact is an important characteristic of the school of Muhammad Abduh. He makes a similar interpretation of the birds (al-ababil). He says that these were in fact the germs of smallpox, and this is stated explicitly in the tafsir of Ustadh Muhammad Abduh on Juz' 'Amma. I think that in the interpretation of these verses this is a great exaggeration, and there is no need for it, because there is nothing here that makes the outward meaning of the words impossible. Yes, we can only say this much: there is nothing in these verses that shows the detailed manner of these events, and this is the method we have adopted.

Thus, Satan was deceiving those polytheists who had come out of their homes boastfully and were displaying their position to the people, and their aim was to turn people away from the path of Allah, and Satan was inciting them to march. Then at the very moment he abandoned them and fled. On the other side, the hypocrites of Madinah and those with diseased hearts were secretly rejoicing and saying that this army had set out on the road to destruction, that it was facing the great power of the polytheists, while these people were few in number and had no preparation either. These people looked at matters only in their outward appearance, and apparently it seemed that the believers had brought great ruin upon themselves. These people were deceived by their new religion, and they had full confidence in their own help. These were the thoughts of the hypocrites.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 8, verse 49:

The hypocrites, who are sick at heart, are generally few in number. These were the people who were in Makkah, who had inclined towards Islam, but whose beliefs were not sound and whose hearts had not come to rest upon Islam. These people too had come along with that Makkan army. But they were wavering, of unsteady conviction. This remark was made by such people, who saw that the Muslims were few and the polytheists very many.

These hypocrites, in whose hearts there is a disease, were in fact unaware of the real causes of victory and success. They could only see the outward circumstances, and they had not been given the insight to understand hidden matters, or those realities which are not apparent. They did not know how much strength lies in ideas, and how much reliance a believer places upon Allah, how much he trusts in Him, and that if there are great armies but no faith in Allah, they have no strength within them. Although these people called the Muslims deluded, and considered them arrogant about their religion, they thought that these people were bringing themselves to the brink of the pit of destruction, since the polytheists were flowing like a flood. But their point of view was mistaken.

A situation that is visible appears outwardly the same in the eyes of a believer and in the eyes of a non-believing observer. As for the inner reality and true worth, the scales and measures of the two differ in this respect. The non-believing mind sees only the outward state of affairs, and the background remains hidden from its sight. But the vision of a believer is far-reaching, and he sees realities beyond the outward state of affairs. The believer, beyond the outward situation, also grasps its reality, and he determines its true weight and value.

﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then indeed Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise.﴾ This is the matter which the believing heart can understand, and upon this reality it becomes content; but in hearts where there is no faith, this reality remains hidden. Therefore they give it no importance. For this reason the scale of the believer is heavy, the outcome is in his favour, and ultimately this reality is decisive in every matter. In every age and in every place this reality is decisive.

Regarding Badr, the hypocrites and those sick at heart who say, "These people have been driven to delusion by their religion," this is a remark that the hypocrites and people of diseased mentality of every age keep making. When they see that the forces of tyranny are at their height, while the true equipment of this religion is its creed, which possesses within itself a power of repulsion; that the community of believers is fighting for the honour and supremacy of Allah; and that it is obvious that Allah is jealous and always helps His friends.

The hypocrites and people of diseased mentality are making spectacles, and they see that the Muslim community is confronting the forces of tyranny. These people look upon them with contemptuous eyes, while the Muslim community is facing dangers and regards them as insignificant. When these diseased and hypocritical people see the Muslim community plunging into dangers, first they are astonished, and then terror overcomes them, because they see that these people are leaping into obvious dangers. They cannot grasp any real cause for such courage and boldness, nor do they understand why these people are casting themselves into destruction. These people regard religion and ideology as a market commodity: if they see clear benefit in it, they take the initiative; and if no clear benefit appears, they consider safety and well-being to be wiser. They do not look at matters with a believer's eye, nor do they measure outcomes by the measure of faith. But from the viewpoint of the believer, this trade always remains profitable. Of two good outcomes, one of them certainly appears: either the believer is victorious and dominant, or he enters Paradise directly. As for the Divine Being, it holds no importance in the eyes of the hypocrites and people of diseased mentality.

The Noble Qur'an invites the people of faith to view all matters from the standpoint of religion and faith, and to assess affairs with a believing insight. They should see matters in the light of Allah's guidance and His directives, should not give heed to the greatness of tyrannical forces, and should not consider their own strength and their own weight to be small, for Allah's Being is with them. And in their hearts this should always remain fresh: "Whoever relies upon Allah, then indeed Allah is All-Mighty, All-Wise."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 8, verse 50–51:

Now Allah presents an example of the involvement of the divine powers in that battle. In this scene the angels are at work. Look at this scene with the eye of insight. The angels are participating in that battle, and they have begun seizing the disbelievers. They are taking their souls with the utmost contempt and inflicting upon them the harshest torment. This is only because these people came with extreme arrogance, swaggering and displaying their pomp and splendour. In this they are told that this treatment in this hard and difficult time is happening to you because of your evil deeds, and in it no injustice is done to you. Then, after this depiction, it is told that the punishment given to the disbelievers for their denial is a continuing Sunnah (established way) of Allah, just as the same has happened to the people of the Pharaoh and to those before them.

And this is in accordance with the principle that when Allah bestows favour upon a people, He does not withdraw His blessings until those people change their own attitude. In accordance with this principle, Allah dealt with Pharaoh and those before him. And in the future too, whichever people adopt such a way, Allah's treatment of them will also be the same.

Commentary of verses 50, 51.

These two verses refer to the polytheists who were killed at the Day of Badr.

Because the angels were participating in that battle, as it is said: "So strike above the necks and strike every fingertip of them. That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger; and whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger – indeed, Allah is severe in penalty." (8:12–13)

Although we do not have knowledge of the detailed manner of that striking and striking every fingertip, as we said while discussing this verse in the ninth part. But if we do not have knowledge of the detailed manner of a meaning, or if it does not come within our understanding, this does not necessitate that we turn the verse away from its apparent meaning. The apparent meaning is that the angels were commanded by Allah to strike, and we also know that the angels never disobey any command of Allah; they do only what they are commanded. So these two verses are, as it were, an indication to remember the events of Badr, and the intention is to tell that this too is among the events of Badr, that on that day the disbelievers were treated in this way.

However, these verses are showing that whenever the time of death comes upon the disbelievers, the angels treat them in this same manner. The angels' treatment is not specific to those killed at Badr. And this address "wa law tara" (and if you could see) is, as it were, for all the believers. And the Qur'an adopts this style wherever people are directed to an open scene that every observer can see.

In any case, whatever interpretation of these two verses is adopted, the sight of the disbelievers' soul-taking is extremely frightening. The angels pull their souls out of their bodies in an extremely humiliating manner, and along with this contempt and humiliation, these people are afflicted with the severe punishment.

"If only you could see when the angels were taking the souls of the disbelieving slain. They were striking their faces and their backs..."

Now from here onward, instead of narrative style, direct address begins:

"Taste now the punishment of burning." The style of address has been adopted so that this scene comes before the eyes, as if Hell with its fire and the process of burning is present and people are being thrown into it. Curses and damnation are also being pronounced.

"This is the recompense for what your own hands had sent forward." Therefore the punishment being given to you is a just punishment; you deserve it and it is the result of your deeds, otherwise "Allah is not unjust to His servants."

Regarding this verse, which depicts the punishment of burning in Hell, a question arises in the mind: whether this threat being given to them by the angels is of the punishment that will be given to them after reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, or whether the disbelievers enter Hell immediately with the mere taking of their souls.

Both possibilities are possible and permissible, and both meanings can be derived from these verses. Beyond this we do not discuss it further, because it is an unseen matter and Allah has preserved it in His knowledge. Our duty is only to believe in it. It will happen, and nothing in it is an obstacle. When it will happen, whether at the time of death or after the reckoning, is in the knowledge of Allah, who is 'Allam al-Ghuyub (the Knower of the unseen).
