Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah al-Anfal (8), verse 70:

The discourse now turns to the prisoners. A prick is applied to revive them and to awaken them from heedless sleep. Their feelings are stirred so that a ray of hope may shine in their consciousness, so that, full of hope, they may come toward the light, their future may be improved over their past, they may attain a better life than the one they are in, and they may come to a better place than the material ransom they have suffered and the land they belong to. Added to this is Allah's mercy and forgiveness. The result is comprehensive good. But this good can reach them only when their hearts open to the light of faith. Allah must know that there is an element of good within them, and that element is the element of faith. This good is so general and all-encompassing that there is no need to mention the word "faith" in it. Faith is, as it were, pure good, and no matter can be good unless it is connected with faith and its existence is the result of the element of faith, and unless it rests upon faith.

Islam shows tolerance toward prisoners only so that it may seek good in their hearts. If there is some hidden spark within them, it should kindle it. It should awaken their nature from the sleep of heedlessness so that they become ready to accept the Islamic worldview and to be influenced by it, and in the end be illuminated by the light of faith. Islam does not take an enemy captive in order to take revenge on him and humiliate him, or to exploit him, as was common among the Romans and other nations and peoples in the time of the Messenger (ﷺ).

Abu Hurairah reported from some people, and named them, that the people of Quraysh sent a delegation to free their prisoners and to pay the ransom. Every tribe freed its prisoner, and the people were content with this. Abbas said: "Messenger of Allah, I was a Muslim." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has the correct knowledge of your Islam. If the matter is as you say, Allah will reward you. But as far as outward appearance is concerned, you were against us. So pay for yourself and for your two nephews, Nawfal ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Aqil ibn Abi Talib ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Also pay for your ally, the brother of Utbah ibn Amr of Banu al-Harith ibn Fihr." Upon this he said: "Where is the ransom for these people to come from?" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Where is the wealth that you and Umm al-Fadl buried, and you told her that if you died on this journey, this wealth which has been buried is for Banu al-Fadl, Abdullah and Qutham?" Upon this he said: "By Allah, Messenger of Allah, I know that you are the Messenger of Allah. This is a secret that no one knows except me and Umm al-Fadl. So count the twenty-four ouqiyah (a unit of weight) of wealth that you have taken from me as part of the ransom." Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This cannot be. That was spoils of war which Allah gave us from you." Then Abbas paid his own ransom, paid the ransom for his two nephews, and paid the ransom for his ally. Upon this the following verse was revealed: "O Prophet, say to those prisoners who are in your hands: If Allah knows that there is any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what has been taken from you, and will forgive your sins; Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

But while showing this ray of light and opening the door of hope, Allah also warns them that if they betray the Messenger, then their condition will be the same as what happened to them.

They betrayed Allah by associating others with Him, and they did not acknowledge Allah alone as their Lord, although He had taken a covenant from their fitrah (innate nature). And if they intend to betray the Messenger ﷺ as well, even though they are now in his custody, then they should reflect on the consequences of their earlier betrayal. They are now held captive among the Muslims, and Allah has left them at the mercy and compassion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah is All-Knowing and All-Wise, and He knows everything.

Imam Qurtubi, in his tafsir (commentary), quoted the statement of Ibn al-Arabi that when the polytheists were taken captive, some of them spoke about Islam. However, they were not Muslims at heart, and the words they spoke about Islam were not unequivocal. Their aim was to draw close to the Muslims while not distancing themselves from the polytheists. Our scholars have said: if a disbeliever speaks words of faith and even affirms it with his tongue, but is not resolute in it, he will not be considered a believer. But if one of the believers makes such a wavering statement, he will be a disbeliever, unless a whisper arises in his heart that is beyond his power to control, for Allah Himself has pardoned that. Allah has revealed this reality to His Messenger.

"And if they intend to betray you": that is, if this statement of theirs is a deception and betrayal, then they had already committed a betrayal against Allah before this. They adopted disbelief, plotted against Islam, and became resolved to wage war against you. Although their statement is good in outward appearance, and Allah knows that there is some good behind it, Allah will forgive them and will annul their past deeds.

Commentary on Verses 72 to 75:

This lesson now concludes, and with it this surah also ends. In it, the internal affairs and relations of the Islamic society, and the relations between the Islamic society and other societies, have been regulated, and on this subject the foundation of a systematic international law has been laid. By reflecting on these rulings and principles, it becomes clear what the temperament of the Islamic society and the Islamic system is: what is the foundation on which its structure rises, and what is the ultimate point to which this system extends.

The foundation of this system is not based on blood ties. Nor is it based on ties of land and territory. It is not based on ties of colour and race. It is not based on the ties of a shared historical heritage. Nor is it based on the ties of a shared language and a shared economic system. This system is neither a system of kinship, nor nationalism, nor patriotism, nor is it a name for economic interests. Rather, this system is founded upon an ideology. It has come into existence under the leadership of one Messenger. It is the name of a movement. Therefore, those who believed, and who left their homeland and came to the abode of hijrah, cut off all their earthly ties, left their land, left their people, left their interests, and performed jihad in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives; and those who gave refuge and gave help, and drew close to those people because of ideas, and joined the movement by accepting Islamic leadership, these are the ones who are brothers and allies of one another. And as for those who believed but did not migrate to the Abode of Islam, there is no walayah (guardianship/alliance) between them and the Muslims, because after accepting the Islamic creed they did not devote themselves to that creed, did not accept the system of that creed, and did not accept the commands of the leadership of the collective movement. For, in an Islamic society, the ideological relationship between two individuals is more important than inheritance. And in contrast, the disbelievers are allies of one another and also heirs of one another. These are the important lines upon which the structure of the Islamic society rises. And upon these lines the relations among the members of society are formed and deteriorate, as has been recorded in these Qur'anic verses.

From the beginning of Islam up to the Day of Badr, the nature of walayah among the Muslims was this: among them there were relations of inheritance and mutual support (takaful), and under this they paid diyah (blood-money); and among them the walayah of mutual help and brotherhood was established, and this walayah stood in place of the walayah of kinship, lineage and blood. But when, after the Day of Badr, Allah gave stability to the Muslims and the Islamic state became firm, walayah and nusrah remained, while inheritance and takaful in diyah were returned to the ties of kinship within the Islamic society. The hijrah referred to in this verse, which has been made a condition for this walayah, whether general or specific, means hijrah from the abode of shirk to the abode of Islam, for those who have the capacity to do so. Those who are able to migrate and do not, and do not because they cherish their interests and kinship ties in the abode of shirk, there is no walayah between them and the Muslims. The same issue applied to those village people who had accepted Islam but, owing to such circumstances, did not migrate. Some of these people were also in Makkah. Regarding such people the ruling is that Allah has made their support obligatory, provided they seek support; but where there is a treaty between the Muslims and the people with whom they are at enmity, no aid is to be given, because the covenant of the Islamic society and its movement's plan is more important than individual needs.

We understand that from these verses and the rulings and principles mentioned in them, the features of the Islamic society become clearly evident. From them it becomes known what the priorities of the Islamic society are, what its organic composition is, and what its fundamental values are. But this matter cannot be fully clear until a note is given on the Islamic society and its historical evolution, and it is made clear what the basic principles of an Islamic society are, and what the method of its movement, struggle and priorities is.

The Islamic call which Muhammad ﷺ took up is, in reality, the last link in the long chain of this universal Islamic call which all the prophets, from Adam (peace be upon him) to Muhammad, presented. Throughout this long history of humanity, the aim and objective of the Islamic call has remained one and the same, namely to introduce people to the one Lord, the Lord of Majesty, to make them His servants and slaves alone, and to free them from all other gods and servitudes besides Him. Human history bears witness that, except for a few individuals and apart from brief intervals, the whole of humanity has never denied the true source of divinity, Allah's Being. This belief has existed in some form among all nations and peoples. However, it has certainly happened that people sometimes stumbled in attaining the correct knowledge of Allah, and at other times associated someone with Him in His divinity and lordship. This shirk has occurred either in worship and belief, or it has occurred in the sphere of sovereignty and obedience, and in their nature and consequences both kinds of shirk are alike. By committing it, people kept going out of the religion of Allah.

In every age, religion reached people through the messengers. Then gradually it happened that people, departing from the religion of truth, returned to that jahiliyyah (ignorance) from which the religion of truth had rescued them. Although these people did not entirely deny God, they associated partners with Him in His Being, or in beliefs and ideas, or in obedience and sovereignty, or in all of these.

This single purpose has been the aim of the Islamic call, and throughout the whole history of humanity the purpose of the call of all the prophets has also been one and the same, namely Islam. In other words, submitting one's head before the one Allah and Lord, removing people from servitude and slavery to all deities and bringing them into the service and obedience of Allah alone, that is, bringing people into the obedience of Allah alone in sovereignty, law, government and all the habits and conduct of life—this is the purpose which Muhammad ﷺ brought, and the aim of all the prophets before him was also this. Its name is Islam, which seeks to bring people back into the sphere of the sovereignty of Allah alone. Consider that throughout this whole universe the sovereignty of Allah operates in a creative (takwini) manner. Not even a leaf moves from its place without the command of Allah. The sun and the moon revolve by His command. In the same way, let all legislative matters also proceed in accordance with the command of that Exalted Being, and let people not adopt for themselves any system of life, any government, or any arrangements which differ from or contradict the system of life, form of government and management prescribed by Allah. For Allah alone has control over this entire universe; rather, He Himself also has control over the natural part of human life, which lies beyond the domain of human choice and will. For example: birth, growth, health and sickness, life and death, and other matters which are directly subject to the natural laws prescribed by Allah, and in which man, in his natural and social life, is bound by these natural principles, willingly or unwillingly. And in no way can these natural and physical laws be changed, nor has any power till today been able to change these laws. Islam wishes that, in the same way, in the voluntary part of life too, man should be bound by the divine laws, and should make Allah alone his sovereign and the one to be obeyed throughout his whole life; and that this voluntary part of his life should also come into harmony with the creative part of life and the universe, so that harmony is found among all three.

For further explanation, see Maulana Abul Ala Maududi's book "Mabadi-e-Islam"; probably the risala Deeniyat is meant.

Jahiliyyah, whose foundation is laid upon human sovereignty, which gives to democracies or dictators the right to make laws for people. It is evident that this form of jahiliyyah, on the one hand, goes outside the nature of the universe, and on the other hand, it creates conflict between the domains of choice and non-choice in human life.

Every prophet has confronted this jahiliyyah and, in every age of human history, has called people to obey Allah alone, without partner. Muhammad ﷺ also confronted this jahiliyyah. This form of jahiliyyah has not existed merely in the form of an idea; at times it has not even had any organized constitution or structure.

This jahiliyyah has remained present in the form of a "collective movement." It has been manifested in an organized society. This collective movement has remained subservient to the leadership provided by that society. This movement fully adopts the ideas, values, life-goals, customs and habits of the jahili society. Then this jahili society has remained a cohesive society. Among its members there has been practical cooperation, joint completion of programmes, discipline, a sense of mutual closeness, and a cooperation of the kind found among the members of a party.

This cohesion of individuals has kept that jahili society in motion, consciously or unconsciously, so that society may protect itself, arrange the defence of its own being, and eliminate all those foundations of danger to its existence which challenge it in any way.

Once it becomes known that jahiliyyah does not appear merely in the form of a creed and ideology, but comes in the form of a society and a collective movement, then it becomes self-evident that bringing people back into the Islamic system of life and the worship of Allah cannot be accomplished merely in the form of an idea, and in that form it cannot be useful to any degree; because in that form the Islamic ideology would not even be able to match the established system of life of jahiliyyah, behind which stands an active society. Much less can the Islamic ideology of life overcome jahiliyyah and prove itself superior to it. For in order to overthrow an established and powerful existence and to raise a new existence in its place, it is absolutely necessary that the other existence be dominant, and that this new system of life differ fundamentally from the established jahiliyyah in its temperament, its method of working, its very being and its details; moreover, the system to be established must exist in the form of a living, dynamic and powerful society, its basic ideas and detailed order must rest on very firm principles, and along with this, this system must also be stronger than that jahili system of life in its relations, connections, coordination and organisation.

At this point the question arises: what is that intellectual and ideological foundation upon which the structure of the Islamic system of life has been built in all ages? It is: La ilaha illa Allah, that is, the testimony that Allah, in His divinity, sovereignty, self-subsistence, kingship and rule, is one without partner. Man should, in his belief and conscience, regard Him as one, worship Him alone, and in practical life obey His law alone. This testimony, unless it is in this meaning, is legally considered non-existent. Its legal existence depends upon its also having an external existence in the practical field, by which it can be decided whether the one bearing witness is a Muslim or a non-Muslim.

And the coming into existence of this ideology means that people return to Allah throughout their whole lives: in every matter and every sphere of life they acknowledge only the decision of God, do not decide by themselves, but in every matter turn to the command of God, obey Him, and it is necessary that, in order to learn the command of Allah, they turn to Muhammad ﷺ. It was he who conveyed the command of Allah to us, and he is the last Messenger of Allah. This is the second part of the two components of the first pillar of Islam, and by this affirmation it comes into existence. This is the basic system of belief of Islam from which the Islamic system of life is formed. When this fundamental belief is applied to the whole of life, a detailed system of life is born from it, by adopting which a Muslim resolves the individual and collective problems of life. The internal problems of the state are also resolved by it, and the external problems too become known to him: what kind of relationship he should maintain with that Muslim society, and what the nature of its relations with non-Muslim societies should be.

Just as we stated above, the Islamic system of life was never meant to present itself merely as a theory, such that anyone who wished could accept it, perform a few acts of worship, and then, merging into the surrounding jahili and dominant society, live under the shadow of jahiliyyah. For in such circumstances, even if Muslims were present in a great number, they could not establish the Islamic system of life in actual and practical form. This is because individuals who have already believed in the Islamic system of life, and yet continue to become a part of a jahili society, will find themselves, consciously or unconsciously, willingly or unwillingly, compelled to advance the aims of that jahili society, and every struggle of their life will in fact be fulfilling the fundamental requirements of that jahili society which are necessary for its existence. Moreover, such people will be even more dangerous to the existence of that jahili society, because a social system always keeps all its components engaged in its own defence, whether they wish it or not. In other words, such individuals, despite believing in the Islamic worldview and being enemies of the jahili system of life, will be engaged in the building and service of that jahili society and will constantly keep strengthening it. Like walking living corpses, they will spend their resources for the survival and permanence of the jahili society. Their abilities, their experiences and their vigour will be spent in making that jahili society alive and strong, whereas all their striving should be directed towards breaking the jahili society and establishing an Islamic society.

Therefore it is absolutely necessary that the fundamental belief of Islam should, at the very first stage, emerge in the form of a collective movement which is separate from and independent of that jahili movement, which Islam has come to eradicate. Likewise, it is necessary that the centre of this collective movement be a leadership which is coloured in the hue of the Prophet ﷺ and the righteous predecessors (salaf al-salih), whose aim is to call people to the Oneness of Allah, without partner, in His divinity, lordship, sovereignty over all, His judgement, and His dominance and authority, and to the Shari'ah.

And whoever joins this movement by pronouncing the Shahadah with full awareness must sever his ties with that jahili society and separate himself from it. This is the same jahili society from which he has come out to this place. Likewise, he will also have to separate himself from the leadership of the jahili society. This jahili leadership takes religious forms as well: they are soothsayers, priests and custodians of shrines, and magicians and fortune-tellers. And this jahili leadership also takes political, tribal and economic forms. In the early days of Islam, both kinds of this leadership existed in the jahili society of Quraysh, and he will have to separate himself from that jahili leadership and confine himself to his loyal Islamic movement and its leaders.

The fundamental belief must emerge in the form of a collective movement at the very first stage, when a Muslim man, with awareness, renews his faith and pronounces the "testimonies" afresh, because the external existence of Muslim society cannot be realised without this. Merely by the fundamental belief becoming firmly rooted in hearts, Muslim society does not come into existence, however large the number of its individuals may be, unless these individuals organise themselves in the form of a collective movement and work together with mutual cooperation. This collective movement must not remain established permanently with its own independent existence; its members must not perform their collective duty as members of the movement, just as the organs of a living body continue to perform their natural functions. These members of Muslim society must work to preserve its existence, to deepen its roots, and to extend it further. They must also defend themselves against those forces which are bent on annihilating this society, and this entire task they must carry out under the guidance of their own independent leadership, which will keep them organised and active, will direct them towards preserving their existence, deepening the roots of the movement and expanding it, and will thus stand against the jahili movements.

Islam came into existence in this manner: first, a concise yet comprehensive principle and worldview was placed before people, and then a movement arose and the foundation of a new society was laid, and this new society was not only different from that jahili society but became a challenge to its existence and stood up in opposition to it. At no time did Islam appear merely in the form of an abstract theory. It always appeared in the form of an active movement, and if it is to be revived in the future too, it can only be revived in the form where there is an active movement behind it; and it is absolutely impossible that an Islamic society could be revived anew under the shadow of a dominant jahili society. The revival of Islam on a purely ideological basis is impossible at any time and in any place, unless a practical movement exists behind it.

When we have understood that the natural development of this religion happens in this way and that this is its philosophy, then we will be able to understand the reality of this religion and its movement-oriented character. When we have grasped well this point, the full details of which we have given in the introduction to Surah al-Anfal, then, only as a result of this background, we will be able to understand the reality of these verses and the meaning of the rulings given at the end of this surah. In it, it has been explained what the organisation of society in Islam will be: what the relations between the Muhajirun and the Ansar will be, what their class position will be, what the relations of the local helpers and Ansar will be with the Muhajirun, how their relations with those who did not migrate at this stage will be, and what the international relations of this Islamic society with other disbelievers will be. And all this reflection and understanding will be necessary in the light of the concepts of the organic identity of this religion and its movement-oriented development.

Now it is possible for us to discuss these verses (72 to 75) in detail in the light of these principles.

{Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave refuge and helped, these are allies of one another. As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of protection toward them until they emigrate. But if they seek your help in matters of religion, then you must help them, except against a people with whom you have a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do. And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do likewise, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption. And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah, and those who gave refuge and helped - those are the believers, truly. For them is forgiveness and noble provision. And those who believed after [that] and emigrated and strove with you - they are of you. But those of relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.}

In Makkah, whoever pronounced the Shahadah would sever his bonds of wilayah with his clan, his tribe, his relatives and the leadership of the Days of Ignorance, and would place the reins of his wilayah and leadership in the hands of Hadrat Muhammad ﷺ. And he would become a member of the society and family that was rising under the leadership of Hadrat Muhammad ﷺ, while the society of Quraysh was defending its own long-established jahili existence, because this new society was in reality in rebellion against the former established society, and this conflict between the two societies had been going on well before the open battlefield of Badr. Quraysh's society wished to uproot this new society from its very foundations.

In these circumstances, the Messenger ﷺ established brotherhood (mu'akhat) among the individuals of this new society, in such a way that those individuals who broke away from the jahili society of Quraysh would become members of this new mutually supportive (Secure) society, and this new society was founded not on the ties of blood and lineage but on the ties of ideas and beliefs. The loyalties of people were increasingly attached to this new leadership, and they were increasingly cut off from the old jahili leadership. Moreover, their love was cut off from that old jahili society and became attached to this new Islamic society.

After this, when Allah opened the doors of the Abode of Migration (Madinah) to the Muslims, a distinct community of believers came into being in Madinah, which pledged unconditional allegiance to the Islamic leadership and vowed to hear and obey in both pleasure and displeasure, and undertook the responsibility of protecting and defending the Messenger of Allah in every circumstance, just as they protect their wealth, children and their women. Then, when the Islamic state was established in Madinah under the leadership of the Messenger of Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ re-established brotherhood between the Ansar and the Muhajirun, and this brotherhood too was established on an Islamic footing, in preference to ties of blood and lineage. In this brotherhood, too, all the requirements of the earlier brotherhood were observed, namely that its members shared with one another in inheritance, blood-money (diyah) and other compensations, just as brotherhood had been established under the earlier system on the basis of ties of blood and lineage. In this regard the command was: "Those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave refuge and helped, these are allies of one another."

These people are allies of one another in support, allies of one another in inheritance, and allies of one another in blood-money, compensations and all collective payments which, in earlier periods, were imposed upon the ties of blood and lineage.

One category of people were those who had entered the religion of Islam but did not in practice enter the Islamic society by migrating. That is, they did not migrate to the Islamic state of Madinah where the Islamic Shari'ah was in force, where the Islamic leadership had its administration and management, and they did not come to that society where the Shari'ah laws governed and in which a complete Islamic identity and existence was established. Whereas in Makkah the existence of that society was present to a comparatively lesser degree; that is, there too people were loyal to the new leadership and had come together in the form of a collective movement and had a separate existence of their own, having cut themselves off from the existing jahili existence of that time, and were confronting the whole jahili society with this new existence of theirs.

In short, such people existed around Makkah as well as around Madinah, who had accepted the creed but had not entered the Islamic society by cutting themselves off from the jahili society. And they were not fully under the Islamic government and leadership established in Madinah, nor were they subject to it.

These people were not considered members of the Islamic society, therefore Allah did not grant them the rights of wilayah in the Islamic society, because in practice they were not members of the Islamic society. And it was concerning such people that this command was revealed: "As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of protection toward them until they emigrate. But if they seek your help in matters of religion, then you must help them, except against a people with whom you have a treaty."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verses 72–73 (part 3 of 3):

This ruling, as we have said, has a logical connection with the temperament of this religion and with its practical, movement-oriented activities, because these people are in reality not parts of the practical society of Islam. For this reason, a bond of walayah (guardianship and alliance) cannot be established between them and the Islamic society. Yes, although there is a connection of beliefs and ideas with such people, the responsibility of the Islamic society is not imposed on them merely as a result of an ideological connection. Except where their religion and ideology are subjected to some aggression, for example, where they are persecuted because of their beliefs. In such circumstances, if they seek help from the Muslims, it is obligatory upon the Muslims to help them, provided that this help does not affect the treaty which the Islamic society has made with some other nation, even if it is the government with which the treaty has been made that is perpetrating this persecution. This is because the real importance lies in the Islamic society and its treaties, not in individuals, since treaties affect the movement-oriented plans of the Islamic society; therefore, treaties have been given greater importance than individuals. Even if the matter is persecution on the basis of ideological grounds, yet since the Muslims who are persecuted did not come to the Islamic abode of migration (Dar al-Hijrah) of their own accord, the oppressor has perhaps been given preference over them. This shows how much greater importance collective movement-oriented interests have in the Islamic system compared with individuals, because the collective existence of Islam is of greater importance, as compared with an individual and his interests.

On this whole scheme, the comment comes: ﴿Wallahu bima ta'malsuna basir﴾ "Allah is seeing what you do." Therefore your entire conduct is before His sight. He is well aware of the outward form and the inward aims of these actions. He knows their antecedents and their consequences. He also understands well their causes and their effects.

Just as the Islamic society is balanced, mutually supportive, helpful and responsible, in the same way the Jahili society also provides social security to its members. ﴿Walladhina kafaru ba'duhum awliya'u ba'd﴾ "And those who disbelieve, they are guardians of one another." As we explained above, the position of the two fronts is exactly like this. The Jahili society also does not function individually; it too possesses an organic identity. Its organs function in the same way as individuals do, and it too defends its own identity in the same way as the Islamic society does. Therefore, the disbelievers are friends and guardians of one another, and the Islamic society also regards itself as one front against the people of disbelief, and Islam also presents itself, in the face of their society, in the form of a society. But the Islamic society stands on a deeper, firmer and stronger foundation against disbelief. If the Islamic society does not raise, against the disbelievers, a collective society of the same kind, then it will constantly face the danger of strife and corruption from the Jahili society, because individually Muslims will not be able to confront a strong and interconnected collective society of Jahiliyyah, and a great strife and corruption will break out in the world, because the society of Jahiliyyah will overpower Islam. In that case, Jahiliyyah will commit aggression and transgression against Islam, and the lordship of servants will prevail over the lordship of Allah, the Exalted, and people will again fall into slavery to other humans. Clearly, what greater corruption could there be than this?

﴿Illa taf'aluhu takun fitnatun fil-ardi wa fasadun kabir﴾ "If you do not do this, there will be strife in the land and great corruption." After this warning, what other warning could there be, and after this threat, what other threat could there be? Those Muslims who do not base their collective existence on this kind of organic and movement-oriented unity, in which there is deep brotherhood among the individuals and which has a single leadership, will be responsible before Allah for the great corruption that befalls their collective existence. And on the Day of Resurrection, all responsibilities will in any case fall upon them, because if the Muslims do not do this, their society will fall victim to corruption.

The Islamic call which Muhammad ﷺ took up is, in reality, the last link in the long chain of this universal Islamic call which all the prophets, from Adam (peace be upon him) to Muhammad, presented. Throughout this long history of humanity, the aim and objective of the Islamic call has remained one and the same, namely to introduce people to the one Lord, the Lord of Majesty, to make them His servants and slaves alone, and to free them from all other gods and servitudes besides Him. Human history bears witness that, except for a few individuals and apart from brief intervals, the whole of humanity has never denied the true source of divinity, Allah's Being. This belief has existed in some form among all nations and peoples. However, it has certainly happened that people sometimes stumbled in attaining the correct knowledge of Allah, and at other times associated someone with Him in His divinity and lordship. This shirk has occurred either in worship and belief, or it has occurred in the sphere of sovereignty and obedience, and in their nature and consequences both kinds of shirk are alike. By committing it, people kept going out of the religion of Allah.

In every age, religion reached people through the messengers. Then gradually it happened that people, departing from the religion of truth, returned to that jahiliyyah (ignorance) from which the religion of truth had rescued them. Although these people did not entirely deny God, they associated partners with Him in His Being, or in beliefs and ideas, or in obedience and sovereignty, or in all of these.

This single purpose has been the aim of the Islamic call, and throughout the whole history of humanity the purpose of the call of all the prophets has also been one and the same, namely Islam. In other words, submitting one's head before the one Allah and Lord, removing people from servitude and slavery to all deities and bringing them into the service and obedience of Allah alone, that is, bringing people into the obedience of Allah alone in sovereignty, law, government and all the habits and conduct of life—this is the purpose which Muhammad ﷺ brought, and the aim of all the prophets before him was also this. Its name is Islam, which seeks to bring people back into the sphere of the sovereignty of Allah alone. Consider that throughout this whole universe the sovereignty of Allah operates in a creative (takwini) manner. Not even a leaf moves from its place without the command of Allah. The sun and the moon revolve by His command. In the same way, let all legislative matters also proceed in accordance with the command of that Exalted Being, and let people not adopt for themselves any system of life, any government, or any arrangements which differ from or contradict the system of life, form of government and management prescribed by Allah. For Allah alone has control over this entire universe; rather, He Himself also has control over the natural part of human life, which lies beyond the domain of human choice and will. For example: birth, growth, health and sickness, life and death, and other matters which are directly subject to the natural laws prescribed by Allah, and in which man, in his natural and social life, is bound by these natural principles, willingly or unwillingly. And in no way can these natural and physical laws be changed, nor has any power till today been able to change these laws. Islam wishes that, in the same way, in the voluntary part of life too, man should be bound by the divine laws, and should make Allah alone his sovereign and the one to be obeyed throughout his whole life; and that this voluntary part of his life should also come into harmony with the creative part of life and the universe, so that harmony is found among all three.

For further explanation, see Maulana Abul Ala Maududi's book "Mabadi-e-Islam"; probably the risala Deeniyat is meant.

Jahiliyyah, whose foundation is laid upon human sovereignty, which gives to democracies or dictators the right to make laws for people. It is evident that this form of jahiliyyah, on the one hand, goes outside the nature of the universe, and on the other hand, it creates conflict between the domains of choice and non-choice in human life.

Every prophet has confronted this jahiliyyah and, in every age of human history, has called people to obey Allah alone, without partner. Muhammad ﷺ also confronted this jahiliyyah. This form of jahiliyyah has not existed merely in the form of an idea; at times it has not even had any organized constitution or structure.

This jahiliyyah has remained present in the form of a "collective movement." It has been manifested in an organized society. This collective movement has remained subservient to the leadership provided by that society. This movement fully adopts the ideas, values, life-goals, customs and habits of the jahili society. Then this jahili society has remained a cohesive society. Among its members there has been practical cooperation, joint completion of programmes, discipline, a sense of mutual closeness, and a cooperation of the kind found among the members of a party.

This cohesion of individuals has kept that jahili society in motion, consciously or unconsciously, so that society may protect itself, arrange the defence of its own being, and eliminate all those foundations of danger to its existence which challenge it in any way.

Once it becomes known that jahiliyyah does not appear merely in the form of a creed and ideology, but comes in the form of a society and a collective movement, then it becomes self-evident that bringing people back into the Islamic system of life and the worship of Allah cannot be accomplished merely in the form of an idea, and in that form it cannot be useful to any degree; because in that form the Islamic ideology would not even be able to match the established system of life of jahiliyyah, behind which stands an active society. Much less can the Islamic ideology of life overcome jahiliyyah and prove itself superior to it. For in order to overthrow an established and powerful existence and to raise a new existence in its place, it is absolutely necessary that the other existence be dominant, and that this new system of life differ fundamentally from the established jahiliyyah in its temperament, its method of working, its very being and its details; moreover, the system to be established must exist in the form of a living, dynamic and powerful society, its basic ideas and detailed order must rest on very firm principles, and along with this, this system must also be stronger than that jahili system of life in its relations, connections, coordination and organisation.

At this point the question arises: what is that intellectual and ideological foundation upon which the structure of the Islamic system of life has been built in all ages? It is: La ilaha illa Allah, that is, the testimony that Allah, in His divinity, sovereignty, self-subsistence, kingship and rule, is one without partner. Man should, in his belief and conscience, regard Him as one, worship Him alone, and in practical life obey His law alone. This testimony, unless it is in this meaning, is legally considered non-existent. Its legal existence depends upon its also having an external existence in the practical field, by which it can be decided whether the one bearing witness is a Muslim or a non-Muslim.

And the coming into existence of this ideology means that people return to Allah throughout their whole lives: in every matter and every sphere of life they acknowledge only the decision of God, do not decide by themselves, but in every matter turn to the command of God, obey Him, and it is necessary that, in order to learn the command of Allah, they turn to Muhammad ﷺ. It was he who conveyed the command of Allah to us, and he is the last Messenger of Allah. This is the second part of the two components of the first pillar of Islam, and by this affirmation it comes into existence. This is the basic system of belief of Islam from which the Islamic system of life is formed. When this fundamental belief is applied to the whole of life, a detailed system of life is born from it, by adopting which a Muslim resolves the individual and collective problems of life. The internal problems of the state are also resolved by it, and the external problems too become known to him: what kind of relationship he should maintain with that Muslim society, and what the nature of its relations with non-Muslim societies should be.

Just as we stated above, the Islamic system of life was never meant to present itself merely as a theory, such that anyone who wished could accept it, perform a few acts of worship, and then, merging into the surrounding jahili and dominant society, live under the shadow of jahiliyyah. For in such circumstances, even if Muslims were present in a great number, they could not establish the Islamic system of life in actual and practical form. This is because individuals who have already believed in the Islamic system of life, and yet continue to become a part of a jahili society, will find themselves, consciously or unconsciously, willingly or unwillingly, compelled to advance the aims of that jahili society, and every struggle of their life will in fact be fulfilling the fundamental requirements of that jahili society which are necessary for its existence. Moreover, such people will be even more dangerous to the existence of that jahili society, because a social system always keeps all its components engaged in its own defence, whether they wish it or not. In other words, such individuals, despite believing in the Islamic worldview and being enemies of the jahili system of life, will be engaged in the building and service of that jahili society and will constantly keep strengthening it. Like walking living corpses, they will spend their resources for the survival and permanence of the jahili society. Their abilities, their experiences and their vigour will be spent in making that jahili society alive and strong, whereas all their striving should be directed towards breaking the jahili society and establishing an Islamic society.

Therefore it is absolutely necessary that the fundamental belief of Islam should, at the very first stage, emerge in the form of a collective movement which is separate from and independent of that jahili movement, which Islam has come to eradicate. Likewise, it is necessary that the centre of this collective movement be a leadership which is coloured in the hue of the Prophet ﷺ and the righteous predecessors (salaf al-salih), whose aim is to call people to the Oneness of Allah, without partner, in His divinity, lordship, sovereignty over all, His judgement, and His dominance and authority, and to the Shari'ah.

And whoever joins this movement by pronouncing the Shahadah with full awareness must sever his ties with that jahili society and separate himself from it. This is the same jahili society from which he has come out to this place. Likewise, he will also have to separate himself from the leadership of the jahili society. This jahili leadership takes religious forms as well: they are soothsayers, priests and custodians of shrines, and magicians and fortune-tellers. And this jahili leadership also takes political, tribal and economic forms. In the early days of Islam, both kinds of this leadership existed in the jahili society of Quraysh, and he will have to separate himself from that jahili leadership and confine himself to his loyal Islamic movement and its leaders.

The fundamental belief must emerge in the form of a collective movement at the very first stage, when a Muslim man, with awareness, renews his faith and pronounces the "testimonies" afresh, because the external existence of Muslim society cannot be realised without this. Merely by the fundamental belief becoming firmly rooted in hearts, Muslim society does not come into existence, however large the number of its individuals may be, unless these individuals organise themselves in the form of a collective movement and work together with mutual cooperation. This collective movement must not remain established permanently with its own independent existence; its members must not perform their collective duty as members of the movement, just as the organs of a living body continue to perform their natural functions. These members of Muslim society must work to preserve its existence, to deepen its roots, and to extend it further. They must also defend themselves against those forces which are bent on annihilating this society, and this entire task they must carry out under the guidance of their own independent leadership, which will keep them organised and active, will direct them towards preserving their existence, deepening the roots of the movement and expanding it, and will thus stand against the jahili movements.

Islam came into existence in this manner: first, a concise yet comprehensive principle and worldview was placed before people, and then a movement arose and the foundation of a new society was laid, and this new society was not only different from that jahili society but became a challenge to its existence and stood up in opposition to it. At no time did Islam appear merely in the form of an abstract theory. It always appeared in the form of an active movement, and if it is to be revived in the future too, it can only be revived in the form where there is an active movement behind it; and it is absolutely impossible that an Islamic society could be revived anew under the shadow of a dominant jahili society. The revival of Islam on a purely ideological basis is impossible at any time and in any place, unless a practical movement exists behind it.

When we have understood that the natural development of this religion happens in this way and that this is its philosophy, then we will be able to understand the reality of this religion and its movement-oriented character. When we have grasped well this point, the full details of which we have given in the introduction to Surah al-Anfal, then, only as a result of this background, we will be able to understand the reality of these verses and the meaning of the rulings given at the end of this surah. In it, it has been explained what the organisation of society in Islam will be: what the relations between the Muhajirun and the Ansar will be, what their class position will be, what the relations of the local helpers and Ansar will be with the Muhajirun, how their relations with those who did not migrate at this stage will be, and what the international relations of this Islamic society with other disbelievers will be. And all this reflection and understanding will be necessary in the light of the concepts of the organic identity of this religion and its movement-oriented development.

Now it is possible for us to discuss these verses (72 to 75) in detail in the light of these principles.

{Indeed, those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave refuge and helped, these are allies of one another. As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of protection toward them until they emigrate. But if they seek your help in matters of religion, then you must help them, except against a people with whom you have a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do. And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do likewise, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption. And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah, and those who gave refuge and helped - those are the believers, truly. For them is forgiveness and noble provision. And those who believed after [that] and emigrated and strove with you - they are of you. But those of relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.}

In Makkah, whoever pronounced the Shahadah would sever his bonds of wilayah with his clan, his tribe, his relatives and the leadership of the Days of Ignorance, and would place the reins of his wilayah and leadership in the hands of Hadrat Muhammad ﷺ. And he would become a member of the society and family that was rising under the leadership of Hadrat Muhammad ﷺ, while the society of Quraysh was defending its own long-established jahili existence, because this new society was in reality in rebellion against the former established society, and this conflict between the two societies had been going on well before the open battlefield of Badr. Quraysh's society wished to uproot this new society from its very foundations.

In these circumstances, the Messenger ﷺ established brotherhood (mu'akhat) among the individuals of this new society, in such a way that those individuals who broke away from the jahili society of Quraysh would become members of this new mutually supportive (Secure) society, and this new society was founded not on the ties of blood and lineage but on the ties of ideas and beliefs. The loyalties of people were increasingly attached to this new leadership, and they were increasingly cut off from the old jahili leadership. Moreover, their love was cut off from that old jahili society and became attached to this new Islamic society.

After this, when Allah opened the doors of the Abode of Migration (Madinah) to the Muslims, a distinct community of believers came into being in Madinah, which pledged unconditional allegiance to the Islamic leadership and vowed to hear and obey in both pleasure and displeasure, and undertook the responsibility of protecting and defending the Messenger of Allah in every circumstance, just as they protect their wealth, children and their women. Then, when the Islamic state was established in Madinah under the leadership of the Messenger of Allah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ re-established brotherhood between the Ansar and the Muhajirun, and this brotherhood too was established on an Islamic footing, in preference to ties of blood and lineage. In this brotherhood, too, all the requirements of the earlier brotherhood were observed, namely that its members shared with one another in inheritance, blood-money (diyah) and other compensations, just as brotherhood had been established under the earlier system on the basis of ties of blood and lineage. In this regard the command was: "Those who believed and emigrated and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave refuge and helped, these are allies of one another."

These people are allies of one another in support, allies of one another in inheritance, and allies of one another in blood-money, compensations and all collective payments which, in earlier periods, were imposed upon the ties of blood and lineage.

One category of people were those who had entered the religion of Islam but did not in practice enter the Islamic society by migrating. That is, they did not migrate to the Islamic state of Madinah where the Islamic Shari'ah was in force, where the Islamic leadership had its administration and management, and they did not come to that society where the Shari'ah laws governed and in which a complete Islamic identity and existence was established. Whereas in Makkah the existence of that society was present to a comparatively lesser degree; that is, there too people were loyal to the new leadership and had come together in the form of a collective movement and had a separate existence of their own, having cut themselves off from the existing jahili existence of that time, and were confronting the whole jahili society with this new existence of theirs.

In short, such people existed around Makkah as well as around Madinah, who had accepted the creed but had not entered the Islamic society by cutting themselves off from the jahili society. And they were not fully under the Islamic government and leadership established in Madinah, nor were they subject to it.

These people were not considered members of the Islamic society, therefore Allah did not grant them the rights of wilayah in the Islamic society, because in practice they were not members of the Islamic society. And it was concerning such people that this command was revealed: "As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you have no obligation of protection toward them until they emigrate. But if they seek your help in matters of religion, then you must help them, except against a people with whom you have a treaty."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verses 72–73 (part 3 of 3):

This ruling, as we have said, has a logical connection with the temperament of this religion and with its practical, movement-oriented activities, because these people are in reality not parts of the practical society of Islam. For this reason, a bond of walayah (guardianship and alliance) cannot be established between them and the Islamic society. Yes, although there is a connection of beliefs and ideas with such people, the responsibility of the Islamic society is not imposed on them merely as a result of an ideological connection. Except where their religion and ideology are subjected to some aggression, for example, where they are persecuted because of their beliefs. In such circumstances, if they seek help from the Muslims, it is obligatory upon the Muslims to help them, provided that this help does not affect the treaty which the Islamic society has made with some other nation, even if it is the government with which the treaty has been made that is perpetrating this persecution. This is because the real importance lies in the Islamic society and its treaties, not in individuals, since treaties affect the movement-oriented plans of the Islamic society; therefore, treaties have been given greater importance than individuals. Even if the matter is persecution on the basis of ideological grounds, yet since the Muslims who are persecuted did not come to the Islamic abode of migration (Dar al-Hijrah) of their own accord, the oppressor has perhaps been given preference over them. This shows how much greater importance collective movement-oriented interests have in the Islamic system compared with individuals, because the collective existence of Islam is of greater importance, as compared with an individual and his interests.

On this whole scheme, the comment comes: ﴿Wallahu bima ta'malsuna basir﴾ "Allah is seeing what you do." Therefore your entire conduct is before His sight. He is well aware of the outward form and the inward aims of these actions. He knows their antecedents and their consequences. He also understands well their causes and their effects.

Just as the Islamic society is balanced, mutually supportive, helpful and responsible, in the same way the Jahili society also provides social security to its members. ﴿Walladhina kafaru ba'duhum awliya'u ba'd﴾ "And those who disbelieve, they are guardians of one another." As we explained above, the position of the two fronts is exactly like this. The Jahili society also does not function individually; it too possesses an organic identity. Its organs function in the same way as individuals do, and it too defends its own identity in the same way as the Islamic society does. Therefore, the disbelievers are friends and guardians of one another, and the Islamic society also regards itself as one front against the people of disbelief, and Islam also presents itself, in the face of their society, in the form of a society. But the Islamic society stands on a deeper, firmer and stronger foundation against disbelief. If the Islamic society does not raise, against the disbelievers, a collective society of the same kind, then it will constantly face the danger of strife and corruption from the Jahili society, because individually Muslims will not be able to confront a strong and interconnected collective society of Jahiliyyah, and a great strife and corruption will break out in the world, because the society of Jahiliyyah will overpower Islam. In that case, Jahiliyyah will commit aggression and transgression against Islam, and the lordship of servants will prevail over the lordship of Allah, the Exalted, and people will again fall into slavery to other humans. Clearly, what greater corruption could there be than this?

﴿Illa taf'aluhu takun fitnatun fil-ardi wa fasadun kabir﴾ "If you do not do this, there will be strife in the land and great corruption." After this warning, what other warning could there be, and after this threat, what other threat could there be? Those Muslims who do not base their collective existence on this kind of organic and movement-oriented unity, in which there is deep brotherhood among the individuals and which has a single leadership, will be responsible before Allah for the great corruption that befalls their collective existence. And on the Day of Resurrection, all responsibilities will in any case fall upon them, because if the Muslims do not do this, their society will fall victim to corruption.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 8, verse 74:

After this, the Qur'an tells them in clear words how true faith is realized:

﴿Those who believed, and migrated, and strove in the way of Allah, and those who gave shelter and help — these are the true believers. For them there is forgiveness and an honorable provision.﴾

Consider the words "they are the true believers" (ٱولٰۗىِٕكَ هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُوْنَ حَقًّا), or rather "they are the believers." This is the real form of faith. And it is in this form and this shape that the true religion grows. The reality of the religion of Islam does not come into existence merely through the proclamation of a doctrine. Nor does the reality of religion come into being merely by accepting a creed, nor does religion come into being merely by performing its rites and acts of worship. This religion is a system of life, and it comes into existence in practice only when it takes shape as an organized, active community. Through mere verbal affirmation of creed, religion comes into existence in a formal sense, but it does not come into existence in reality. It comes into existence in reality only when it takes the form of a practical, activist society and collective organization.

Such people are truly believers, and forgiveness and an honorable provision are binding upon them. The mention of "honorable provision" here is because the subject under discussion is jihad in the way of Allah, spending in the way of Allah, the provision of shelter, and the provision of help and other hardships, and for all these deeds the reward and recompense is the forgiveness of Allah, which is a great blessing and a generous hospitality.

After this, it is explained that although the first forerunners among the Muhajirun and Ansar hold an elevated rank, those who come later are also included with them and under their authority, and these later believers too are entitled to guardianship (wilayah) and membership of the Islamic movement's society.

﴿Those who believed afterwards, emigrated, and strove alongside you, they are indeed among you.﴾ Those who believed later, emigrated and came over, and began to struggle alongside you, they too are counted among you. This system of hijrah (migration) remained in place until Makkah was conquered. After the conquest of Makkah, the land of Arabia came under Islamic leadership, and the people all became part of the Islamic society. But after the conquest of Makkah, this command of hijrah was abolished, and jihad (struggle) was kept in force, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said. This position remained for 1200 years, and Islam ruled over this earth. The Islamic system of law was in force, and Islamic leadership remained the ruler and governor. But today, jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance of divine guidance) has once again become dominant and ruling over this entire world, and at present, in no region of the earth is the Shariah of Allah enforced over people's lives. Rather, authority and the legal system throughout the world are those of taghut (tyrannical powers that oppose God). People have entered into slavery to their fellow human beings, whereas Islam had freed them from human slavery. Therefore, the Islamic movement will now pass through the same stages that it passed through the first time. It began with organisation, and the movement advanced gradually, until Dar al-Hijrah (the abode of migration) is established, and then it will begin to spread out from the Dar al-Islam (abode of Islam) and Dar al-Hijrah, and then hijrah will end, but jihad will continue, just as it happened the first time.

The first time the Islamic movement was established, there were certain specific rulings for this movement's process. This movement had certain specific responsibilities owing to its particular circumstances. At that time, the relations of brotherhood and kinship had been removed from the basis of blood and lineage and placed on the foundation of Islamic principles. All forms of mu'akhah (brotherhood), all responsibilities, namely collective support (takaful), diyah (blood-money) and other financial obligations of indemnity, had been placed on Islamic brotherhood. But when the Islamic society was established, and the Muslims gained victory at the Battle of Badr, certain interim rulings were changed, because these interim rulings were for temporary and exceptional circumstances. Among the important changes were that collective support, the payment of diyah, and the relations of inheritance were restored and established on the basis of kinship and blood relations, but within the Islamic society and along Islamic lines.

﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾. Therefore, after the practical establishment of Islam, within the sphere of Islam, relatives can be given importance. This is one aspect of the natural human inclination. Islam does not impose a restriction that human natural desires must be suppressed, provided that these natural inclinations do not harm the Islamic and collective aspect of society, and do not harm other natural feelings and consciousness. Islam does not break natural inclinations, but regulates them, and it regulates them in such a way that they become beneficial for the lofty existence of the Islamic society. It regulates them for the sake of the collective existence of the Islamic society. If the needs of the collective existence of the Islamic society do not arise, then Islam leaves human natural inclinations free, within the general sphere of the Islamic system. This is why in Islam some rulings are temporary and interim, and these belong to the process of the Islamic movement. Such rulings are not regarded as Islam's final legal rulings, which are meant for establishing, sustaining and preserving the dominant existence of the Islamic society. Therefore, we must properly understand the difference between the rulings that came in the initial stage of Islam's establishment and its final rulings, which were given to preserve an established society permanently.

﴿Indeed Allah is All-Knowing of everything.﴾ Surely Allah knows everything. This remark and conclusion is most fitting at the end of these rulings, because these various rulings and administrative guidelines come from Allah, and Allah possesses the most comprehensive knowledge. He gives every command with knowledge. Here it is necessary to give a note on the establishment and organisation of this kind of Islamic society.

Islam, by giving the Muslim community a fundamental belief, and through its particular method of action, through a collective movement, giving it external existence, and making the fundamental belief the foundation of this collective movement, establishes it so that through it, it may bring forth the humanity of the human being. Islam, under its particular method of action, brings forth its fundamental principles. Islam, under its particular method of action, makes its fundamental principles, its teachings, its laws and its rulings, aim at this very development of humanity as its real objective.

Since human beings share their existence with all animals and even with inanimate matter, the proponents of scientific ignorance sometimes say that a human being is merely an animal, and sometimes say that his existence is merely a material existence. But it is quite evident that, despite sharing existence with animals and matter, human beings possess qualities that distinguish them from ordinary matter and animals and grant them a unique existence. Now, after some time, these proponents of scientific ignorance have been compelled to acknowledge this truth, and facts, realities, observations and experiments have broken the pride of their arrogance, and now they have been forced, helplessly, to acknowledge this truth only by hints and implications, without sincerity or explicit statement.

Those who have studied Islamic history impartially, and who also have a view of the whole of human history, know that the results of the Islamic system of life and of its method of establishment have been, to a considerable degree, magnificent. Islam built a modern society not on weak ties such as colour, homeland, nationality, national interests and regional relations, but solely on faith, principles, beliefs and concepts, and from this viewpoint it ignored the animal and material aspect of human existence and sought to bring out the humanity of the human being. Its first benefit was that the doors of entry into Islamic society were opened to people of every race and every class, and thus the noble and the lowly stood in one row, and no restriction or distinction of animal bondage or mutual discrimination remained between them. In this way, into the crucible of the Islamic society were poured the qualities and capacities of the various kinds of mankind, and in that crucible all these characteristics took the form of a beautiful combination, and from this raw material a new existence came into being. All this happened in a remarkably short period, and from it there emerged a strange, uniform and harmonious group of people, which gave birth to a radiant and magnificent civilisation. That civilisation was, in its own era, the essence of humanity's capacity and excellence, although in that age there were great distances between settlements and the system of communication was almost non-existent.

In this most exalted society, people of Arab, Persian, Syrian, Egyptian, Maghribi, Turkish, Chinese, Indian, Roman, Greek, Indonesian and African, and countless other nations and races, joined together and merged into it at the same time. In the development of Islamic civilisation and Islamic society, the abilities and intellects of all these people came together and worked in mutual cooperation and harmony. History bears witness that at no time was this magnificent civilisation merely an Arab civilisation, nor has it ever been a national civilisation in the usual sense; rather, it has always remained an intellectual civilisation.

All these people gathered in this civilisation on the principles of pure equality. Mutual kindness and compassion joined them together; because of the unity of the destination, they came together, and for this aim and purpose they expended all their capacities, in a society of their own, founded on equality.

They expended all their capacities, displayed all their national and historical characteristics, and devoted their personal and inherited excellences to the building and development of the new society, which was their own society founded on equality. Upon the basis of equality and unity, their belief was that the Lord, Sovereign, Owner and Creator of all of them is one and the same. Against the background of this belief, humanity emerged without any hindrance. The belief in the Oneness of God holds the belief in the "Oneness of Humanity."

This society is the most famous society, yet within it too many colours, countless languages and several nationalities can be seen, and each has a different temperament and way of thinking. Despite this, the foundation of that society was not laid upon humanity or on loftier principles; rather, it was a kind of class alliance, in which on one side was the class of the nobility, and on the other side was the group of slaves and the weak. On the other hand, we see that in the Roman Empire the conquering and the conquered peoples appear separate. The Roman conquerors are in every respect superior and exalted, and the conquered peoples are slaves and subjugated. These were the very causes why Roman society could not reach the heights that Islamic society reached, nor did it accomplish in human history those achievements which befit a healthy Islamic society. After that, several other societies also came into existence, for example the modern society established by English civilisation. This society too was in reality the successor and heir of Roman society, and in practical terms it also proved to be a class-based and exploitative society, and its fundamental principle was that the English nation should retain leadership and superiority. The clear proof of this is found in the economic and social surveys of those colonies which at one time were under English rule, and exactly the same conduct has been the practice of the other imperial and social powers of Europe. They too treated their colonies in the same way. The Spanish, Portuguese and French societies treated the original inhabitants of all their colonies in one and the same manner, and their conduct itself showed how despicable, destructive and degraded those societies were.

After this, before us appears the communist society. Although it removed colour, race, sex, language and homeland from its fundamental principles, its foundation too did not rise upon purely human foundations, but upon a new class struggle. This society too became a class society of the Roman type. The only difference was that Roman society emerged in support of the nobles (Lords), whereas communist society arose in support of the poor (Labours). Its technique was to sow the seeds of hatred against all other classes within the work of the labourers. Consequently, a long era of bloody conflict began, and in it humanity suffered such calamities as have no parallel in the whole of human history, because its foundation was not humanity but purely animal life. It claimed that sexual relations, food and shelter are the major problems of humanity, and that the welfare of humanity lies in solving them. Likewise, communism, by presenting the dialectical philosophy of history, made it into a history of class struggle.

But it is the great favour of Islamic society upon the world that in its system of life it brought out only those characteristics of human beings which are purely human. In this way it raised the human being far above the level of mere matter and mere animal, and in this respect the Islamic system of life is unparalleled in the whole history of humanity. Therefore it can rightly be said that those who abandon the Islamic system of life and adopt other systems are in reality enemies of humanity, and they wish to organise human life on the basis of nation, homeland, sex and classes in place of lofty human values, whereas nothing is weaker and more despicable and base than these. These people are enemies of humanity, and they do not want the construction of a human society on purely human foundations in accordance with natural principles, nor do they allow human society the opportunity to benefit from all human experiences and all human qualities and excellences. And concerning such people, the Lord, the Exalted, says:

﴿Say: Shall We inform you of those who are the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good. Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds are rendered void, and We shall assign them no weight on the Day of Resurrection. That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved and took My signs and My messengers in mockery.﴾ "O Muhammad, say to them: Shall we tell you who are the most failed and unsuccessful people in their deeds? Those whose whole striving in the life of this world went astray from the right path, while they thought they were setting everything right. These are the people who refused to accept the signs of their Lord and did not believe in appearing before Him. So all their deeds were wasted. On the Day of Resurrection We shall not give them any weight. Their reward is Hell, because of the disbelief they committed and because of the mockery they made of My signs and My messengers."

Because these people work against the human lines of progress, and want to change human society back into the form of a society of beasts, whose sole aim is the search for grass and grain, and they carry out this work in circumstances where Allah has, through His final Book, given people such guidance that all humanity can unite upon it.

But it is a surprising matter that those who wish to build human society upon lofty human values, these people call them, who wish to run society on purely animal ideologies, rigid reactionaries and by other names. The truth is that all these attractive words and all these accusations of theirs exist only because they wish to flee from lofty human values.

But Allah has full control over His affairs. Therefore, these lowly conditions that have come to dominate human societies, and that have reduced man to a mere animal, are not destined to endure. Soon that light will spread, and those societies will come into being which Allah loves. Humanity will soon regain the station of honor, just as humanity once gathered upon human values, and there is no parallel to it in history. It still shines on the horizon of history, and it is an example for people. Again that society will be organized, and one day it will become an ideal society. Insha'Allah!
